children.title: Canonical Conic Forms
children.top_down_role: Equivalent organizations distinguished by the placement of affine structure, cone membership, and explicit slack variables.

children.title: Conic-Variable Equality Form
children.top_down_role: The equality-oriented standard-form family with cone-constrained decision variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Variable Equality Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality form with a closed convex cone constraining the decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The conic-variable equality form is
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ c^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad x\in K.
\]
Thus all nonlinearity of the feasible set is isolated in membership of the decision variable in \(K\), while the remaining constraint is affine. A constant objective offset may be added without changing the minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a linear objective subject to affine equalities and membership of the decision variable in a closed convex cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) is a conic-variable equality-form program.

notation.meaning: Primal cone constraining the decision variable.
Equality map, right-hand side, and objective vector.

children.title: Affine Cone-Inclusion Form
children.top_down_role: The function-in-cone family used by mathematical modeling interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Cone-Inclusion Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional function-in-cone form with an affine residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The affine cone-inclusion form is
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ c^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad b-Ax\in K.
\]
More generally, several inclusions may be combined by taking a Cartesian-product cone. The convention \(Ax-b\in K\) describes the same modeling family after replacing \(K\) by \(-K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a linear objective while requiring an affine function of the decision variable to belong to a closed convex cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:b-Ax\in K\}\) is an affine cone-inclusion program.

notation.meaning: Affine residual constrained to the cone.
The reflected cone consisting of negatives of elements of the cone.

children.title: Slack-Explicit Conic Form
children.top_down_role: Canonical forms exposing cone-valued slack blocks separately from affine mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Explicit Conic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine cone inclusion rewritten with an explicit cone-valued slack variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), the inclusion \(b-Ax\in K\) is equivalent to introducing \(s\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and writing
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x,s}\ c^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+s=b,\qquad s\in K.
\]
The correspondence is exact: every feasible \(x\) determines the unique slack \(s=b-Ax\), and eliminating \(s\) recovers the original inclusion. The variable \(x\) is unrestricted unless additional cone blocks are specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expose the affine residual as a cone-valued slack satisfying an equality; eliminating that slack recovers the cone inclusion exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

children.title: Linear-Quadratic Objective Variant Family

children.title: Linear-Objective Conic Variants
children.top_down_role: Conic standard forms whose objective remains linear at the solver boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Objective Conic Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite-dimensional linear-objective forms obtained using cone-inclusion, explicit-slack, or product-cone coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty closed convex cones, let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}\). A linear-objective conic program may be written as
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ c^{\mathsf T}x+d
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in C,\qquad b-Ax\in K.
\]
Its slack-explicit form replaces the second inclusion by \(Ax+s=b\) and \(s\in K\). Equivalently, both cone restrictions can be collected as \((x,b-Ax)\in C\times K\). These forms have the same feasible \(x\), objective values, and minimizers. The constant \(d\) shifts every objective value by \(d\) without changing the feasible set or minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional linear-objective conic program has equivalent affine-inclusion, explicit-slack, and product-cone representations; a constant objective offset shifts values without changing feasibility or minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) are nonempty closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints \(x\in C,\ b-Ax\in K\), \(x\in C,\ Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\), and \((x,b-Ax)\in C\times K\) give equivalent representations in the variable \(x\).

notation.meaning: Cartesian-product cone collecting the decision-variable and residual cone restrictions.

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Set as an Exposed Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry induced by a linear objective over the conic feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:x\in C,\ b-Ax\in K\}\) be nonempty and convex, and suppose \(\alpha=\min_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\) is attained. Then \[ F_*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=F\cap\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x=\alpha\} \] is an exposed face of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a linear-objective conic program attains its optimum, its minimizers form the exposed face selected by the objective vector.
assumptions_latex: \(F=\{x:x\in C,\ b-Ax\in K\}\) is nonempty and convex.
The minimum of \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(F\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_*=F\cap\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x=\alpha\}\) is an exposed face of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Attained optimal value excluding any constant offset.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Set as an Exposed Face

children.title: Quadratic-Objective Conic Variants
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing forms that retain a convex quadratic objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Objective Conic Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex quadratic objective combined directly with an affine conic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a nonempty closed convex cone. A convex quadratic-objective conic variant has the form
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d
\quad\text{subject to}\quad b-Ax\in K.
\]
Positive semidefiniteness of \(Q\) makes the objective convex. The same feasible region has the slack-explicit representation \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), with \(s\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic objective may be minimized over a finite-dimensional affine conic feasible region written either as an inclusion or with an explicit cone-valued slack.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d:b-Ax\in K\}\) is a convex quadratic-objective conic program, and \(b-Ax\in K\iff\exists s\in K\text{ with }Ax+s=b\).

notation.meaning: Cone of symmetric positive semidefinite matrices of order n.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness supplied by the retained quadratic objective independently of the conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:b-Ax\in K\}\) be convex and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\). If \(Q\succ0\), then \(f\) is strictly convex and \(\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) has at most one minimizer. If \(Q\succeq0\) is singular, the quadratic term is not strictly convex along nonzero directions in \(\ker Q\); uniqueness may follow from the feasible geometry but is not guaranteed by the objective alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite retained quadratic guarantees at most one optimizer, whereas a singular PSD quadratic does not guarantee uniqueness by itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succ0\Longrightarrow |\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)|\leq1\); singular \(Q\succeq0\) does not alone imply uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Convexity and Uniqueness Boundary

children.title: Quadratic-Objective Conic Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted cone representations replacing retained quadratic objective structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Objective Conic Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph lift of a finite-dimensional convex quadratic objective into a rotated second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), choose \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\) satisfying \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\), and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a nonempty closed convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be given. Define
\[
\mathcal Q_r^{p+2}=\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^p:u\geq0,\ v\geq0,\ 2uv\geq\lVert w\rVert_2^2\}.
\]
Then the problem
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d
\quad\text{subject to}\quad b-Ax\in K
\]
has the epigraph lift
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ t\in\mathbb{R}}\ t+c^{\mathsf T}x+d
\quad\text{subject to}\quad b-Ax\in K,\qquad (t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r^{p+2}.
\]
The two problems have the same infimum and the same minimizing \(x\) whenever minimizers exist. At every optimum of the lifted problem, \(t=\tfrac12\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic objective can be represented by a linear objective and a rotated second-order-cone epigraph constraint, preserving the infimum and any minimizing decision vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r^{p+2}\iff t\geq\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), so the displayed rotated-cone program is an epigraph lift of the quadratic-objective program.

notation.meaning: Rotated second-order cone under the displayed normalization.
Epigraph variable for the quadratic term.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary-SOC normalization equivalent to the seed’s rotated-cone lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\succeq0\). Then \[ t\geq\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \left\|\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt2Rx\\ t-1\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\leq t+1. \] Replacing the quadratic objective term by \(t\) and imposing this constraint preserves the infimum and the minimizing \(x\)-vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PSD quadratic epigraph may be encoded by an ordinary SOC as well as by the rotated SOC in the seed.

notation.meaning: Factor of the positive-semidefinite quadratic matrix.

children.title: Primal–Dual Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Paired conic representations and the conventions that determine their solver-data orientations.

children.title: Primal Cone-Variable Orientation
children.top_down_role: Primal representations centered on a cone-constrained decision variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Cone-Variable Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal member of the standard equality-form conic primal–dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone. The primal cone-variable orientation is
\[
(P)\qquad \operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ c^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad x\in K.
\]
Its defining orientation places cone membership on the primal decision variable and equality feasibility on its linear image. With the dual-cone convention \(K^*=\{s:\langle s,x\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}\), this orientation pairs with stationarity \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal orientation constrains the decision variable to the primal cone and maps it through affine equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P)=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) is the primal cone-variable orientation.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative dual cone under the stated inner-product convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry of the Primal Feasible Slice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness, convexity, and recession geometry induced by equality slicing of the primal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\), the set \(F\) is convex and is closed when \(K\) is closed. If \(F\neq\varnothing\), then its recession cone is \[\operatorname{rec}F=K\cap\ker A.\] Thus the feasible directions that remain valid for every nonnegative step are exactly the cone vectors annihilated by the equality map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal feasible region is an affine slice of the cone, and its recession cone is the intersection of the cone with the nullspace of the equality map.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is closed and convex and \(\operatorname{rec}F=K\cap\ker A\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry of the Primal Feasible Slice

children.title: Dual Cone-Slack Orientation
children.top_down_role: Dual representations centered on a dual-cone slack and affine stationarity data.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Cone-Slack Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual member paired with the primal cone-variable equality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal program \((P)\) given by minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(x\in K\), define \(K^*=\{s:\langle s,x\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}\). Its dual cone-slack orientation is
\[
(D)\qquad \operatorname*{maximize}_{y,s}\ b^{\mathsf T}y
\quad\text{subject to}\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad s\in K^*.
\]
The variable \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) prices the primal equality, while \(s\) is the dual-cone slack. Every primal–dual feasible pair satisfies \(b^{\mathsf T}y\leq c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual orientation maximizes the equality multiplier’s value subject to affine stationarity and membership of the slack in the dual cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The primal data are \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D)=\sup\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), and primal–dual feasibility implies \(b^{\mathsf T}y\leq c^{\mathsf T}x\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the primal equality constraint.
Dual-cone slack in the stationarity equation.
Nonnegative dual cone of the primal cone.

children.title: Cone Convention Translation System
children.top_down_role: Convention families governing cone polarity, residual orientation, and optimization sense.

children.title: Residual Sign Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign choices used for affine residuals in primal–dual representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Sign Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation between opposite signs for affine conic residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x)=b-Ax\). The convention \(r(x)\in K\) is exactly equivalent to
\[
-r(x)=Ax-b\in -K.
\]
In slack-explicit coordinates, \(r(x)=s\) with \(s\in K\) becomes \(-r(x)=\tilde s\) with \(\tilde s=-s\in-K\). Therefore a residual sign reversal preserves the feasible set only when the cone and slack are simultaneously reflected. If \(K=-K\), as for a linear subspace, the cone need not be renamed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating an affine residual preserves feasibility only when its cone and explicit slack are also negated, except for sign-symmetric cones.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b-Ax\in K\iff Ax-b\in-K\), with \(\tilde s=-s\) in slack-explicit form.

notation.meaning: Affine residual under the first sign convention.

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

source_witnesses.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled transformation of a conic residual and its polar-cone Lagrange multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)\in K\) be represented by \(L(x,z)=f(x)+\langle z,r(x)\rangle\), with \(z\in K^\circ\). Under the equivalent convention \(-r(x)\in-K\), set \(\widetilde z=-z\). Since \((-K)^\circ=-K^\circ\), one has \(\widetilde z\in(-K)^\circ\) and \(f(x)+\langle\widetilde z,-r(x)\rangle=f(x)+\langle z,r(x)\rangle\). Thus residual reflection preserves the Lagrangian and stationarity when the multiplier is reflected simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing a conic residual also reverses its polar multiplier, leaving the Lagrangian and stationarity unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.

notation.meaning: Polar-cone multiplier under the original residual orientation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Translation Under Residual Reversal

children.title: Cone Polarity Conventions
children.top_down_role: Dual-cone versus polar-cone conventions under selected inner products.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Polarity Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation between nonnegative dual-cone and nonpositive polar-cone conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a cone \(K\) in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, define
\[
K^*=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }x\in K\},
\qquad
K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\leq0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}.
\]
Then \(K^\circ=-K^*\). Consequently, a dual slack condition \(s\in K^*\) translates to \(z=-s\in K^\circ\). In an affine stationarity equation \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), this substitution yields \(A^{\mathsf T}y-z=c\); changing cone terminology without this sign change does not preserve the represented dual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonpositive polar cone is the negative of the nonnegative dual cone, so translating conventions also negates the dual slack.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.

notation.meaning: Dual cone defined by nonnegative pairings.
Polar cone defined by nonpositive pairings.

children.title: Objective-Sense Conventions
children.top_down_role: Minimization-oriented versus maximization-oriented conic representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Sense Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact translation between minimization and maximization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any feasible set \(F\) and extended-real objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), changing objective sense is performed by negation:
\[
\inf_{x\in F} f(x)=-\sup_{x\in F}(-f(x)).
\]
Whenever either side is attained, \(x\) minimizes \(f\) over \(F\) if and only if it maximizes \(-f\) over \(F\). Thus conversion between minimization and maximization preserves feasible points and optimizers but negates the reported optimal value. In primal–dual displays, bound directions must be translated consistently with this value negation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating the objective converts minimization to maximization, preserves feasible points and optimizers, and negates the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=-\sup_{x\in F}(-f(x))\), with identical optimizer sets when attained.

notation.meaning: Feasible set, unchanged by the objective-sense translation.

children.title: Convention Translation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries encountered when converting between convention families.

knowledge_statements.title: Convention Translation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by changing a residual sign without translating its cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Convention changes are not independent symbol substitutions. For the scalar cone \(K=\mathbb{R}_+\), the constraint
\[
x-1\in\mathbb{R}_+
\]
has feasible set \([1,\infty)\). Negating only the residual while retaining the same cone gives \(1-x\in\mathbb{R}_+\), whose feasible set is \(( -\infty,1]\). The equivalent translation is instead \(1-x\in-\mathbb{R}_+\). Analogously, replacing \(K^*\) by \(K^\circ\) requires negating the dual slack, and reversing objective sense requires negating both the objective and reported value. Omitting any coupled transformation can change feasibility, stationarity, or bound direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convention translation fails when a residual, cone polarity, or objective sense is changed without its coupled sign transformations.
assumptions_latex: Convention translations are required to preserve the represented feasible set and objective ordering.

children.title: Cartesian Cone Products
children.top_down_role: Geometric organization of independent cone factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Cone Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Cartesian products of convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_i\subseteq E_i\) be convex cones in finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Their Cartesian product is the cone
\[
K:=\prod_{i=1}^{m}K_i=\{(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\in E_1\times\cdots\times E_m:z_i\in K_i\text{ for every }i\}.
\]
Membership in \(K\) is therefore equivalent to the componentwise conditions \(z_i\in K_i\). The product is closed whenever every factor is closed, and it is pointed whenever every factor is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite Cartesian product of cones consists exactly of tuples whose components belong to their respective factors; closedness and pointedness pass componentwise to the product.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_i\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space \(E_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\prod_{i=1}^{m}K_i\) is a convex cone with componentwise membership.

notation.meaning: Ambient space of the ith factor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Geometry of Finite Cone Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Span, lineality, relative interior, interior, pointedness, and full dimensionality of a finite Cartesian cone product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\prod_{i=1}^mK_i\) in \(E=\prod_{i=1}^mE_i\). Then \[\operatorname{span}K=\prod_i\operatorname{span}K_i,\qquad \operatorname{lin}K=\prod_i\operatorname{lin}K_i,\qquad \operatorname{ri}K=\prod_i\operatorname{ri}K_i,\] where \(\operatorname{lin}K=K\cap(-K)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{int}_E K=\prod_i\operatorname{int}_{E_i}K_i\). Hence \(K\) is pointed exactly when every factor is pointed, and it is full-dimensional exactly when every factor is full-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Span, lineality, relative interior, and interior of a finite cone product are componentwise, as are pointedness and full dimensionality.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_i\) is a nonempty convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space \(E_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ri}(\prod_iK_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{ri}K_i\) and \(\operatorname{lin}(\prod_iK_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{lin}K_i\), with the stated pointedness and full-dimensionality equivalences.

notation.meaning: Interior in the full product ambient space.

children.title: Cone-Block Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Partitioning of affine rows and slacks by cone family and block size.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise organization of a conic affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E,F_1,\ldots,F_m\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:E\to F_1\times\cdots\times F_m\) be linear, and let \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_m)\in F_1\times\cdots\times F_m\). Write \(A_i:=\pi_i\circ A\), where \(\pi_i\) is the ith coordinate projection. For cones \(K_i\subseteq F_i\), the constraint
\[
Ax+b\in\prod_{i=1}^{m}K_i
\]
is equivalent to the block system
\[
A_i x+b_i\in K_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Thus each affine row block and corresponding slack block has dimension \(\dim F_i\), and all encoded objects must use the same ordered block boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning affine rows, offsets, and slacks according to cone-factor dimensions makes one product-cone constraint exactly equivalent to separate blockwise cone constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\subseteq F_i\) are cones, \(A:E\to\prod_iF_i\) is linear, and \(b\in\prod_iF_i\).

notation.meaning: Affine-map row block for the ith cone factor.
Offset block in the ith factor space.
Projection onto the ith product-space coordinate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordered Block Alignment and Simultaneous Permutation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between harmless simultaneous block reordering and a mismatched cone-data ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a permutation \(\sigma\), define \(P_\sigma(z_1,\ldots,z_m)=(z_{\sigma^{-1}(1)},\ldots,z_{\sigma^{-1}(m)})\). Then \[Ax+b\in K_1\times\cdots\times K_m\iff P_\sigma(Ax+b)\in K_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}\times\cdots\times K_{\sigma^{-1}(m)}.\] Thus one common permutation of affine row blocks, offsets, slack blocks, and cone descriptors preserves the constraint, while permuting only some of them generally does not. For example, \((1,-1)\in\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_-\), but swapping only its affine blocks gives \((-1,1)\notin\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_-\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block order may be changed only by applying the same permutation to every affine, slack, and cone object; mismatched ordering can change feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(P_\sigma\) permutes complete factor blocks without altering coordinates within a block.
The affine blocks and their assigned cone factors have compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A simultaneous block permutation preserves feasibility, whereas an unmatched permutation need not preserve it.

notation.meaning: Linear permutation of complete product-space blocks.

children.title: Repeated Cone Factors
children.top_down_role: Collections formed from structurally identical cone factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Cone Factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Products containing multiple identical cone factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a cone \(K\subseteq E\) and an integer \(r\geq1\), the r-fold repeated cone factor is
\[
K^r:=\underbrace{K\times\cdots\times K}_{r\text{ factors}}\subseteq E^r.
\]
A tuple \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)\) belongs to \(K^r\) if and only if \(z_j\in K\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,r\). Repetition identifies a common cone family and dimension but does not impose equality among the component values \(z_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An r-fold repeated cone is the product of r identical cone factors; every component satisfies the same cone type, but components need not equal one another.

notation.meaning: The r-fold Cartesian power of the cone.
The jth component of a product-space element.

children.title: Batched Cone Descriptors
children.top_down_role: Compact solver-facing metadata for grouped cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Batched Cone Descriptors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact descriptors for consecutive repeated cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each batch descriptor be a triple \(d_q=(\tau_q,n_q,r_q)\), where \(\tau_q\) selects a cone family, \(n_q\) its size parameter, and \(r_q\geq1\) its multiplicity. If \(K_{\tau}(n)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\delta(\tau,n)}\), then the descriptor list \(D=(d_1,\ldots,d_s)\) represents
\[
K(D):=\prod_{q=1}^{s}K_{\tau_q}(n_q)^{r_q}.
\]
Its ambient dimension is \(\sum_{q=1}^{s}r_q\delta(\tau_q,n_q)\), and descriptor order fixes the order of the encoded cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch descriptor records cone family, size, and multiplicity; an ordered descriptor list expands into a product cone with a computable total dimension.
assumptions_latex: Each family-size pair \((\tau,n)\) determines a cone \(K_{\tau}(n)\) and dimension \(\delta(\tau,n)\).
The descriptor list is finite and every multiplicity \(r_q\) is positive.

notation.meaning: Ambient dimension of the indicated cone type.
Product cone expanded from the descriptor list.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies a canonical batched-descriptor convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed family-size-multiplicity encoding is coherent, but it is a chosen data convention rather than an intrinsic mathematical definition, and no inspectable source supports it.

children.title: Mixed-Size Batch Regimes
children.top_down_role: Batch organizations containing related cone factors with differing dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Size Batch Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for batches with heterogeneous cone dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For descriptors \(d_q=(\tau_q,n_q,r_q)\), a mixed-size batch regime occurs when the dimensions \(\delta_q:=\delta(\tau_q,n_q)\) are not all equal. It is well formed precisely when every factor is assigned its own dimension and the expanded block intervals
\[
I_{q,j}:=\{o_{q,j}+1,\ldots,o_{q,j}+\delta_q\}
\]
are pairwise disjoint, consecutive in descriptor order, and cover \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\), where \(N:=\sum_qr_q\delta_q\). A single fixed-stride interpretation is invalid unless all \(\delta_q\) coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-size batching is valid only with explicit per-factor dimensions and consecutive nonoverlapping offsets; a universal fixed stride works only when all factor dimensions match.
assumptions_latex: A finite ordered descriptor list determines positive dimensions \(\delta_q\) and multiplicities \(r_q\).
Expanded factors are stored contiguously in descriptor order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The batch is well formed exactly when the intervals \(I_{q,j}\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\) in order.

notation.meaning: Coordinate dimension of factors in batch q.
Coordinate interval occupied by factor j of batch q.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the data-layout convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the asserted storage convention, and the offsets \(o_{q,j}\) used to define the intervals are not introduced. The intended mathematical version therefore remains uncertain.

children.title: Batch Partition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits governing when cone blocks may share a batch descriptor.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Partition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate boundaries induced by ordered cone batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Expand the ordered batches into factor dimensions \(d_1,\ldots,d_M\), and define prefix boundaries by \(p_0:=0\) and
\[
p_j:=\sum_{k=1}^{j}d_k,
\qquad j=1,\ldots,M.
\]
The jth cone factor occupies coordinates \(p_{j-1}+1\) through \(p_j\). A batch partition is valid if and only if \(0=p_0<p_1<\cdots<p_M=N\), each width satisfies \(p_j-p_{j-1}=d_j\), and affine rows, offsets, and slack coordinates all use these same boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefix sums of expanded factor dimensions define the unique contiguous block boundaries, which must be shared by affine rows, offsets, and slack coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(d_j\in\mathbb{N}\) is the positive ambient dimension of expanded factor \(j\).
All encoded blocks use one common coordinate ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p_{j-1},p_j]\) is the jth block, and the intervals form a partition exactly under the stated boundary conditions.

notation.meaning: Dimension of expanded cone factor j.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the batch-boundary convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The prefix-sum construction is coherent for contiguous storage, but the record presents a specific shared-boundary encoding convention without any cited source.

children.title: Product-Cone Duality
children.top_down_role: Componentwise dual organization of Cartesian cone products.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Cone Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual cone of a finite Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_i\subseteq E_i\) be cones in finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, equip \(E_1\times\cdots\times E_m\) with the product inner product, and define \(K_i^*:=\{y_i:\langle y_i,x_i\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }x_i\in K_i\}\). Then
\[
\left(\prod_{i=1}^{m}K_i\right)^*=\prod_{i=1}^{m}K_i^*.
\]
Consequently, a vector \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_m)\) is dual-feasible for the product cone exactly when every component \(y_i\) belongs to the corresponding dual cone \(K_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the product inner product, the dual of a finite product of cones is the product of their dual cones, so dual feasibility is componentwise.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\subseteq E_i\) are cones in finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
The product space carries \(\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_i\langle x_i,y_i\rangle\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the ith factor.
The relevant factor or product inner product.

children.title: Affine Preimage Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Preimage Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representing a set as an affine inverse image of a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E,F\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq F\) be a convex cone, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear, and let \(b\in F\). Define the affine map \(f:E\to F\) by \(f(x):=Ax+b\). Its cone preimage representation is
\[
S:=f^{-1}(K)=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}.
\]
The represented set \(S\) is convex. If \(K\) is closed, then \(S\) is closed because \(f\) is continuous in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine preimage representation describes all points whose affine image lies in a cone; it gives a convex set and is closed whenever the cone is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(A:E\to F\) is linear, \(b\in F\), and \(K\subseteq F\) is a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}\) is convex, and it is closed if \(K\) is closed.

notation.meaning: Linear part of the affine map.
Set represented by the affine preimage.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession and Lineality of an Affine Cone Preimage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic asymptotic geometry of a nonempty affine preimage of a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq F\) be a closed convex cone and let \(S=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}\) be nonempty. Then \[ \operatorname{rec}S=\{v\in E:Av\in K\},\qquad \operatorname{lin}S=\{v\in E:Av\in K\cap(-K)\}. \] In particular, \(\ker A\subseteq\operatorname{lin}S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone of a nonempty affine cone preimage is the linear preimage of the cone, and its lineality is the preimage of the cone's lineality space.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq F\) is a closed convex cone.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the represented set.
Lineality space of the represented set.

children.title: Cone Section Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Section Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representing an affine set as a height-one section of a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a linear map \(A:E\to F\), a vector \(b\in F\), and a convex cone \(K\subseteq F\), define
\[
C:=\{(x,t)\in E\times\mathbb{R}:Ax+tb\in K,\ t\geq0\}.
\]
Then \(C\) is a convex cone, and its height-one affine section represents
\[
S:=\{x\in E:(x,1)\in C\}=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}.
\]
If \(K\) is closed, then \(C\) and the section \(S\) are closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing an affine cone constraint produces a cone in one extra scalar coordinate, whose height-one section is exactly the original represented set.
assumptions_latex: \(E,F\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces and \(A:E\to F\) is linear.
\(K\subseteq F\) is a convex cone and \(b\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a convex cone and \(S=\{x:(x,1)\in C\}=\{x:Ax+b\in K\}\).

children.title: Preimage–Section Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Preimage–Section Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between affine cone preimages and height-one cone sections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq F\) be a convex cone and \(f(x):=Ax+b\). Define the homogenized cone
\[
C_f:=\{(x,t)\in E\times\mathbb{R}:Ax+tb\in K,\ t\geq0\}.
\]
Then the affine preimage and height-one section coincide:
\[
f^{-1}(K)=\{x\in E:(x,1)\in C_f\}.
\]
Conversely, for any cone \(C\subseteq E\times\mathbb{R}\), its height-one section \(\{x:(x,1)\in C\}\) is the affine preimage of \(C\) under the embedding \(x\mapsto(x,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine preimages of cones are precisely height-one sections of suitable homogenized cones, and every height-one cone section is an affine preimage under the canonical embedding.
assumptions_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(K\) and \(C\) are convex cones in their stated ambient spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{-1}(K)=\{x:(x,1)\in C_f\}\), and every height-one cone section has this affine-preimage form.

notation.meaning: Affine map given by the linear part and translation.
Homogenized cone associated with the affine map.
Canonical affine embedding into the height-one hyperplane.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Height-One Sections Do Not Determine the Ambient Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of the correspondence as one between represented sets rather than a bijection of ambient cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The map \(C\mapsto\{x:(x,1)\in C\}\) is not injective on cones. In \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\), let \[ C_1:=\{(0,0)\},\qquad C_2:=\{(x,0):x\geq0\}. \] These are distinct closed convex cones, but \[ \{x:(x,1)\in C_1\}=\varnothing=\{x:(x,1)\in C_2\}. \] Thus an ambient cone cannot generally be reconstructed from its height-one section alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct cones can have the same height-one section, so the correspondence is exact for represented sets but not one-to-one between ambient cones.
assumptions_latex: Height-one sections are taken in \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Distinct closed convex cones with identical height-one sections.

children.title: Degenerate Affine Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Rank-deficient or lower-dimensional restrictions affecting the represented domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Affine Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empty, universal, and kernel-invariant affine cone restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(S:=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}\), degeneracy occurs at three elementary boundaries. If \(A=0\), then \(S=E\) when \(b\in K\), and \(S=\varnothing\) when \(b\notin K\). More generally,
\[
S=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (b+\operatorname{range}A)\cap K=\varnothing.
\]
If \(v\in\ker A\), then \(x\in S\) implies \(x+tv\in S\) for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\). Hence a nontrivial kernel makes the restriction unable to distinguish points along its kernel directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine cone restriction may be empty or universal; a nonzero kernel also forces invariance along entire affine lines and prevents pointwise distinction in those directions.
assumptions_latex: \(A:E\to F\) is linear, \(b\in F\), and \(K\subseteq F\) is a cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated range-intersection and kernel conditions characterize the elementary degeneracies of \(S\).

notation.meaning: Image subspace of the linear map.
Kernel directions invisible to the restriction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction by directions invisible to the linear part of an affine cone restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}\), let \(N=\ker A\), and let \(\pi:E\to E/N\) be the quotient map. There is a unique injective linear map \(\bar A:E/N\to F\) satisfying \(A=\bar A\pi\). For \[ \bar S:=\{\xi\in E/N:\bar A\xi+b\in K\}, \] one has \(S=\pi^{-1}(\bar S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient affine restriction factors exactly through the quotient by its kernel, where the induced linear map is injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bar A\pi\), \(\bar A\) is injective, and \(S=\pi^{-1}(\bar S)\).

notation.meaning: Induced injective map on the quotient.

children.title: Product Cone Representations
children.top_down_role: Cartesian assembly of independently represented cone-domain factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Product Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of finitely many conic representations using a product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(S_i:=\{x\in E:A_i x+b_i\in K_i\}\), where \(A_i:E\to F_i\) is linear and \(K_i\subseteq F_i\) is a convex cone. Define
\[
A x:=(A_1x,\ldots,A_mx),\qquad b:=(b_1,\ldots,b_m),\qquad K:=\prod_{i=1}^{m}K_i.
\]
Then
\[
\bigcap_{i=1}^{m}S_i=\{x\in E:Ax+b\in K\}.
\]
Thus finitely many conic restrictions on a shared variable compose into one conic representation over the Cartesian product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stacking affine maps and offsets turns finitely many cone constraints on one variable into a single constraint over the product of their cones.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite and all restrictions share the same variable space \(E\).
Each \(A_i:E\to F_i\) is linear and each \(K_i\subseteq F_i\) is a convex cone.

notation.meaning: Set represented by the ith conic restriction.
Product map obtained by stacking the component maps.
Cartesian product of the component cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections obtained by stacking conic constraints while retaining one common decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_i}\) be a convex cone, \(A_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{q_i}\) and \(B_i:\mathbb R^{p_i}\to\mathbb R^{q_i}\) be linear, \(b_i\in\mathbb R^{q_i}\), and
\[
S_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i},\ A_ix+B_iy_i-b_i\in K_i\}.
\]
Define \(K=\prod_{i=1}^mK_i\), \(A x=(A_1x,\ldots,A_mx)\), \(B(y_1,\ldots,y_m)=(B_1y_1,\ldots,B_my_m)\), and \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_m)\). Then
\[
\bigcap_{i=1}^mS_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists (y_1,\ldots,y_m),\ Ax+B(y_1,\ldots,y_m)-b\in K\}.
\]
Thus finite intersection preserves conic representability when finite product cones are admitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting finitely many conically represented sets amounts to stacking their constraints, sharing the visible variable, and taking the product of their cones.
assumptions_latex: All displayed spaces are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
The admissible cone family is closed under finite Cartesian products.

notation.meaning: The cone used by the ith representation.
Auxiliary variable specific to the ith representation.
The explicitly defined stacked conic data.

children.title: Shared-Variable Composition

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Variable Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiber-product composition of conic systems coupled through designated common variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(j=1,\ldots,m\), let \(u\in\mathbb R^r\), \(v_j\in\mathbb R^{s_j}\), \(y_j\in\mathbb R^{p_j}\), \(K_j\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_j}\), and let \(A_j:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^{q_j}\), \(C_j:\mathbb R^{s_j}\to\mathbb R^{q_j}\), and \(B_j:\mathbb R^{p_j}\to\mathbb R^{q_j}\) be linear, with \(b_j\in\mathbb R^{q_j}\). Define
\[
T_j=\{(u,v_j):\exists y_j\in\mathbb R^{p_j},\ A_ju+C_jv_j+B_jy_j-b_j\in K_j\}.
\]
The shared-variable composition
\[
T=\{(u,v_1,\ldots,v_m):(u,v_j)\in T_j\text{ for every }j\}
\]
has the product-cone representation
\[
T=\{(u,v_1,\ldots,v_m):\exists(y_1,\ldots,y_m),\ (A_ju+C_jv_j+B_jy_j-b_j)_{j=1}^m\in\prod_{j=1}^mK_j\}.
\]
The variable \(u\) is shared rather than independently quantified in the component systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic systems sharing a visible variable compose by retaining one copy of that variable and placing all component constraints in a product cone.
assumptions_latex: All displayed spaces are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fiber-product set \(T\) has the displayed product-cone representation.

notation.meaning: Visible variable shared by every component system.
Visible variable local to component j.
Auxiliary variable local to component j.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duplicate Product Blocks Alter Additive Barrier Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-level consequence of duplicating a cone restriction while leaving the visible feasible set unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) admit a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier \(F\). Duplicating the restriction \(g(x)\in K\) gives the product representation \((g(x),g(x))\in K\times K\) and additive barrier \[\widehat F(g(x),g(x))=F(g(x))+F(g(x)).\] The product barrier has parameter \(2\nu\), although \[\{x:g(x)\in K\}=\{x:(g(x),g(x))\in K\times K\}.\] More generally, additive product barriers sum the parameters of all factors, including redundant duplicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating a cone block leaves feasibility unchanged but doubles that block's contribution to an additive barrier parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(K\).
The product representation uses the additive barrier on its factors.

notation.meaning: barrier for the original cone factor
additive barrier for the duplicated product representation

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Product Blocks Alter Additive Barrier Parameters

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Predicate Redundancy Can Fail with Shared Auxiliaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier-order boundary for deleting a block whose components share auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R\) be visible and let \(u\in\mathbb R\) be a shared auxiliary variable. Define \[F_1(x,u)\iff u=0,\qquad F_2(x,u)\iff u=1.\] Individually, both projected predicates \(\exists u\,F_j(x,u)\) hold for every \(x\). Nevertheless, \[\{x:\exists u\,[F_1(x,u)\wedge F_2(x,u)]\}=\varnothing,\] whereas deleting either predicate yields all of \(\mathbb R\). Thus redundancy cannot be tested by separately projecting components when their witnesses must agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two constraints may each impose no visible restriction after separate projection yet be jointly inconsistent because they share an auxiliary variable.
assumptions_latex: The same auxiliary variable \(u\) is shared by both predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u(F_1\wedge F_2)\not\equiv(\exists uF_1)\wedge(\exists uF_2),\text{ and deleting either block changes the visible set}.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Predicate Redundancy Can Fail with Shared Auxiliaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Violation-Optimization Test for a Scalar Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy test for a scalar component over the jointly projected remaining composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the visible feasible set obtained after jointly eliminating the auxiliary variables from every component except \(g_r(x)\le0\), and define \[\rho_r:=\sup\{g_r(x):x\in R\}.\] If \(\rho_r\le0\), the component is redundant. Conversely, any \(x\in R\) with \(g_r(x)>0\) certifies nonredundancy. The test must use the joint remaining system rather than separately projected component witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a component's violation over the jointly projected remaining system: a nonpositive bound proves redundancy, while a positive feasible violation proves nonredundancy.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is the visible feasible set of the remaining jointly composed system.
The removed component has the scalar form \(g_r(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r\le0\Rightarrow g_r\text{ is redundant};\quad \exists x\in R:g_r(x)>0\Rightarrow g_r\text{ is nonredundant}.\)

notation.meaning: jointly projected visible feasible set after removing component r
supremal violation of the removed component

knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Optimization Test for a Scalar Component

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Visible-Projection Definition of a Redundant Composition Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General redundancy definition retaining all sharing constraints among auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x:\exists u\;\bigwedge_{j=1}^mF_j(x,u)\}\) and \(S_{-r}=\{x:\exists u\;\bigwedge_{j\ne r}F_j(x,u)\}\), where the same jointly quantified vector \(u\) retains every auxiliary-variable sharing constraint. Block \(r\) is redundant exactly when \(S=S_{-r}\). Since \(S\subseteq S_{-r}\), this is equivalently \(S_{-r}\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition block is redundant exactly when deleting it leaves the jointly projected visible set unchanged.
assumptions_latex: All sharing equations and retained component constraints remain under one existential quantifier.
Deleting block \(r\) does not delete auxiliary constraints needed by retained blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_r\text{ is redundant}\iff S=S_{-r}\iff S_{-r}\subseteq S.

notation.meaning: Visible projections before and after deletion of block r
Joint auxiliary vector, including shared auxiliaries

knowledge_statements.title: Visible-Projection Definition of a Redundant Composition Block
Redundant Composition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of component constraints already implied by the remaining conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_j\) be conic feasibility predicates on a common visible variable \(x\), possibly with separate auxiliary variables, and define \(S=\{x:F_j(x)\text{ holds for }j=1,\ldots,m\}\). If an index \(r\) satisfies
\[
\{x:F_j(x)\text{ holds for all }j\ne r\}\subseteq\{x:F_r(x)\text{ holds}\},
\]
then
\[
S=\{x:F_j(x)\text{ holds for all }j\ne r\}.
\]
Hence the \(r\)-th factor in the stacked product-cone representation is redundant and may be removed without changing the represented visible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composed conic constraint is redundant when all remaining constraints imply it; deleting its cone block then leaves the represented set unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Every predicate \(F_j\) has a well-defined conic representation.
The displayed implication holds after existential auxiliary variables are eliminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting \(F_r\) and its product-cone block preserves \(S\).

notation.meaning: The feasibility predicate contributed by component j.
Index of the potentially redundant component.
The visible feasible set of the full composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended conic formulations whose extra coordinates are existentially eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) has an auxiliary-variable lift over a cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) if there exist \(p\ge0\), linear maps \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(B:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^q\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\) such that
\[
S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+By-b\in K\}.
\]
The lifted feasible set is \(L=\{(x,y):Ax+By-b\in K\}\), and the original set is recovered by eliminating \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An auxiliary-variable lift represents a set as the visible coordinates of an affine conic system in a higher-dimensional space.
assumptions_latex: All ambient spaces are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.

children.title: Coordinate Projections

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Projections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a lifted feasible set onto its designated visible coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For integers \(n,p\ge0\), the coordinate projection onto the first \(n\) coordinates is the linear map
\[
\pi_x:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^n,\qquad \pi_x(x,y)=x.
\]
For any set \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\), its coordinate projection is
\[
\pi_x(L)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^p,\ (x,y)\in L\}.
\]
Thus projection is precisely existential elimination of the coordinates indexed by \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate projection retains selected visible coordinates and existentially eliminates all remaining coordinates of the lifted set.

notation.meaning: Set in the extended coordinate space.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Projections onto subspaces p. 37

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Projections onto subspaces p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Conicity under Coordinate Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic properties preserved when coordinates are eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\). If \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\) is convex, then \(\pi_x(L)\) is convex. If \(L\) is a convex cone, then \(\pi_x(L)\) is a convex cone. Neither conclusion asserts that \(\pi_x(L)\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate projection preserves convexity and conicity but need not preserve closedness.
assumptions_latex: For the conic conclusion, \(L\) is a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\pi_x(L)\text{ convex},\qquad L\text{ a convex cone}\Rightarrow\pi_x(L)\text{ a convex cone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Conicity under Coordinate Projection

children.title: Lift–Projection Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence between an extended formulation and its projected feasible domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Projection Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between existential lifted formulations and coordinate projections of affine conic slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a cone. The following are equivalent: (i) there exist \(p,A,B,b\) such that
\[
S=\{x:\exists y\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+By-b\in K\};
\]
(ii) there is an affine conic slice
\[
L=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p:Ax+By-b\in K\}
\]
whose coordinate projection satisfies \(S=\pi_x(L)\). Consequently, introducing auxiliary variables and projecting them away are the two directions of the same representation operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set has an auxiliary-variable conic formulation exactly when it is the coordinate projection of the corresponding affine conic slice.
assumptions_latex: All maps act between finite-dimensional real vector spaces.

notation.meaning: Affine conic slice in the lifted space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective and Optimizer Preservation across a Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization consequence of exact lift–projection equivalence for visible-coordinate objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\pi_x(L)\) and \(\varphi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Then \[\inf_{x\in S}\varphi(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in L}\varphi(x).\] Moreover, \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in L}\varphi(x)=\{(x,y)\in L:x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in S}\varphi(u)\},\] so projection of the lifted optimizer set equals the original optimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift preserves every objective depending only on visible variables, including its value and projected optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) depends only on the visible coordinate \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective and Optimizer Preservation across a Lift

children.title: Nonclosed Projection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Projected cone-representable sets whose boundary behavior requires closure distinctions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Safe Regime for Projection Closedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Major class in which projection cannot lose closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) is a polyhedron, then \(\pi_x(P)\) is a polyhedron and hence is closed. In particular, every coordinate projection or linear image of a polyhedral convex cone is a closed polyhedral convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves polyhedrality, so nonclosed projection regimes require nonpolyhedral geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Safe Regime for Projection Closedness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded-Witness Necessity for a Missing Projection Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary auxiliary-variable escape when a closed lifted set has a missing projected limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\) be closed, let \((x_k,y_k)\in L\), and suppose \(x_k\to\bar x\notin\pi_x(L)\). Then \((y_k)\) has no bounded subsequence, equivalently \(\|y_k\|\to+\infty\). Consequently, if every convergent sequence \((x_k)\subseteq\pi_x(L)\) has witnesses \(y_k\) containing a bounded subsequence, then \(\pi_x(L)\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missing limit point of the projection of a closed lifted set requires every associated witness sequence to escape to infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is closed in a finite-dimensional product space.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary witnesses for the visible sequence.
Missing limit point of the projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Witness Necessity for a Missing Projection Limit
Nonclosed Projection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed semidefinite cone can have a nonclosed coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the closed convex cone
\[
L=\left\{(a,b,c)\in\mathbb R^3:\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb S_+^2\right\}
\]
and the coordinate projection \(\pi(a,b,c)=(a,b)\). Then
\[
\pi(L)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},
\]
which is not closed. Thus a coordinate projection of a closed convex cone need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinate projection of the closed two-by-two positive-semidefinite cone onto its first diagonal and off-diagonal entries is a nonclosed convex cone.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^2\) carries the Euclidean topology inherited from \(\mathbb S^2\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite two-by-two matrices.
Coordinate realization of the positive-semidefinite cone in three variables.
Coordinate projection retaining a and b.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Cone Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic representation of a convex function through a lift of its epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. An epigraph cone lift of \(f\) over a convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) consists of an integer \(p\ge0\), linear maps \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(B:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^q\), and vectors \(d,b\in\mathbb R^q\) such that
\[
\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:\exists y\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
f(x)\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epigraph cone lift encodes the inequality f(x) ≤ t as feasibility of an affine conic system with auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f\) equals the displayed projection of an affine \(K\)-constraint.

notation.meaning: Set of pairs (x,t) satisfying f(x) at most t.
Coefficient vector of the scalar epigraph variable t.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Objective Reformulation by an Epigraph Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion of convex-function minimization into minimization of an epigraph coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists y,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K\}\), then for every \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \[\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\inf\{t:x\in X,\ \exists y,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K\}.\] Finite attained minimizers in the visible variable coincide, and every optimal lifted point satisfies \(t=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact epigraph lift replaces a convex objective by a linear epigraph objective without changing its value or visible minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has the displayed exact epigraph cone lift.
The additional feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Additional feasible set for the visible variable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Objective Reformulation by a Hypograph Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion of concave-function maximization into maximization of a hypograph coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{hypo}g=\{(x,t):\exists y,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K\}\), then for every \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \[\sup_{x\in X}g(x)=\sup\{t:x\in X,\ \exists y,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K\}.\] Finite attained maximizers in the visible variable coincide, and every optimal lifted point satisfies \(t=g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact hypograph lift replaces a concave objective by a linear hypograph objective without changing its value or visible maximizers.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) has the displayed exact hypograph cone lift.
The additional feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Objective Reformulation by a Hypograph Lift
Hypograph Cone Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic representation of a concave function through a lift of its hypograph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be proper and concave. A hypograph cone lift of \(g\) over a convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) consists of \(p\ge0\), compatible linear maps \(A,B\), and affine data \(d,b\) such that
\[
\operatorname{hypo}g=\{(x,t):\exists y\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
t\le g(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y,\ Ax+dt+By-b\in K.
\]
This is also an epigraph cone lift of the convex function \(-g\) after replacing \(t\) by \(-t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypograph cone lift encodes t ≤ g(x) for a concave function as a projected affine conic constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{hypo}g\) equals the displayed projection of an affine \(K\)-constraint.

notation.meaning: Set of pairs with t at most g(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-Scale Recovery of the Original Epigraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of the original epigraph as the unit-scale slice of its closed perspective cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed perspective \(f^\pi\) of a proper closed convex function \(f\), \[\operatorname{epi}f^\pi\cap\{(x,\tau,s):\tau=1\}=\{(x,1,s):(x,s)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit-scale affine slice of the perspective epigraph cone is exactly the original epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Scale Recovery of the Original Epigraph

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Scale Homogenization of an Epigraph Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of the positive-scale perspective system from an exact epigraph cone lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(u,r):\exists v,\ Au+dr+Bv-b\in K\}.\] For \(\tau>0\), \[s\ge\tau f(x/\tau)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y,\ Ax+ds+By-\tau b\in K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epigraph lift is homogenized at positive scale by multiplying its affine offset by the scale coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has the displayed exact epigraph lift over a cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Scale Homogenization of an Epigraph Lift
Perspective Cone Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous epigraph construction for the closed perspective of a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(f^\infty\) be its recession function. Define the closed perspective
\[
f^\pi(x,\tau)=\begin{cases}\tau f(x/\tau),&\tau>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&\tau=0,\\+\infty,&\tau<0.\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{epi}f^\pi=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,\tau,s):\tau>0,\ s\ge\tau f(x/\tau)\}
\]
is a closed convex cone. A perspective cone lift is any affine conic lift whose projection equals this epigraph; its conic homogeneity represents simultaneous scaling of \(x\), \(\tau\), and \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective homogenizes a convex function; its epigraph is a closed convex cone and may itself admit an auxiliary conic lift.
assumptions_latex: The recession function \(f^\infty\) uses the standard closed-convex convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f^\pi\) is the displayed closed convex cone.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard closed-perspective construction in finite-dimensional convex analysis
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed-perspective formula and assertion that its epigraph is a closed convex cone are nontrivial convex-analysis claims. No inspectable authoritative citation is supplied.

children.title: Perspective Closure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases arising when the perspective scaling coordinate reaches its limiting domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary failure of closedness for a strictly positive-scale perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(f^\infty(x)=0\) and \[P_+=\{(x,\tau,s):\tau>0,\ s\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}P_+=\{(x,\tau,s):\tau\ge0,\ s\ge0\}.\] Thus every \((x,0,s)\) with \(s\ge0\) is omitted by the positive-scale formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even the zero function has a nonclosed positive-scale perspective epigraph; closure adds its zero-scale boundary.
assumptions_latex: Closure is taken in \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Function Zero-Scale Omission
Perspective Closure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary completion at zero scale and failure of the unclosed positive-scale perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For proper closed convex \(f\), define \(P_+=\{(x,\tau,s):\tau>0,\ s\ge\tau f(x/\tau)\}\). Its closure satisfies
\[
\operatorname{cl}P_+=P_+\cup\{(x,0,s):s\ge f^\infty(x)\}.
\]
Thus the positive-scale formula alone generally fails to produce a closed cone: it omits every finite recession boundary point at \(\tau=0\). The closed-perspective epigraph is obtained exactly by adjoining these points. In particular, whenever \(f^\infty(x)<+\infty\) for some \(x\), sequences with \(\tau\downarrow0\) can converge to boundary points absent from \(P_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-scale perspective is generally nonclosed; closure adds exactly the zero-scale epigraph of the recession function.
assumptions_latex: Closure is taken in \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Recession function determining the zero-scale boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Cone Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological closedness of cones in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed if it is closed in the Euclidean topology; equivalently,
\[
x_k\in K\text{ for every }k\quad\text{and}\quad x_k\to x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\in K.
\]
Here conicity means \(\lambda x\in K\) whenever \(x\in K\) and \(\lambda\ge0\). Closedness does not by itself imply convexity or pointedness. If \(K\) is also convex, pointed, and has nonempty interior, then it is a proper cone under the standard finite-dimensional convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone is closed when it contains every limit of its convergent sequences; closedness alone does not imply convexity or pointedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ is closed}\Longleftrightarrow[(x_k\in K,\ x_k\to x)\Rightarrow x\in K]\).

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure as the Minimal Closed Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure completion of an arbitrary cone in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its Euclidean closure \(\overline K\) is a cone and is the smallest closed cone containing \(K\). If \(K\) is convex, then \(\overline K\) is also convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closure of a cone is its smallest closed-cone enlargement, and closure preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline K\) is the smallest closed cone containing \(K\), and \(K\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\overline K\text{ convex}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Closure as the Minimal Closed Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness and Convexity of the Positive-Semidefinite Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the basic topological and convexity property of the real PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\in\mathbb N\), let
\[
\mathbb S_+^n:=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\langle Xu,u\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^n\}.
\]
Then \(\mathbb S_+^n\) is a closed convex subset of \(\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive integer n, the set of real symmetric matrices whose quadratic forms are nonnegative is closed and convex in the real symmetric matrix space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb S_+^n\text{ is a closed convex subset of }\mathbb S^n

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Cone Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex cones, without assuming closedness, pointedness, or full dimensionality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(K\subseteq V\) of a finite-dimensional real vector space is a convex cone when \(K\neq\varnothing\) and, for every \(x,y\in K\) and \(\alpha,\beta\geq 0\), one has \(\alpha x+\beta y\in K\). Equivalently, \(K\) is closed under addition and multiplication by nonnegative scalars. In particular, \(0\in K\), and every line segment joining two points of \(K\) lies in \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cone is a nonempty set closed under every nonnegative linear combination of two of its elements.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic algebraic constructions on convex cones, without asserting preservation of closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Arbitrary intersections of convex cones are convex cones. If \(K\) and \(L\) are convex cones, then \(K\times L\) and \(K+L=\{x+y:x\in K,\ y\in L\}\) are convex cones. For every linear map \(A\), both \(A(K)\) and \(A^{-1}(K)\) are convex cones. Sums and linear images need not preserve closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersections, products, sums, linear images, and linear preimages preserve convex conicity, although sums and images can lose closedness.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) and \(L\) are convex cones in finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_iK_i\), \(K\times L\), \(K+L\), \(A(K)\), and \(A^{-1}(K)\) are convex cones whenever defined.

children.title: Conic-Hull Regimes
children.top_down_role: Domains arising from conic hull formation over generating sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Hull Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic hulls of arbitrary subsets of finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any subset \(S\subseteq V\), its conic hull is the smallest convex cone containing \(S\), and it admits the finite-combination representation
\[\operatorname{cone}(S)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i s_i:m\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0},\ s_i\in S,\ \lambda_i\geq0\right\}.\]
The sum for \(m=0\) is defined to be \(0\), so this representation also applies when \(S=\varnothing\). If \(\dim V=n\), every \(x\in\operatorname{cone}(S)\) admits such a representation with \(0\leq m\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic hull consists of all finite nonnegative combinations of points in the set, including the empty sum zero; in an n-dimensional space every element needs at most n generators.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite-dimensional, with \(\dim V=n\) for the generator bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cone}(S)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i s_i:m\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0},\ s_i\in S,\ \lambda_i\geq0\right\}\), and every \(x\in\operatorname{cone}(S)\) has such a representation with \(m\leq n\).

children.title: Nonclosed Conic Hulls

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex Generators with a Nonclosed Conic Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric epigraph family witnessing failure of closedness under conic-hull formation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(c>0\), let
\[
S_c=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\ge c/u\}.
\]
Then \(S_c\) is closed and convex, but
\[
\operatorname{cone}(S_c)=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(a,b):a>0,\ b>0\},
\]
which is not closed. In particular, \((1,1/k)\in\operatorname{cone}(S_c)\) for every \(k\ge1\), while \((1,1/k)\to(1,0)\notin\operatorname{cone}(S_c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex reciprocal-epigraph generator can have the open positive quadrant plus zero as its conic hull, so closed generators need not produce a closed cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_c\) is closed and convex while \(\operatorname{cone}(S_c)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Generators with a Nonclosed Conic Hull

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure treatment for a conic hull that is not topologically closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
\operatorname{clcone}(S):=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(S)}.
\]
It is the smallest closed convex cone containing \(S\), and
\[
x\in\operatorname{clcone}(S)\iff \exists x_k\in\operatorname{cone}(S)\text{ with }x_k\to x.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{cone}(S)\) is nonclosed exactly when \(\operatorname{cone}(S)\subsetneq\operatorname{clcone}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed conic hull adds precisely the limits of finite nonnegative combinations and is the smallest closed convex cone containing the generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clcone}(S)=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(S)}\), with strict containment exactly when the conic hull is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Conic Hull Completion
Nonclosed Conic Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed convex generating set whose conic hull is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[S=\left\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\geq u^{-1}\right\}.\]
The set \(S\) is closed and convex in \(\mathbb R^2\), but
\[\operatorname{cone}(S)=\{(0,0)\}\cup\left\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0,\ b>0\right\}.\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{cone}(S)\) is not closed: the sequence \(((1,k^{-1}))_{k\geq1}\) lies in \(\operatorname{cone}(S)\) and converges to \((1,0)\notin\operatorname{cone}(S)\). Thus closedness of a generating set does not ensure closedness of its conic hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex epigraph in the positive half-plane generates the open positive quadrant plus zero, which is a nonclosed cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is closed and convex, while \(\operatorname{cone}(S)\) is not closed.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Interior Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient interior of a cone in a finite-dimensional normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a cone \(K\subseteq V\), its interior is
\[\operatorname{int}K=\left\{x\in K:\text{there exists }\varepsilon>0\text{ such that }B(x,\varepsilon)\subseteq K\right\}.\]
Here \(B(x,\varepsilon)=\{y\in V:\|y-x\|<\varepsilon\}\). The interior-cone regime consists of cones satisfying \(\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing\). For a convex cone in finite dimensions, this is equivalent to \(\operatorname{span}K=V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone has nonempty interior when it contains an ambient open ball; for convex cones this is equivalent to spanning the ambient space.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional normed real vector space.
\(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone for the stated equivalence.

notation.meaning: open ball of radius epsilon about x
