children.title: Relative-Entropy Models
children.top_down_role: Cone representations involving relative entropy between nonnegative quantities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Convexity, Homogeneity, and Equal-Mass Nonnegativity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core structural properties of closed vector relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative vectors with the closed extended-value convention, \(D(p\|q)=\sum_i p_i\log(p_i/q_i)\) is jointly convex and positively homogeneous: \[D(\lambda p_1+(1-\lambda)p_2\|\lambda q_1+(1-\lambda)q_2)\le\lambda D(p_1\|q_1)+(1-\lambda)D(p_2\|q_2)\] for \(0\le\lambda\le1\), and \(D(\alpha p\|\alpha q)=\alpha D(p\|q)\) for \(\alpha\ge0\). If \(\mathbf1^Tp=\mathbf1^Tq<\infty\), then \(D(p\|q)\ge0\), with equality if and only if \(p=q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative entropy is jointly convex and positively homogeneous; for nonnegative vectors of equal total mass it is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when the vectors agree.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ uses its closed extended-value convention}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is jointly convex and positively homogeneous; if }\mathbf1^Tp=\mathbf1^Tq,\ D(p\|q)\ge0\text{ with equality iff }p=q
review_flags: Revised the builder claim from probability-vector nonnegativity to the sharp equal-total-mass form.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Convexity, Homogeneity, and Equal-Mass Nonnegativity
Relative-Entropy Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone epigraph model for discrete relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p,q\in\mathbb R_+^n\), define \(D(p\|q)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\log(p_i/q_i)\), with \(0\log(0/q_i)=0\) and value \(+\infty\) if some \(p_i>0=q_i\). Its epigraph satisfies \[r\ge D(p\|q)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists d\in\mathbb R^n:\ r\ge\sum_{i=1}^n d_i,\quad (-d_i,p_i,q_i)\in K_{\exp}\ \ (i=1,\ldots,n).\] Each cone constraint imposes \(d_i\ge p_i\log(p_i/q_i)\) with the stated closed-domain conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-entropy epigraph is represented by one exponential-cone constraint per coordinate and a linear sum bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-entropy epigraph formulation and extended-value boundary conventions are mathematically consistent, but no inspectable source is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropy as Relative Entropy to the Uniform Reference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed normalized identity relating two sibling model families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R_+^n\) with \(\sum_i p_i=1\) and \(u=\frac1n\mathbf1\), \[D(p\|u)=\log n-H(p).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For probability vectors, entropy maximization equals minimization of relative entropy to the uniform distribution.
review_flags: This sibling-bridging identity is adequately represented by a cross-index and need not be duplicated as a local publication record.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy as Relative Entropy to the Uniform Reference

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is the closed relative-entropy epigraph, joint convexity, positive homogeneity, and sharp equal-mass Gibbs inequality. The proposed uniform-reference identity is deferred in favor of a cross-index to Entropy Models. Generalized divergences and zero-coordinate closure pathology remain in their dedicated siblings.

children.title: Divergence Models
children.top_down_role: Cone-representable discrepancy measures derived from entropy structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone epigraph for generalized KL divergence with its affine correction terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in\mathbb R_+^n\), define \(I(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(x_i\log(x_i/y_i)-x_i+y_i\bigr)\) with the closed relative-entropy convention. Then \[I(x,y)\le\tau\iff\exists d\in\mathbb R^n:\ (-d_i,x_i,y_i)\in K_{\exp}\ (i=1,\ldots,n),\quad \sum_{i=1}^n(d_i-x_i+y_i)\le\tau.\] Moreover, \(I(x,y)\ge0\), with equality if and only if \(x=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized KL divergence adds affine correction terms to relative entropy; its epigraph uses one exponential cone per coordinate and it vanishes exactly when the vectors agree.
assumptions_latex: I\text{ uses the closed extended-value convention}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(x,y)\ge0,\quad I(x,y)=0\iff x=y,\quad \operatorname{epi}I\text{ has the displayed exponential-cone lift}
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized KL or I-Divergence Model
Divergence Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of generalized Kullback–Leibler divergence by exponential cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x,y\in\mathbb R_+^n\), and define \(D(x\|y)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log(x_i/y_i)\) using its closed extended-value convention. Its epigraph has the representation
\[
D(x\|y)\leq \tau
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists t\in\mathbb R^n:\ (-t_i,x_i,y_i)\in K_{\exp}\ (i=1,\ldots,n),\quad \sum_{i=1}^n t_i\leq\tau,
\]
where \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\}\). Thus any optimization model containing a convex upper bound on separable relative entropy admits an exponential-cone lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized KL-divergence epigraph is represented by one exponential-cone constraint per coordinate and a linear bound on their epigraph variables.
assumptions_latex: D(x\|y) uses the closed extended-value convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent and the representation content kind fits the Divergence Models leaf, but no inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied for the closed extended-value convention and exponential-cone epigraph equivalence.

children.title: Entropy Domain Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Closure-sensitive regimes involving zero coordinates or unsupported sign patterns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-scale closure branch governing entropy and relative-entropy cone models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v e^{u/v}\le w\},\] one has \[K_{\exp}=\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v e^{u/v}\le w\}\cup\{(u,0,w):u\le0,\ w\ge0\}.\] Hence \(K_{\exp}\cap\{v=0\}=\{(u,0,w):u\le0,\ w\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential cone's zero-scale boundary consists exactly of points with nonpositive first coordinate and nonnegative third coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Exponential-Cone Boundary Branch
Entropy Domain Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed scalar entropy and relative-entropy conventions at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed negative-entropy function is \(f(x)=x\log x\) for \(x>0\), \(f(0)=0\), and \(f(x)=+\infty\) for \(x<0\). Its perspective \(d(x,y)=x\log(x/y)\) satisfies \(d(0,y)=0\) for \(y\geq0\), \(d(x,0)=+\infty\) for \(x>0\), and is finite only when \(x=0\) or \(x>0,y>0\). Consequently, entropy-cone formulations must retain nonnegativity and the closed cone: imposing strict positivity excludes valid boundary points, while assigning a finite value at \(x>0,y=0\) destroys closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed entropy assigns zero at zero; relative entropy is infinite when its numerator is positive and denominator zero. Strict positivity can exclude valid solutions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary conventions are precise, and failure_boundary is the correct role for this leaf. An authoritative locator is still required to support the closure conventions at zero and the stated modeling consequences.

children.title: Geometric Programming in Exponential-Conic Form
children.top_down_role: Logarithmic transformations connecting geometric programs to exponential-cone models.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Programming in Exponential-Conic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic lift of a finite-dimensional geometric program with positive variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider positive variables \(x_j\), posynomial inequalities \(\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}c_{ik}x^{a_{ik}}\leq1\), and monomial equalities \(d_r x^{b_r}=1\), where \(c_{ik},d_r>0\). Set \(y_j=\log x_j\). Each posynomial inequality is equivalent to
\[
\exists u_{ik}\geq0:\ (a_{ik}^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_{ik},1,u_{ik})\in K_{\exp},\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{m_i}u_{ik}\leq1.
\]
Each monomial equality becomes \(b_r^{\mathsf T}y+\log d_r=0\). A posynomial objective is handled analogously by an epigraph variable, producing an exponential-cone program in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking logarithms converts monomial equalities to affine equations and lifts each posynomial inequality into exponential-cone constraints plus one linear sum bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k c_{ik}x^{a_{ik}}\leq1\iff\exists u_{ik}:\ (a_{ik}^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_{ik},1,u_{ik})\in K_{\exp},\ \sum_k u_{ik}\leq1

notation.meaning: componentwise logarithm of the positive decision vector

source_refs.locator: 9 Linear, quadratic, and geometric models p. 293

source_witnesses.locator: 9 Linear, quadratic, and geometric models p. 293

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating standard geometric programs from signomial or nonconvex equality models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The logarithmic convexification of a standard geometric program requires positive variables, positive posynomial coefficients, posynomial inequalities, and monomial equalities. A general posynomial equality becomes equality to a convex nonaffine log-sum-exp function and is generally nonconvex. Negative coefficients produce signomials for which the standard logarithmic log-sum-exp lift is unavailable in general. Such constraints therefore lack the standard exact exponential-cone GP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard conversion relies on positive coefficients and monomial equalities; general posynomial equalities and signomials fall outside it.
assumptions_latex: Standard GP monomial coefficients are positive
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{monomial equality}\mapsto\text{affine equality}\), whereas a general posynomial equality or signomial is not a convex GP constraint in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Program Convexity Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Recovery Under the Logarithmic Change of Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-point and minimizer correspondence for the exact standard-GP reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The componentwise map \(x\mapsto y=\log x\) is a bijection from \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\) to \(\mathbb R^n\), with inverse \(x=\exp y\). Therefore a standard GP and its exact logarithmic exponential-cone reformulation have corresponding feasible points. For a positive objective \(f_0\), minimizing the monotone transform \(\log f_0(e^y)\) preserves ordering, and attained minimizers recover as \(x^\star=\exp y^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logarithmic variables biject positive GP variables with unconstrained transformed variables and preserve minimizers under the monotone logarithm.
assumptions_latex: The transformed constraints are the exact standard-GP constraints
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Recovery Under the Logarithmic Change of Variables

children.title: Logistic Loss Exponential-Cone Model
children.top_down_role: Model family linking logistic objectives to exponential-cone graph representations.

children.title: Softplus Lift Family
children.top_down_role: Direct and log-sum-exp-based softplus representation families.

knowledge_statements.title: Softplus Lift Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-term exponential-cone epigraph lift for the softplus function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z,t\in\mathbb R\), the softplus epigraph admits the exact lift
\[
t\geq\log(1+\exp z)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists u,v\geq0:\ (-t,1,u)\in K_{\exp},\quad (z-t,1,v)\in K_{\exp},\quad u+v\leq1.
\]
Indeed, the two cone memberships encode \(u\geq\exp(-t)\) and \(v\geq\exp(z-t)\). This is the two-term log-sum-exp lift and can be applied independently to every softplus term in a separable objective or constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A softplus epigraph uses two exponential-cone triples and one linear sum inequality, equivalently representing a two-term log-sum-exp epigraph.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-term softplus lift is exact under the stated exponential-cone convention, and representation is the correct content kind. No source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Binary Logistic Encodings
children.top_down_role: Cone-model variants for binary-label likelihood and loss conventions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of linear aggregation in binary logistic cone models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell(r)=\log(1+e^{-r})\), \[\ell''(r)=\frac{e^r}{(1+e^r)^2}>0.\] Thus multiplying a nonconstant logistic term by a negative weight makes that term strictly concave in its affine margin. Arbitrary negative sample weights therefore do not, in general, define a convex logistic-loss model representable by minimizing the standard epigraph lifts with a linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative weights preserve convexity; a negative weight reverses a nonconstant logistic term and generally destroys the convex cone-model interpretation.
assumptions_latex: The margin varies along a nonzero affine direction
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Weight Convexity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-data cone model assembled from binary logistic epigraph blocks without regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observations \((a_i,y_i)\), \(y_i\in\{-1,1\}\), scores \(s_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}\beta+b\), and weights \(w_i\ge0\), the loss \(\sum_{i=1}^N w_i\log(1+e^{-y_i s_i})\) is represented by variables \(t_i,u_i,v_i\) satisfying \[(-t_i,1,u_i)\in K_{\exp},\quad (-y_i s_i-t_i,1,v_i)\in K_{\exp},\quad u_i+v_i\le1,\] while minimizing \(\sum_i w_i t_i\). For each positive-weight term, an attained optimum has a representative with \(t_i=\log(1+e^{-y_i s_i})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted binary logistic objective uses one independent two-cone softplus block per sample and a weighted linear objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\beta,b}\sum_i w_i\log(1+e^{-y_i s_i})\) equals the minimum of \(\sum_iw_it_i\) subject to the stated cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Binary Logistic Sample Aggregation
Binary Logistic Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone encoding for binary logistic loss under signed-label and Bernoulli conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s=a^{\mathsf T}\beta+b\). For a signed label \(y\in\{-1,1\}\), the logistic loss is \(\ell=\log(1+\exp(-ys))\). Its epigraph \(t\geq\ell\) is equivalent to
\[
\exists u,v\geq0:\ (-t,1,u)\in K_{\exp},\quad (-ys-t,1,v)\in K_{\exp},\quad u+v\leq1.
\]
For a Bernoulli label \(q\in\{0,1\}\), the equivalent loss is \(\log(1+\exp s)-qs\); it uses the same lift after replacing the softplus argument by \(s\) and subtracting \(qs\) through the epigraph affine expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary logistic loss is a softplus of the negative signed margin; signed and Bernoulli label conventions yield equivalent exponential-cone lifts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signed-label lift is correct, and the Bernoulli convention is consistently related through an affine epigraph adjustment. The representation kind fits Binary Logistic Encodings, but the record has no authoritative source locator.

children.title: Multiclass Probabilistic Loss Encodings
children.top_down_role: Log-sum-exp model variants for multiclass losses.

children.title: Multiclass Logistic Encodings
children.top_down_role: Exponential-cone encodings of multiclass logistic losses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential structure of hard-label multiclass logistic loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(p=\operatorname{softmax}(s)\) and one-hot vector \(e_y\), \[\nabla_sL(s,y)=p-e_y,\qquad \nabla_s^2L(s,y)=\operatorname{Diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Therefore the loss is convex; at finite scores its only Hessian null direction is the common-shift direction \(\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hard-label multiclass logistic gradient is predicted probability minus the observed one-hot label, and its Hessian is the softmax covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiclass Logistic Gradient and Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-Margin Form of Multiclass Logistic Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent hard-label loss expressed through competitor-relative scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observed class \(y\), \[L(s,y)=\log\sum_{k=1}^K e^{s_k}-s_y=\log\!\left(1+\sum_{k\ne y}e^{s_k-s_y}\right).\] Thus the loss depends only on relative scores, is nonnegative, and is strictly positive for every finite score vector. Its infimum zero is approached exactly when every competitor margin \(s_y-s_k\), \(k\ne y\), tends to \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard-label multiclass logistic loss is a log-sum-exp of competitor-relative scores and approaches zero only as all correct-class margins diverge.

notation.meaning: competitor score relative to the observed-class score

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Margin Form of Multiclass Logistic Loss
Multiclass Logistic Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone epigraph of hard-label multiclass logistic loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scores \(s\in\mathbb R^K\) and observed class \(y\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), define \(L(s,y)=\log(\sum_{k=1}^K\exp s_k)-s_y\). Then
\[
t\geq L(s,y)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists u\in\mathbb R_+^K:\ (s_k-s_y-t,1,u_k)\in K_{\exp}\ (k=1,\ldots,K),\quad \sum_{k=1}^K u_k\leq1.
\]
The formulation is invariant under adding the same scalar to every score, so an affine score normalization may be added without changing the represented loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard-label multiclass logistic loss is represented by one exponential-cone constraint per class and a linear sum bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hard-label multiclass logistic epigraph and common-shift invariance claim are mathematically consistent, and representation fits the leaf. No cited source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Cross-Entropy Encodings
children.top_down_role: Exponential-cone encodings of categorical cross-entropy losses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex differential structure for a fixed simplex-valued target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H(q,s)=\log\sum_k e^{s_k}-q^{\mathsf T}s\), \(q\in\Delta_K\), and \(p=\operatorname{softmax}(s)\), \[\nabla_sH(q,s)=p-q,\qquad \nabla_s^2H(q,s)=\operatorname{Diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Hence finite stationary points are exactly logits satisfying \(p=q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-entropy has gradient predicted probability minus target probability and a positive-semidefinite softmax-covariance Hessian.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Entropy Gradient and Hessian

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value decomposition and minimizers for a fixed target distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\in\Delta_K\), \(p=\operatorname{softmax}(s)\), and \(0\log0=0\), \[H(q,s)=-\sum_kq_k\log p_k=H(q)+D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q\|p)\geq H(q).\] Equality holds exactly when \(p=q\). A finite score vector attains equality if and only if every \(q_k>0\); if some \(q_k=0\), the infimum \(H(q)\) is approached only as the corresponding probabilities tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-entropy equals target entropy plus KL divergence; a finite-logit minimizer exists exactly for full-support targets.

notation.meaning: Shannon entropy of the target distribution

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Entropy Entropy–Divergence Decomposition
Cross-Entropy Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone epigraph for cross-entropy with a fixed target distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\mathbb R_+^K\) satisfy \(\sum_{k=1}^Kq_k=1\), and let \(s\in\mathbb R^K\) be class logits. The cross-entropy between \(q\) and the softmax probabilities generated by \(s\) is
\(H(q,s)=\log(\sum_{k=1}^K\exp s_k)-q^{\mathsf T}s\). Its epigraph is
\[
t\geq H(q,s)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists u\in\mathbb R_+^K:\ (s_k-q^{\mathsf T}s-t,1,u_k)\in K_{\exp}\ (k=1,\ldots,K),\quad \sum_{k=1}^K u_k\leq1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-entropy with fixed target probabilities is a log-sum-exp minus a linear score average and has a direct exponential-cone lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\geq H(q,s)\iff\exists u\geq0:\ (s_k-q^{\mathsf T}s-t,1,u_k)\in K_{\exp},\ \sum_k u_k\leq1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a fixed simplex-valued target, the stated cross-entropy formula and exponential-cone epigraph are correct. The selected representation kind fits the exact container, but an authoritative source locator is absent.

children.title: Class-Score Normalization
children.top_down_role: Log-sum-exp normalization structure shared by multiclass loss encodings.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Softmax Hessian Nullspace and Gauge Identifiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential characterization of common-shift nonidentifiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=\operatorname{softmax}(s)\) and \(f(s)=\log\sum_k e^{s_k}\). For finite \(s\), every \(p_k>0\), and \[\nabla^2f(s)=\operatorname{Diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{null}(\nabla^2f(s))=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}.\] Thus \(f(s)-q^{\mathsf T}s\), with \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}q=1\), is strictly convex on an affine gauge whose direction space is complementary to \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), but not on all of \(\mathbb R^K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The only flat direction of log-sum-exp is the common score shift; a complementary affine gauge removes that nonidentifiability.
knowledge_statements.title: Softmax Hessian Nullspace and Gauge Identifiability
Class-Score Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation invariance and affine gauges for softmax class scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(s\in\mathbb R^K\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\), softmax probabilities satisfy
\[
\frac{\exp(s_k+c)}{\sum_j\exp(s_j+c)}=\frac{\exp s_k}{\sum_j\exp s_j}.
\]
Accordingly, both hard-label logistic loss and distributional cross-entropy are unchanged by \(s\mapsto s+c\mathbf1\). Every score vector therefore has a unique representative satisfying \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s=0\), and each equivalence class also has a unique representative satisfying \(s_K=0\). Either affine normalization removes the common-shift nonidentifiability without altering predicted probabilities or loss values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Softmax probabilities and cross-entropy are invariant to a common score shift; zero-sum or reference-class gauges remove this nonidentifiability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The translation invariance and uniqueness of both the zero-sum and reference-class representatives are correct. Property is the appropriate content kind for this leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable source.

children.title: Label-Encoding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Categorical, indicator-vector, and probabilistic label formats used at the model boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditions under which a label vector is a categorical target distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L_q(s)=\log\sum_k e^{s_k}-q^{\mathsf T}s\), a categorical target requires \(q\geq0\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}q=1\). If \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}q\neq1\), then \[L_q(s+c\mathbf1)=L_q(s)+c(1-\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}q),\] so common-shift invariance fails. If some \(q_k<0\), \(q\) is not a probability distribution and the expression is not categorical cross-entropy, even when its entries sum to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A probabilistic label must be nonnegative and sum to one; otherwise either shift invariance or the probability interpretation fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\in\Delta_K\) is necessary and sufficient for \(q\) to encode a categorical target distribution
knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Label Validity Boundary
Label-Encoding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified hard, one-hot, and distributional label encodings for multiclass cross-entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\Delta_K=\{q\in\mathbb R_+^K:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}q=1\}\). The distributional-label loss is
\[
L_q(s)=\log\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^K\exp s_k\right)-q^{\mathsf T}s.
\]
A hard class label \(y\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\) is encoded by \(q=e_y\), giving \(L_{e_y}(s)=\log(\sum_k\exp s_k)-s_y\). Thus class indices and one-hot vectors produce the same multiclass logistic model, whereas general \(q\in\Delta_K\) covers soft labels and label smoothing without changing the exponential-cone epigraph template.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard indices and one-hot labels are equivalent; simplex-valued soft labels use the same cross-entropy and exponential-cone template.

notation.meaning: cross-entropy loss for target distribution q

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relationship among hard-index, one-hot, and simplex-valued labels is precise and compatible with the shared exponential-cone template. Representation fits the terminal container, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Regularized Logistic Cone Models
children.top_down_role: Composite models coupling exponential-cone losses with conic regularizers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Regularization Ensures a Unique Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundary for regularized affine-margin logistic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper, closed, and \mu-strongly convex with \mu>0. If every affine margin m_i is finite on \operatorname{dom}R and \lambda>0, then F(\beta)=\sum_{i=1}^N\log(1+e^{-m_i(\beta)})+\lambda R(\beta) is proper, closed, coercive, and \lambda\mu-strongly convex; hence it has a unique minimizer. Without positive coercive regularization, separating directions may prevent attainment and data-null directions may prevent uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive strongly convex regularizer gives existence and uniqueness; without adequate regularization, separation or null directions can cause nonattainment or nonuniqueness.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is proper, closed, and }\mu\text{-strongly convex}
m_i\text{ is affine and finite on }\operatorname{dom}R
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Regularization Ensures a Unique Solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete linear- and rotated-second-order-cone regularizer lift combined with exponential-cone logistic losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let m_i(\beta) be affine, \lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0, and Q=L^{\mathsf T}L\succeq0. The problem \min_\beta\sum_i\log(1+e^{-m_i(\beta)})+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}\beta^{\mathsf T}Q\beta has an exact product-cone formulation using the per-observation softplus lifts, a_j\ge\beta_j, a_j\ge-\beta_j, and (q,1,L\beta)\in\mathcal Q_r, where \mathcal Q_r=\{(u,v,z):2uv\ge\|z\|_2^2,\ u,v\ge0\}. The linear objective is \sum_i t_i+\lambda_1\sum_j a_j+\lambda_2q.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic-net logistic regression combines exponential-cone loss blocks, linear absolute-value epigraphs, and one rotated-cone quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_\beta\left[\sum_i\log(1+e^{-m_i(\beta)})+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+\tfrac{\lambda_2}{2}\beta^{\mathsf T}Q\beta\right]\text{ is preserved by the product-cone lift}
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Logistic Product-Cone Form
Regularized Logistic Cone Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite exponential-cone logistic loss with a conically representable convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let observations have affine margins \(m_i(\beta)\), and suppose a convex regularizer \(R\) has a conic epigraph \(R(\beta)\leq r\iff\exists w:\ A\beta+Br+Cw-d\in K_R\). For \(\lambda\geq0\), the problem
\[
\min_\beta\ \sum_{i=1}^N\log(1+\exp(-m_i(\beta)))+\lambda R(\beta)
\]
is equivalently obtained by minimizing \(\sum_i t_i+\lambda r\), imposing the two-exponential-cone softplus lift for every \(t_i\geq\log(1+\exp(-m_i(\beta)))\), and imposing \(A\beta+Br+Cw-d\in K_R\). Hence exponential-cone losses compose directly with norm, second-order-cone, or semidefinite regularizer lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized logistic regression combines per-observation exponential-cone loss lifts with any available conic epigraph of the convex regularizer.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is convex with the displayed conic epigraph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_\beta\sum_i\log(1+e^{-m_i(\beta)})+\lambda R(\beta)\text{ has a product-cone formulation over }K_{\exp}\text{ and }K_R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-cone construction correctly combines affine-margin softplus epigraphs with the assumed conic epigraph of a convex regularizer, and representation fits the composite-model leaf. The claim lacks an authoritative source locator.

children.title: Logistic Margin Numerical Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes created by extreme margins and poor data scaling.

children.title: Margin Scaling Effects
children.top_down_role: Conditioning consequences associated with the scale of logistic margins.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Hinge Approximation Under Margin Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform error for normalized scaled logistic loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), \(m\in\mathbb R\), and \(h(m)=\max\{0,-m\}\), \[0\leq \alpha^{-1}\log(1+e^{-\alpha m})-h(m)\leq\frac{\log2}{\alpha}.\] Consequently the normalized scaled logistic losses converge uniformly to \(h\), with the upper bound attained at \(m=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized scaled logistic loss approximates the hinge function uniformly with exact worst-case error log two divided by the scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Hinge Approximation Under Margin Scaling
Margin Scaling Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of positive margin scaling on logistic loss and its hinge-loss limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For margin \(m\in\mathbb R\) and scale \(\alpha>0\), define \(\ell_\alpha(m)=\log(1+\exp(-\alpha m))\). Then
\[
\ell_\alpha'(m)=-\frac{\alpha}{1+\exp(\alpha m)},\qquad
\ell_\alpha''(m)=\frac{\alpha^2\exp(\alpha m)}{(1+\exp(\alpha m))^2}>0.
\]
Moreover, \(\alpha^{-1}\ell_\alpha(m)\to\max\{0,-m\}\) pointwise as \(\alpha\to\infty\). Scaling therefore steepens the transition near zero margin, increases curvature there quadratically, and yields the hinge loss after normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling steepens logistic loss around zero; after division by the scale, the loss converges pointwise to the hinge function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The derivatives, strict convexity, normalized pointwise limit, and curvature-at-zero interpretation are correct. Property is suitable for Margin Scaling Effects, but the record has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Large Positive-Margin Regime
children.top_down_role: Numerical behavior arising from strongly positive logistic margins.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First- and second-order decay of logistic loss on nonnegative margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell(m)=\log(1+e^{-m})\) and \(m\geq0\), \[\frac12e^{-m}\leq-\ell'(m)=\frac{e^{-m}}{1+e^{-m}}\leq e^{-m},\qquad \frac14e^{-m}\leq\ell''(m)=\frac{e^{-m}}{(1+e^{-m})^2}\leq e^{-m}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative margins, both gradient magnitude and curvature are comparable to exp minus the margin.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Margin Gradient and Curvature Bounds
Large Positive-Margin Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative decay of logistic loss for nonnegative signed margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the logistic margin loss \(\ell(m)=\log(1+\exp(-m))\) and every \(m\geq0\),
\[
\exp(-m)-\tfrac12\exp(-2m)\leq\ell(m)\leq\exp(-m).
\]
Consequently, \(\ell(m)/\exp(-m)\to1\) as \(m\to+\infty\), while \(\ell'(m)=-1/(1+\exp m)\to0\). Thus correctly classified observations with large positive margins contribute exponentially small loss and gradient, although their contribution remains strictly positive at every finite margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At large positive margins, logistic loss and gradient decay exponentially; the loss is asymptotic to the negative-margin exponential.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounds and asymptotic statements are correct for nonnegative margins, and property fits the regime leaf. No authoritative source with an inspectable locator is provided.

children.title: Large Negative-Margin Regime
children.top_down_role: Numerical behavior arising from strongly negative logistic margins.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order behavior of scalar logistic loss on nonpositive margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell(m)=\log(1+e^{-m})\) and \(m\leq0\), \[\ell''(m)=\frac{e^m}{(1+e^m)^2},\qquad \frac14e^m\leq\ell''(m)\leq e^m.\] Hence \(\ell''(m)\to0\) exponentially as \(m\to-\infty\), while \(\ell'(m)\to-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At large negative margins, logistic-loss curvature vanishes exponentially while the gradient saturates at minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Margin Curvature Decay

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies the linear asymptote and gradient saturation for nonpositive logistic margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the logistic loss \(\ell(m)=\log(1+e^{-m})\) and every margin \(m\le 0\), write \(s=-m\ge 0\). Then \[\ell(m)=s+\log(1+e^{-s}),\qquad 0<\ell(m)-s\le e^{-s}.\] Moreover, \(\ell'(m)=-1/(1+e^m)\), so \[0\le \ell'(m)+1=\frac{e^m}{1+e^m}\le e^m.\] Thus the loss approaches \(-m\) and its derivative approaches \(-1\), both with errors exponentially small in \(-m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a large negative margin, logistic loss is the linear function minus the margin up to an exponentially small correction, while its derivative approaches minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Large Negative-Margin Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic identities and bounds are mathematically consistent and fit the property container, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Overflow Avoidance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation limits relevant to overflow-resistant exponential-cone models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branchwise evaluation of the scalar logistic derivative without positive exponential arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The derivative may be evaluated as \[\ell'(m)=\begin{cases}-e^{-m}/(1+e^{-m}),&m\geq0,\\-1/(1+e^m),&m<0.\end{cases}\] Each branch exponentiates a nonpositive argument, so the exponential lies in \((0,1]\) in exact arithmetic and creates no exponential overflow. If the exponential underflows to zero, the branch returns the corresponding limiting value \(0\) or \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign-based formula evaluates the logistic gradient using only nonpositive exponential arguments and avoids exponential overflow.
assumptions_latex: The exponential implementation does not overflow on nonpositive finite arguments
knowledge_statements.title: Overflow-Safe Logistic Gradient Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a small positive logistic loss through rounded addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(e^{-m}\) is representable, naive evaluation of \(\log(1+e^{-m})\) can return zero for large positive \(m\) if \(\operatorname{fl}(1+e^{-m})=1\). Evaluating \(\log1p(e^{-m})\), or the max-plus-\(\log1p\) identity, avoids this addition-level loss subject to the numerical guarantees of the supplied \(\log1p\) routine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naive evaluation can lose a representable small loss when one plus the exponential rounds to one; log1p avoids that addition-level loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Softplus Precision Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(F_{\max}>1\) is the largest finite representable positive number
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct evaluation of \(e^{-m}\) can overflow when \(m<-\log F_{\max}\), whereas the stabilized formula has no positive exponential argument.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point overflow boundary for direct and stabilized evaluation of scalar logistic loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\max}>1\) be the largest finite positive value in a floating-point system. Directly evaluating \(e^{-m}\) in \(\ell(m)=\log(1+e^{-m})\) can overflow whenever \(-m>\log F_{\max}\). The equivalent identity \[\ell(m)=\max\{0,-m\}+\log\!\left(1+e^{-|m|}\right)\] evaluates an exponential whose argument is always nonpositive, hence its exponential lies in \((0,1]\) and cannot overflow. Underflow of \(e^{-|m|}\) merely removes a correction smaller than the system's representable range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct logistic-loss evaluation risks overflow below minus the logarithm of the largest finite number; the standard max-plus-log formula prevents exponential overflow.
knowledge_statements.title: Overflow Avoidance Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stabilized identity is correct, but the precise overflow and underflow assertions depend on the floating-point model and require a source with a specific locator.

children.title: Power-Cone Models
children.top_down_role: Power, norm, product, and weighted-mean representations using power-cone blocks.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Sets Representable Using the Power Cone

children.title: Scalar Power-Function Models
children.top_down_role: Power-function graph models organized by exponent and domain regime.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating genuine power-cone regimes from the exponent-zero constant function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p=0\), the real power satisfies \(x^0=1\) on \(x>0\), whose epigraph is \[E_0=\{(x,t):x>0,\ t\ge1\}.\] Its closure is \[\overline E_0=\{(x,t):x\ge0,\ t\ge1\},\] corresponding to the closed extension that assigns value one at zero. Retaining the positive domain instead excludes all points with \(x=0\). Because the formulas \(K_{1/p}\) and \(K_p\) have no meaning at \(p=0\), the chosen domain or closed extension must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At exponent zero the power is constant on the positive domain; including zero requires an explicit closed-extension convention and cannot be obtained by formal substitution into a power-cone formula.
assumptions_latex: The scalar power is initially defined on \(x>0\).
No value at \(x=0\) has been imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Exponent Domain Convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint interpretation of the absolute-power epigraph at exponent one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the closed endpoint convention \[K_1=\{(u,v,w):u\ge|w|,\ v\ge0\},\] the seed formula at \(p=1\) becomes \[(t,1,x)\in K_1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad t\ge|x|.\] If a modeling system defines power cones only for parameters strictly between zero and one, the same endpoint must instead be represented by the two linear inequalities \(t\ge x\) and \(t\ge-x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At exponent one, the closed power-cone endpoint is the absolute-value epigraph; systems without endpoint cones should use two linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Either the displayed closed endpoint convention is adopted or the endpoint is modeled linearly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t,1,x)\in K_1\iff t\ge|x|\) under the closed endpoint convention.

notation.meaning: closed parameter-one endpoint of the power-cone family

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Power Endpoint Convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-domain epigraph model for scalar powers with negative exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p<0\) and \(\alpha=1/(1-p)\in(0,1)\). Then \[x>0,\quad t\ge x^p\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(t,x,1)\in K_\alpha.\] Because the signed cone coordinate is fixed to the nonzero constant one, cone membership forces both \(t>0\) and \(x>0\), preserving the strict natural domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative scalar power has a one-block power-cone epigraph whose fixed nonzero coordinate automatically enforces the strict positive domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Power Epigraphs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-cone model for a nonnegative scalar power with exponent strictly between zero and one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<p<1\), \(x\ge0\), and \(t\in\mathbb R\). Then \[t\le x^p\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists z\ge0:\ (x,1,z)\in K_p,\quad t\le z.\] If \(t\ge0\) is already imposed, this is equivalently \((x,1,t)\in K_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional power between zero and one has a one-block nonnegative hypograph model and a one-auxiliary full-hypograph model.
knowledge_statements.title: Concave Fractional-Power Hypographs

notation.meaning: three-dimensional power cone with parameter alpha

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex epigraph representation for the scalar absolute-power function with exponent \(p\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\alpha\le1\), define the three-dimensional power cone by \[K_\alpha=\left\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R:\ u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\ge |w|\right\}.\] If \(p\ge1\), then the epigraph of \(x\mapsto |x|^p\) has the exact conic representation \[t\ge |x|^p\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t,1,x)\in K_{1/p}.\] Constants or affine expressions may replace \(x\) and \(t\) when the resulting cone arguments remain affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exponent at least one, the epigraph of the scalar absolute power is exactly one three-dimensional power-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Power-Function Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is standard and fits the container, but no source is supplied and the endpoint convention for K_1 should be supported explicitly.

children.title: General p-Norm Power-Cone Models
children.top_down_role: Norm epigraph constructions using separable power-cone components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint boundary of the separable p-norm power-cone construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the primitive definition \(K_\alpha=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\}\) restricted to \(0<\alpha<1\), the separable construction applies directly to \(1<p<\infty\). For \(p=1\), adopting the degenerate endpoint convention \(K_1=\{(u,v,w):u\ge|w|,\ v\ge0\}\) reduces the construction to linear absolute-value epigraphs. The case \(p=\infty\) is represented directly by \(-t\le x_i\le t\) for every \(i\), not by substituting \(\alpha=0\) into the finite-p construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite p uses genuine power cones; p=1 is a degenerate linear endpoint, while the infinity norm uses linear coordinate bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_\infty\le t\iff -t\le x_i\le t\ \text{for every }i\), while \(p=1\) requires an explicit endpoint convention.

notation.meaning: Degenerate endpoint power cone under the stated convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Exponent Conventions

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_p\le t\iff \exists r\in\mathbb R_+^n:\ (r_i,t,x_i)\in K_{1/p},\ \sum_i r_i\le t\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable power-cone formulation of the finite-dimensional \(p\)-norm epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge1\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(t\ge0\). Using \(K_\alpha=\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R:u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\}\), one has \[\|x\|_p\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists r\in\mathbb R_+^n:\ (r_i,t,x_i)\in K_{1/p}\ \text{for all }i,\quad \sum_{i=1}^n r_i\le t.\] For \(t>0\), each cone constraint is equivalent to \(|x_i|^p\le r_i t^{p-1}\); the equivalence extends to \(t=0\) by closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A p-norm epigraph is represented by one separable power-cone constraint per coordinate and a single linear sum inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: General p-Norm Power-Cone Models

children.title: Weighted Product Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Product-domain representations indexed by exponent weights.

children.title: Monomial Cone Representations
children.top_down_role: Power-cone interfaces for monomial expressions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp convex-representability boundary for direct nonnegative monomial hypographs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \beta\ge0,\ \beta\ne0,\quad d:=\sum_i\beta_i>1\Longrightarrow\operatorname{hypo}\left(\prod_i x_i^{\beta_i}\right)\ \text{is nonconvex}.\quad In particular,\ \operatorname{hypo}(x\mapsto x^2)\ \text{is nonconvex}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total degree greater than one makes the monomial hypograph nonconvex, so its normalized root representation is not a direct conic hypograph of the original monomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Degree Boundary for Monomial Hypographs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-power-cone representation when total monomial degree does not exceed one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \beta_i\ge0 and d=\sum_i\beta_i\in(0,1]. Set \gamma=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_n,1-d), omitting the final zero weight when d=1. Then\quad t\le\prod_i x_i^{\beta_i}\Longleftrightarrow\exists z\ge0:\ ((x,1),z)\in K_\gamma,\quad t\le z.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monomial of degree at most one has a direct power-cone hypograph after adding a fixed unit coordinate of weight one minus the degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\le\prod_i x_i^{\beta_i}\iff\exists z\ge0:\ ((x,1),z)\in K_{(\beta,1-d)},\ t\le z
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Hypographs of Concave Monomials
Monomial Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized cone representation of a nonnegative monomial's weighted geometric-mean root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta_i\ge0\), \(d=\sum_{i=1}^n\beta_i>0\), and \(\alpha_i=\beta_i/d\). For \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(q\ge0\), the generalized power cone gives \[q\le\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\alpha_i}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (x,q)\in K_\alpha,\] where \[K_\alpha=\left\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R_+^n\times\mathbb R:\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\alpha_i}\ge|z|\right\}.\] At equality, \(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\beta_i}=q^d\). The final scalar power relation requires separate convexity analysis and is not generally itself a cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative root variable, normalized monomial exponents give an exact generalized-power-cone representation of the weighted geometric-mean root; recovering the original monomial requires a separate scalar power relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\le\prod_i x_i^{\beta_i/d}\iff (x,q)\in K_{\beta/d}\), and equality implies \(\prod_i x_i^{\beta_i}=q^d\).

children.title: Weighted-Product Cone Representations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Direct Use of the Hypograph Variable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample showing why the absolute-value cone coordinate needs a nonnegative auxiliary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x_i=1 for every i and t=-2. Then t\le\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}=1, but (x,t)\notin K_\alpha because |t|=2>1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative hypograph value can be feasible while failing direct generalized-power-cone membership.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Direct Use of the Hypograph Variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual under the Euclidean pairing for strictly positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: K_\alpha^*=\left\{(y,w)\in\mathbb R_+^n\times\mathbb R:\ |w|\le\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{y_i}{\alpha_i}\right)^{\alpha_i}\right\},\qquad \alpha_i>0,\quad\sum_i\alpha_i=1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual weighted-product cone has the same product form after dividing each nonnegative dual coordinate by its weight.

children.title: Exponent-Weight Normalization
children.top_down_role: Normalization conventions governing exponent-weight data.

children.title: Weighted Geometric-Mean Hypographs
children.top_down_role: Direct generalized-power-cone models indexed by weight vectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural Properties of the Weighted Geometric Mean
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic properties supporting the direct convex hypograph model for positive normalized weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) satisfy \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and define \(G_\alpha(x)=\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}\) on \(\mathbb R_+^n\) by continuous extension. Then \(G_\alpha\) is continuous, coordinatewise nondecreasing, concave, and positively homogeneous of degree one. On \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \[\log G_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i\log x_i.\] Its hypograph is therefore a closed convex cone, and \(G_\alpha(x+y)\ge G_\alpha(x)+G_\alpha(y)\) for \(x,y\in\mathbb R_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive normalized weights, the geometric mean is continuous, monotone, concave, degree-one homogeneous, log-affine in logarithmic coordinates, and superadditive; its hypograph is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{hypo}G_\alpha\) is a closed convex cone and \(G_\alpha(x+y)\ge G_\alpha(x)+G_\alpha(y)\).

notation.meaning: hypograph of the weighted geometric mean

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Properties of the Weighted Geometric Mean

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfy \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and define \(G_\alpha(x)=\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}\) on \(\mathbb R_+^n\). Its closed hypograph is \[\operatorname{hypo}G_\alpha=\left\{(x,t):\exists z\ge0,\ (x,z)\in K_\alpha,\ t\le z\right\},\] where \[K_\alpha=\left\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R_+^n\times\mathbb R:G_\alpha(x)\ge|z|\right\}.\] Hence any affine lower bound on \(G_\alpha(x)\) is representable using one generalized power-cone membership and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed hypograph of any normalized weighted geometric mean has a direct generalized power-cone representation with one nonnegative auxiliary.

children.title: Three-Dimensional Power-Cone Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Extended formulations assembled from basic three-dimensional power-cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Hypograph from a Nonnegative Product Tree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of the nonnegative-root tree lift to an unrestricted hypograph coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the weighted binary-tree construction of the immutable seed, let \(z_r\ge0\) be the root auxiliary and let \(t\in\mathbb R\). Then \[t\le\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\alpha_i}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists(z_v):\ \mathcal T(x,z)\ \text{holds and }t\le z_r,\] where \(\mathcal T(x,z)\) denotes all tree power-cone constraints. Thus one additional affine inequality recovers the full closed hypograph, including negative values of \(t\). A full binary tree with \(n\) leaves has \(n-1\) internal auxiliaries and cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding t no greater than the nonnegative root converts the product tree into a representation of the full geometric-mean hypograph.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Hypograph from a Nonnegative Product Tree
Three-Dimensional Power-Cone Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary extended formulation of the nonnegative portion of a generalized weighted geometric-mean hypograph using three-dimensional cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a rooted binary tree have leaf \(i\) carrying \(x_i\ge0\) and weight \(\alpha_i>0\), with \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\). For every node \(v\), let \(w_v\) be the sum of its descendant leaf weights, and set \(z_i=x_i\) at the leaves. If an internal node \(v\) has children \(a,b\), impose \[(z_a,z_b,z_v)\in K_{w_a/w_v},\qquad z_v\ge0.\] These constraints project at each node onto \[0\le z_v\le\prod_{i\in L(v)}x_i^{\alpha_i/w_v}.\] In particular, at the root \(r\) they project exactly onto \[0\le z_r\le\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\alpha_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary tree of three-dimensional power cones exactly represents the nonnegative portion of a weighted geometric-mean hypograph.
assumptions_latex: A rooted binary tree has leaves indexed by \(1,\ldots,n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tree's three-dimensional power-cone constraints project exactly onto \(0\le z_r\le\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}\).

children.title: Product-Tree Topology Tradeoff

children.title: Balanced Product Trees
children.top_down_role: Product decompositions organized to limit tree depth.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Trees for Arbitrary Leaf Counts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Height-minimizing equal-weight geometric-mean decomposition for a non-power-of-two number of factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\) and \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\ge0\). A full binary tree with \(n\) leaves can have height \(h=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\). For each node \(v\), let \(m_v\) be its number of descendant leaves, set leaf values \(z_i=x_i\), and, for every internal node \(v\) with children \(a,b\), impose \((z_a,z_b,z_v)\in K_{m_a/m_v}\) and \(z_v\ge0\). The root projection is exactly \[0\le z_r\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\right)^{1/n}.\] The formulation has \(n-1\) internal auxiliaries and cone blocks and dependency depth \(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every factor count, a minimum-height binary tree exactly represents the equal-weight geometric mean with n minus one power-cone blocks and ceiling-logarithmic depth.
assumptions_latex: Each internal exponent is the child subtree size divided by the parent subtree size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le z_r\le(\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}\) is represented with \(n-1\) blocks and depth \(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\).

notation.meaning: number of descendant leaves of node v
three-dimensional power cone with parameter theta

knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Trees for Arbitrary Leaf Counts
Balanced Product Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equal-weight nonnegative geometric-mean formulation for a power-of-two number of factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=2^h\) and \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\ge0\). Place the factors at the leaves of a complete binary tree of height \(h\). For each internal node \(v\) with child values \(z_a,z_b\), introduce \(z_v\ge0\) and impose \[(z_a,z_b,z_v)\in K_{1/2},\] equivalently \(z_v^2\le z_a z_b\). The constraints project at the root exactly onto \[0\le z_r\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\right)^{1/n}.\] The formulation uses \(n-1\) cone blocks and has dependency depth \(\log_2 n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a power-of-two number of factors, a balanced tree of geometric-mean cones exactly represents the nonnegative portion of the geometric-mean hypograph with logarithmic dependency depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete balanced tree of \(K_{1/2}\) constraints represents \(0\le z_r\le(\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}\) with depth \(h\).

children.title: Sequential Product Trees
children.top_down_role: Product decompositions organized as successive factor combinations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Left-deep decomposition of a weighted geometric mean with arbitrary positive normalized weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i\ge0\), \(\alpha_i>0\), and \(A_k=\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i\), with \(A_n=1\). Set \(q_1=x_1\). For \(k=2,\ldots,n\), introduce \(q_k\ge0\) and impose \[(q_{k-1},x_k,q_k)\in K_{A_{k-1}/A_k}.\] The stage-\(k\) projection is \[0\le q_k\le\prod_{i=1}^k x_i^{\alpha_i/A_k},\] and the final projection is \[0\le q_n\le\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\alpha_i}.\] The lift uses \(n-1\) power-cone blocks and has dependency depth \(n-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive power-cone combinations exactly represent an arbitrarily weighted geometric mean when each stage uses the accumulated-weight ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le q_n\le\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}\) is represented with \(n-1\) blocks and depth \(n-1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Sequential Product Recursion
Sequential Product Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Left-deep exact formulation of the nonnegative portion of an equal-weight geometric-mean hypograph using successive power cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\ge0\), set \(q_1=x_1\). For \(k=2,\ldots,n\), introduce \(q_k\ge0\) and impose \[(q_{k-1},x_k,q_k)\in K_{(k-1)/k},\] equivalently \(q_k\le q_{k-1}^{(k-1)/k}x_k^{1/k}\). The recursion projects exactly onto \[0\le q_n\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\right)^{1/n}.\] This sequential formulation uses \(n-1\) three-dimensional cone blocks and has dependency depth \(n-1\), with every internal auxiliary shared only by adjacent stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successively combining the current nonnegative partial mean with one new factor exactly represents the nonnegative portion of the geometric-mean hypograph using n minus one cones and linear dependency depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion \(q_k\le q_{k-1}^{(k-1)/k}x_k^{1/k}\) represents \(0\le q_n\le(\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}\) with depth \(n-1\).

children.title: Tree Depth–Sparsity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparative depth, auxiliary-variable, and sparsity profiles of product trees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dependency-depth bounds for binary product-tree decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a rooted binary tree has \(m\ge2\) leaves and height \(h\), then \(m\le2^h\), so every binary product-tree decomposition satisfies \[h\ge\lceil\log_2 m\rceil.\] A minimum-height full binary tree attains \(h=\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\), while a left-deep sequential tree has \(h=m-1\). Every full binary topology has exactly \(m-1\) internal cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ceiling log base two of the factor count is the sharp minimum binary-tree depth; a sequential tree has the maximal linear depth, while all full binary trees use the same number of blocks.
assumptions_latex: Each internal product operation has exactly two children.
Dependency depth is the maximum root-to-leaf edge count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\le h\le m-1\), with the endpoint profiles attained by minimum-height and sequential trees.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Binary-Tree Dependency Depth
Tree Depth–Sparsity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-tree formulations of an equally weighted geometric mean using local power-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\ge 0\) label the leaves of a full binary tree. For each node \(v\), let \(m_v\) be its number of descendant leaves and impose \(z_v\le z_{v_L}^{m_{v_L}/m_v}z_{v_R}^{m_{v_R}/m_v}\) at every internal node, with \(z_i=x_i\) at leaves. Then \(z_{\mathrm{root}}\le(\prod_{i=1}^m x_i)^{1/m}\), and equality is attainable recursively. Every topology uses \(m-1\) three-variable cone constraints. A balanced tree has depth \(\lceil\log_2m\rceil\), whereas a sequential tree has depth \(m-1\); thus topology changes propagation depth and global incidence structure but not local constraint sparsity or the projected hypograph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All binary product trees use the same number of locally sparse constraints, but balanced trees reduce dependency depth from linear to logarithmic without changing the represented geometric mean.
assumptions_latex: Each internal constraint uses weights equal to the child subtree sizes divided by the parent subtree size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{root}}\le(\prod_{i=1}^m x_i)^{1/m}\), with \(m-1\) local constraints and topology-dependent depth.

notation.meaning: number of original factors below tree node v
auxiliary value associated with node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the topology, depth, sparsity, and exact-projection claims have no cited evidence.

children.title: Degenerate Factor Placement
children.top_down_role: Topology-sensitive behavior involving zero or boundary factors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Root Does Not Identify a Zero Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse to upward zero propagation in a hypograph product tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a product-tree hypograph lift with nonnegative auxiliaries and constraints \(z_v\le z_a^{\theta_v}z_b^{1-\theta_v}\), where \(0<\theta_v<1\). Even if every leaf satisfies \(x_i>0\), setting one internal auxiliary and all its ancestors to zero is feasible. Consequently, \(z_r=0\) does not imply that any leaf factor is zero. The universally valid implication is only that a zero leaf forces every auxiliary on its ancestor path to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypograph slack allows a zero root even when every factor is positive, so root zero does not certify a degenerate input factor.
assumptions_latex: The lift uses hypograph inequalities rather than graph equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_r=0\not\Rightarrow\exists i:\ x_i=0\), while \(x_i=0\Rightarrow z_v=0\) for every ancestor \(v\) of leaf \(i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Root Does Not Identify a Zero Factor
Degenerate Factor Placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of locating zero or fixed factors at different leaves of a product tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a valid weighted product-tree representation of \(g(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m x_i^{\alpha_i}\), where \(x_i\ge 0\), \(\alpha_i>0\), and \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\). Permuting factor-weight pairs among the leaves preserves the projected hypograph \(\{(x,t):t\le g(x)\}\) when all subtree weights are recomputed from their descendant leaf weights. If a leaf factor is zero and all auxiliary variables are constrained to be nonnegative, every auxiliary variable on the path from that leaf to the root is forced to zero. Thus placement changes the length and location of the guaranteed forced-zero chain, while leaving the root value and projected hypograph unchanged; other auxiliaries may also be zero for independent reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reordering factor-weight pairs does not change the represented weighted geometric mean. A zero leaf forces every auxiliary on its path to the root to zero, although other auxiliaries may also vanish independently.
assumptions_latex: Every subtree weight is the sum of its descendant leaf weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Leaf permutations preserve the projected hypograph, and a zero leaf forces every auxiliary on its ancestor path to zero.

notation.meaning: weighted geometric mean of the leaf factors

children.title: Geometric-Mean Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Domain behavior when weighted factors approach or attain the boundary.

children.title: Zero-Factor Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric-mean domains containing factors fixed at zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Factor Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary value of a weighted geometric mean when a positive-weight factor vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^m\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i=1\), and define \(g_\alpha(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m x_i^{\alpha_i}\) on \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\), using its continuous extension from \(\mathbb{R}_{++}^m\). Then \(g_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if at least one coordinate \(x_i\) is zero. Hence the hypograph condition \(t\le g_\alpha(x)\) reduces to \(t\le0\) on any such boundary face; if the model also imposes \(t\ge0\), it forces \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With strictly positive weights, one zero factor makes the geometric mean zero; a nonnegative hypograph variable is then forced to zero.

notation.meaning: weighted geometric mean with weight vector alpha

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-factor characterization is precise and fits the leaf, but no source supports the stated continuous boundary extension.

children.title: Vanishing-Factor Limits
children.top_down_role: Behavior as positive weighted factors approach zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the zero-limit conclusion when another supported factor may diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2>0\) with \(\alpha_1+\alpha_2=1\), set \(x_1(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon\) and \(x_2(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-\alpha_1/\alpha_2}\). Then \(x_1(\varepsilon)\downarrow0\) and \(x_2(\varepsilon)\to+\infty\), while \(x_1(\varepsilon)^{\alpha_1}x_2(\varepsilon)^{\alpha_2}=1\). Thus a supported factor tending to zero forces the mean to zero only when the remaining supported factors are suitably controlled, for example fixed or bounded above.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diverging supported factor can exactly offset a vanishing factor, so the zero limit requires control of the other factors.

notation.meaning: Positive path parameter tending to zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Compensating-Factor Path Dependence
Vanishing-Factor Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic behavior as one positive-weight factor approaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(j\), weights \(\alpha_i>0\) with \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and positive coordinates \(x_i\) for \(i\ne j\). Writing \(C=\prod_{i\ne j}x_i^{\alpha_i}>0\), the weighted geometric mean satisfies \(g_\alpha(x)=C x_j^{\alpha_j}\). Therefore \(g_\alpha(x)\to0\) as \(x_j\downarrow0\), with exact order \(x_j^{\alpha_j}\). On the positive orthant, \(\partial g_\alpha/\partial x_j=\alpha_j Cx_j^{\alpha_j-1}\); this derivative diverges when \(0<\alpha_j<1\), remains constant when \(\alpha_j=1\), and never has a finite boundary derivative in the multi-factor positive-weight case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing factor drives the mean to zero at its weight’s power; for a genuine multi-factor mean, the corresponding derivative blows up.

notation.meaning: product of the fixed nonvanishing factors with their weights

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic and derivative formulas are consistent for a genuine multi-factor positive-weight mean, but they lack cited support.

children.title: Boundary Weight Regimes
children.top_down_role: Domain effects associated with limiting or degenerate exponent weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Weight Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension to zero weights and the exceptional joint limit at a zero factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) with \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), define the closed-simplex extension \(g_\alpha(x)=\prod_{i:\alpha_i>0}x_i^{\alpha_i}\) on \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\). A coordinate with \(\alpha_i=0\) is omitted and therefore does not affect the value. For fixed \(x_i>0\), \(x_i^{\alpha_i}\to1\) as \(\alpha_i\downarrow0\). This extension is not jointly continuous at \((\alpha_i,x_i)=(0,0)\): along \(x_i=0\) and \(\alpha_i>0\), the factor equals zero, while at \(\alpha_i=0\) the omitted factor equals one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-weight coordinates are ignored, but weight and factor cannot jointly approach zero continuously under the usual omitted-factor convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_i=0\) removes coordinate \(i\), but the resulting extension is discontinuous at \((\alpha_i,x_i)=(0,0)\).

notation.meaning: closed-simplex weighted geometric mean under the omitted-factor convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the omitted-factor convention and asserted joint discontinuity require a source.

children.title: Support-Pattern Consequences
children.top_down_role: Dependence of geometric-mean behavior on the locations of active factors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypograph reduction induced by the support of the weight vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{i:\alpha_i>0\}\) and \(g_\alpha(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i^{\alpha_i}\). Over \(\mathbb R_+^m\), \(\operatorname{hypo}g_\alpha=\{(x,t):(x_S,t)\in\operatorname{hypo}g_{\alpha_S},\ x_{S^c}\in\mathbb R_+^{S^c}\}\). Thus unsupported coordinates are free nonnegative cylinder directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted-geometric-mean hypograph is a cylinder over the lower-dimensional hypograph on positively weighted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Reduced Hypograph Cylinder
Support-Pattern Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of the geometric mean’s zero set on the support of its weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) satisfy \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), set \(S=\{i:\alpha_i>0\}\), and use \(g_\alpha(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i^{\alpha_i}\) for \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Then \(g_\alpha(x)>0\) if and only if \(x_i>0\) for every \(i\in S\), and \(g_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if some supported coordinate vanishes. Coordinates outside \(S\) neither affect the value nor generate a zero boundary. Thus the active boundary faces of the geometric-mean hypograph are determined exactly by the weight-support pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only coordinates with positive weights matter: the mean is positive exactly when every supported factor is positive.

notation.meaning: weighted geometric mean over supported coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-based zero-set characterization is mathematically coherent and locally appropriate, but it has no cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines semidefinite representability through affine LMI lifts and records its immediate consequences for sublevel sets and convex-program reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is semidefinite representable (SDr) if there exist \(k,m\) and an affine map \(L:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{S}^m\) such that \[x\in X\iff \exists u\in\mathbb{R}^k:\ L(x,u)\succeq0.\] Thus \(X\) is the projection onto the \(x\)-space of an LMI feasible set. A convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is SDr if and only if its epigraph is SDr. Consequently, every sublevel set \(\{x:f(x)\le a\}\) of an SDr function is SDr. If every \(X_i\) in \(\min\{c^Tx:x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^mX_i\}\) has a known semidefinite representation, the problem admits an explicit semidefinite-program formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex set is semidefinite representable when membership is equivalent to the existence of auxiliary variables satisfying an affine linear matrix inequality, so the set is a projection of an LMI feasible set. A convex extended-real function is semidefinite representable when its epigraph is. Its sublevel sets are then semidefinite representable, and a linear-objective problem whose constraint sets have known such representations can be converted explicitly to an SDP.
assumptions_latex: L(x,u)\text{ is affine and takes values in }\mathbb{S}^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in X\iff\exists u:L(x,u)\succeq0,\qquad f\text{ is SDr}\iff\operatorname{epi}f\text{ is SDr}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence for a symmetric block matrix when its leading diagonal block is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[A=\begin{pmatrix}B&C^T\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{S}^{k+l},\qquad B\in\mathbb{S}^k,\quad D\in\mathbb{S}^l,\] and assume \(B\succ0\). Then \[A\succ0\iff D-CB^{-1}C^T\succ0,\qquad A\succeq0\iff D-CB^{-1}C^T\succeq0.\] The matrix \(D-CB^{-1}C^T\) is the Schur complement of \(B\) in \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric block matrix with a positive-definite leading block B, the full matrix is positive definite, respectively positive semidefinite, exactly when D minus C B inverse C transpose has the corresponding property. This latter matrix is the Schur complement of B.

children.title: Affine Matrix-Inequality Models
children.top_down_role: Direct PSD-cone representations of affine symmetric-matrix constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Matrix-Inequality Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct positive-semidefinite-cone representation of an affine symmetric-matrix inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_n\in\mathbb{S}^p\), and define the affine symmetric-matrix map \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iF_i\). The linear matrix inequality \(F(x)\succeq0\) is exactly the cone-membership constraint \(F(x)\in\mathbb{S}_+^p\). Consequently, a model with affine scalar equalities and one or more such inequalities is a conic linear program over a Cartesian product of positive-semidefinite cones. No lifting is required beyond introducing a matrix slack \(S=F(x)\) when the solver interface separates affine equations from cone membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine symmetric-matrix inequality is directly a positive-semidefinite-cone constraint, optionally connected to a matrix slack by affine equations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-Form Characterization of an Affine LMI
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent scalar family characterizing direct PSD membership of an affine symmetric pencil.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For F(x)=F_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iF_i\in\mathbb S^p, \quad F(x)\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow y^{\mathsf T}F(x)y\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in\mathbb R^p. Thus an affine LMI compactly represents an infinite family of affine inequalities in x indexed by y.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine symmetric pencil is positive semidefinite exactly when all its quadratic forms are nonnegative.

children.title: Schur-Complement Lift Families
children.top_down_role: Matrix-block lift families connecting quadratic, inverse, and norm structures to PSD domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Lift Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite Schur-complement equivalence underlying quadratic and matrix-fractional lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^p\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), and \(C\in\mathbb{S}^q\). The Schur-complement identity gives \[\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C-B^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}B\succeq0.\] In particular, for \(Q\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^p\), the quadratic epigraph \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}x\) is represented exactly by \[\begin{pmatrix}Q&x\\x^{\mathsf T}&t\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Thus inverse-quadratic and matrix-fractional inequalities admit affine positive-semidefinite lifts whenever the leading block is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite leading block converts a block PSD constraint into its Schur complement, yielding exact semidefinite lifts of inverse-quadratic inequalities.

notation.meaning: inverse of the positive-definite leading block

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Norm Cone Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cone epigraphs for spectral, nuclear, and Frobenius matrix norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the spectral-norm epigraph has the semidefinite representation \[\|X\|_2\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\begin{pmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] The nuclear norm satisfies \[\|X\|_* =\min_{U,V}\left\{\tfrac12(\operatorname{tr}U+\operatorname{tr}V):\begin{pmatrix}U&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&V\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] Finally, \(\|X\|_F\le t\) is the second-order-cone constraint \((t,\operatorname{vec}X)\in\mathcal Q_{mn+1}\). These formulations distinguish direct second-order-cone modeling from positive-semidefinite lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral and nuclear matrix norms have exact PSD formulations, while the Frobenius norm is directly second-order-cone representable after vectorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed PSD and second-order-cone systems represent the respective norm epigraphs exactly.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.7 Convex matrix functions p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral–Nuclear Norm Duality and Equality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual support representations and an equality certificate for spectral–nuclear pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}, \quad \|X\|_*=\max_{\|Y\|_2\le1}\langle Y,X\rangle,\qquad \|X\|_2=\max_{\|Y\|_*\le1}\langle Y,X\rangle. Consequently \langle Y,X\rangle\le\|X\|_*\|Y\|_2. If X\ne0 has compact singular-value decomposition X=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}, then Y=UV^{\mathsf T} has \|Y\|_2=1 and \langle Y,X\rangle=\|X\|_*. For X=0, Y=0 is an equality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral and nuclear norms are dual, and singular vectors provide an exact support-function certificate.

notation.meaning: compact singular-value decomposition of a nonzero X

\langle X,Y\rangle_F=\sum_{i,j=1}^n X^{(i,j)}Y^{(i,j)},
