children.top_down_role: Closure failures underlying duality gaps, nonattainment, and weak infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Description of the Image Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar characterization of a conic image closure without asserting which optimization pathology occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone and \(T:E\to Y\) be linear. Then \[(T(K))^*=\{y\in Y:T^*y\in K^*\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}T(K)=\{z\in Y:\langle y,z\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\text{ with }T^*y\in K^*\}.\] Thus a point of \(\operatorname{cl}T(K)\setminus T(K)\) satisfies every non-strict dual inequality valid on the image but has no exact conic preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closure of a conic image is the bipolar determined by adjoint-feasible dual vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone and \(T:E\to Y\) is linear.

notation.meaning: Positive dual cone of a cone C

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Description of the Image Closure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Major cone-class boundary excluding nonclosed linear images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is a finite-dimensional polyhedral convex cone and \(T\) is linear, then \(T(K)\) is a polyhedral cone and is closed. Hence a nonclosed linear image of a closed cone requires a nonpolyhedral source cone and cannot occur for ordinary finite-dimensional linear-programming cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear images of polyhedral cones are polyhedral and closed.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional polyhedral convex cone.

notation.meaning: Linear image of the cone K

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Closed-Image Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trivial Cone-Kernel Intersection Ensures a Closed Image
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition excluding the nonclosed linear-image regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and let \(T:E\to Y\) be linear. If \[K\cap\ker T=\{0\},\] then \(T(K)\) is closed. Consequently, every nonclosed image has a nonzero source-cone direction annihilated by \(T\), although the existence of such a direction alone does not imply nonclosedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed cone has a closed linear image when the map annihilates no nonzero cone direction; nonclosedness therefore requires, but is not guaranteed by, a nontrivial cone-kernel intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.

notation.meaning: kernel of the linear map T

knowledge_statements.title: Trivial Cone-Kernel Intersection Ensures a Closed Image

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Infeasibility and Failure of Strict Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility-image characterization under a fixed positive-dual convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A:E\to Y\) be linear, and consider \(Ax=b,\ x\in K\). Then \[b\in\operatorname{cl}A(K)\setminus A(K)\] if and only if the system is infeasible and there is no \(y\in Y\) satisfying \[A^*y\in K^*,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle<0.\] In this regime \(\operatorname{dist}(b,A(K))=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic equality system is weakly infeasible exactly when its right-hand side is an unattained image limit, equivalently when it is infeasible at zero distance and has no strict classical separating certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\in\operatorname{cl}A(K)\setminus A(K)\iff \bigl[b\notin A(K)\text{ and no }y\text{ has }A^*y\in K^*,\ \langle b,y\rangle<0\bigr].
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Infeasibility and Failure of Strict Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Placement condition linking a missing augmented-image boundary point to an unattained finite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, \(A:E\to Y\) linear, and \[M:=\{(Ax,\langle c,x\rangle+r):x\in K,\ r\in\mathbb R_+\}.\] For \(v(b):=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\in\mathbb R\), one has \((b,v(b))\in\operatorname{cl}M\), and the infimum is attained if and only if \((b,v(b))\in M\). Thus nonattainment occurs exactly when this lower boundary point belongs to \(\operatorname{cl}M\setminus M\); nonclosedness elsewhere does not imply nonattainment at \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite conic infimum is unattained exactly when its lower boundary point is a missing limit point of the feasibility-objective image.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Image Criterion for Value Attainment

assumptions_latex: The space is finite-dimensional, \(K\) is a closed convex cone, and \(A\) is linear.
The relevant projected conic set is formed by a linear image of \(K\) or an associated epigraphical cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonclosed image contains convergent sequences whose limits lack conic preimages; this closure defect is the geometric mechanism permitting unattained values and limiting feasibility without exact feasibility.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear images of closed convex cones need not be closed, and missing limit points obstruct exact certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Focuses on closure defects in projected cones, without asserting that every defect produces every pathology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \(K\) is closed, its linear image \(T(K)\) need not be closed. The nonclosed linear-image regime occurs when \[T(K)\subsetneq\operatorname{cl}T(K),\] equivalently when some sequence \((x_k)\subset K\) satisfies \(Tx_k\to z\) for a point \(z\notin T(K)\). Such a point is representable only as a limit of conic images, not by an exact conic preimage. When the image encodes feasibility or an objective epigraph, this closure defect can underlie nonattainment, weak infeasibility, or a duality gap; additional placement conditions are needed to determine which pathology occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed cone may have a nonclosed linear image, leaving limit points without exact conic preimages and enabling nonattainment, weak infeasibility, or gaps.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Linear-Image Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of a nonclosed linear image is correct, but the stated links to nonattainment, weak infeasibility, and duality gaps require a source specifying the relevant image constructions and placement conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Nonclosed Image of the Positive-Semidefinite Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete projection example whose canonical home is the projection-closedness leaf rather than this abstract regime leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(T:\mathbb S^2\to\mathbb R^2\) by \(T([\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{smallmatrix}])=(a,b)\). Then \(T(\mathbb S_+^2)=\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\), which is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a two-by-two positive-semidefinite matrix to its first diagonal and off-diagonal entries gives a nonclosed cone.

notation.meaning: coordinate projection retaining the first diagonal and off-diagonal entries

knowledge_statements.title: A Nonclosed Image of the Positive-Semidefinite Cone

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Primal-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional strong infeasibility for the conic system \(Ax=b,\ x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal conic system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), is strongly infeasible precisely when \(b\notin\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\), equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(b,A(K))>0\). A strong primal-infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\in Y\) satisfying \[A^*y\in K^*,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle<0.\] Such a certificate establishes that the primal system has no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong primal infeasibility is equivalent to positive separation of b from A(K), witnessed by a dual vector whose adjoint image is cone-dual feasible and whose pairing with b is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(b\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(b,A(K))>0\) if and only if such a certificate exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Certificate Validation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact independent validation; floating-point acceptance requires separately justified error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reported vector \(y\in Y\), an exact primal-infeasibility validator independently recomputes and accepts exactly when \[A^*y\in K^*\qquad\text{and}\qquad \langle b,y\rangle<0.\] Acceptance certifies that the primal system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), is infeasible. Failure of either test means only that the reported vector is not a valid certificate; it does not establish feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The validator recomputes dual-cone membership and the strictly negative pairing. Passing proves primal infeasibility; failing merely rejects the submitted certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(b\in Y\).
The validator can recompute \(A^*y\), \(\langle b,y\rangle\), and membership in \(K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies that \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), has no solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Breakdown under Weak Primal Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of strict finite separation at weak primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak primal infeasibility is the regime \[b\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(b,A(K))=0.\] In this regime no \(y\in Y\) satisfies both \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\). Thus the ordinary strong primal-infeasibility certificate system is not exhaustive when the conic image is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At weak primal infeasibility, b is unattainable but arbitrarily approximable from A(K), and no strictly separating finite certificate exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(b\in Y\).
The primal system is infeasible and \(\operatorname{dist}(b,A(K))=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No ordinary vector \(y\) satisfies \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal semidefinite example of an unattained right-hand side in the closure of a conic image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\), \(A:\mathbb S^2\to\mathbb R^2\) satisfy \(A(X)=(X_{11},X_{12})\), and let \(b=(0,1)\). The system \(A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\), is infeasible. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[X_\varepsilon=\begin{pmatrix}\varepsilon&1\\1&\varepsilon^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad A(X_\varepsilon)=(\varepsilon,1)\to b.\] Therefore \(b\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PSD constraints X11=0 and X12=1 are inconsistent, although PSD matrices can approach them arbitrarily closely.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^2\) carries the trace inner product.
Matrix coordinates use the standard symmetric-matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\notin A(K)\), \(\operatorname{dist}(b,A(K))=0\), and no ordinary strict primal-infeasibility separator exists.

notation.meaning: Cone of real two-by-two positive-semidefinite matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Dual-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional strong infeasibility for \(A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*\). The dual conic system \(A^*y+s=c\), \(s\in K^*\), is strongly infeasible precisely when \(c\notin\operatorname{cl}(D)\), equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(c,D)>0\). A strong dual-infeasibility certificate is a vector \(x\in X\) satisfying \[x\in K,\qquad Ax=0,\qquad \langle c,x\rangle<0.\] Such a certificate establishes that the dual system has no feasible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong dual infeasibility is positive separation of c from the dual feasible image, witnessed by a conic null-space direction having negative cost pairing.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(c\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(c,\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)>0\) if and only if such a certificate exists.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner-product-norm quantitative form of the strong dual-infeasibility certificate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*\), with norm induced by the fixed inner product. Then \[\operatorname{dist}(c,D)=\max\{-\langle c,x\rangle:x\in K,\ Ax=0,\ \|x\|\le1\}.\] Hence strong dual infeasibility holds exactly when this maximum is positive; a unit-norm maximizer realizes the separation distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to the dual feasibility image equals the largest negative cost margin of a unit conic null-space direction.

\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance-Based Validation Is Not an Exact Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact independent validation and solver tolerance diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditions \(\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\le\varepsilon_K\), \(\|Ax\|\le\varepsilon_A\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle\le-\varepsilon_c\) with positive tolerances do not alone imply the existence of \(\bar x\in K\cap\ker A\) satisfying \(\langle c,\bar x\rangle<0\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At weak dual infeasibility, c lies outside but arbitrarily near the dual feasible image, and no strictly separating recession certificate exists.

\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(c\in X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal semidefinite realization of zero-distance dual infeasibility without an ordinary recession certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb S^2\), \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\), \(Y=\mathbb R\), \(A(X)=X_{22}\), and \(c=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(A^*y=yE_{22}\), and \(yE_{22}+S=c,\ S\succeq0\), is infeasible. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[S_\varepsilon=\begin{pmatrix}\varepsilon&1\\1&\varepsilon^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad y_\varepsilon=-\varepsilon^{-1},\qquad y_\varepsilon E_{22}+S_\varepsilon\to c.\] Thus \(c\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)\setminus(\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)\). Every \(Z\succeq0\) satisfying \(AZ=Z_{22}=0\) also satisfies \(Z_{12}=0\) and \(\langle c,Z\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This two-by-two dual SDP is infeasible but arbitrarily approximable, while every conic null-space direction has zero cost pairing.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^2\) carries the trace inner product.
\(E_{22}\) has its sole nonzero entry in position \((2,2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual system is weakly infeasible and admits no \(Z\succeq0\) with \(AZ=0\) and \(\langle c,Z\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Two-by-Two Weakly Dual-Infeasible Semidefinite System

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A product-semidefinite example showing that paired status (1,1) is attainable.

Set \(b=(0,1,0)\) and \(c=(0,C)\), where \(C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(b\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K)\) and \(c\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)\setminus(\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)\). Hence this standard primal-dual pair has paired status \((w_P,w_D)=(1,1)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status pair for the standard equality-form primal and affine-plus-dual-cone dual feasibility systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic primal-dual pair \(Ax=b,\ x\in K\) and \(A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\), define \(w_P=1\) exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K)\), and define \(w_D=1\) exactly when \(c\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)\setminus(\operatorname{range}(A^*)+K^*)\). The paired weak-infeasibility status is \((w_P,w_D)\in\{0,1\}^2\); the status \((1,1)\) means that both declared feasibility systems are weakly infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The paired status records separately whether the primal and dual feasibility systems are infeasible boundary points of their respective conic images.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
The primal feasibility system is \(P=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\), and the dual alternative system is \(D=\{y:A^*y\in K^*,\ \langle b,y\rangle=-1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is weakly infeasible exactly when \(P=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(K,\{x:Ax=b\})=0\); equivalently, no \(y\in D\) exists although arbitrarily small primal feasibility residuals occur. The paired dual regime is obtained by interchanging the primal affine-conic system with its dual affine-conic system. Hence primal and dual weak infeasibility are separate regimes: either side, or in pathological conic pairs both sides, may lack feasibility while remaining at zero distance from its corresponding constraint set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\{x\in E:Ax=b\}\). The primal system is weakly infeasible when \(K\cap L=\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(K,L)=0\). Its normalized strong-infeasibility certificates form \(D=\{y:A^*y\in K^*,\ \langle b,y\rangle=-1\}\); weak infeasibility implies \(D=\varnothing\). Applying the same definition to the dual affine-conic feasibility system gives weak dual infeasibility. These predicates are logically distinct, and a paired weak-infeasibility regime records which of the primal and dual systems satisfies its weak-infeasibility predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A paired regime records whether the primal system, the dual system, or both are infeasible but have zero distance from their respective affine and conic constraint sets.

children.top_down_role: Limits of ordinary infeasibility certificates in zero-distance regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, and \(P=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\) is infeasible.
A standard certificate is a vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P\) is weakly infeasible, then no standard certificate exists. Thus any procedure whose infeasibility outcome requires such a vector cannot certify weak infeasibility, even with exact arithmetic; it must return an unresolved outcome or use an augmented construction such as facial reduction or an extended dual.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(y\) with \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\) strictly separates \(K\) from \(\{x:Ax=b\}\), so its existence implies \(\operatorname{dist}(K,\{x:Ax=b\})>0\). Consequently, when \(P=\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(K,\{x:Ax=b\})=0\), no such vector exists. Standard strict-separation certificates therefore detect strong infeasibility but cannot certify weak infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard strict-separation certificate detects positive-distance infeasibility. Weakly infeasible systems have zero distance, so no certificate of that standard form can exist.

children.title: Minimal-Face Geometry
children.top_down_role: Facial location of the feasible region within the ambient cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal face of a nonempty finite-dimensional conic feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=K\cap L\neq\varnothing\), define the minimal face containing the feasible set by \[F_{\min}:=\bigcap\{F:F\unlhd K,\ S\subseteq F\}.\] In finite dimensions, \(F_{\min}\) is a face of \(K\), is contained in every face of \(K\) containing \(S\), and satisfies \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}(F_{\min})\neq\varnothing\). Thus the same affine constraints are relatively strictly feasible over \(F_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face is the unique smallest face of the cone containing every feasible point; the feasible set meets that face's relative interior.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and \(S=K\cap L\neq\varnothing\), where \(L\subseteq E\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a unique face \(F_{\min}\) of \(K\) satisfying \(S\subseteq F_{\min}\) and \(F_{\min}\subseteq F\) for every face \(F\unlhd K\) containing \(S\). Moreover, \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}(F_{\min})\neq\varnothing\), so replacing \(K\) by \(F_{\min}\) restores relative strict feasibility.

notation.meaning: Closed convex cone and affine constraint set.
Minimal face of the cone containing the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent pointwise characterization of the minimal face containing a nonempty convex subset of a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, let \(S\subseteq K\) be nonempty and convex, and choose \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}S\). If \(\operatorname{face}_K(\bar x)\) is the smallest face of \(K\) containing \(\bar x\), then \[F_{\min}(S)=\operatorname{face}_K(\bar x).\] Thus every point in \(\operatorname{ri}S\) generates the same face of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every relative-interior point of a nonempty convex feasible set generates exactly its minimal containing cone face.

\(S\subseteq K\) is nonempty and convex, and \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}S\).

children.title: Singularity-Degree Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Singularity-Degree Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity degree counted by proper exposing steps in finite-dimensional facial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A facial-reduction chain is \(F_0=K\) and \(F_i=F_{i-1}\cap z_i^{\perp}\), where \(z_i\in F_{i-1}^*\), \(S\subseteq z_i^{\perp}\), and \(F_i\subsetneq F_{i-1}\). The singularity degree is \[d(S,K):=\min\{d:F_d=F_{\min}\}.\] Accordingly, \(d=0\) exactly when \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}(K)\neq\varnothing\); \(d=1\) means one exposing reduction suffices; and \(d\geq 2\) means no single valid exposing vector reaches \(F_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singularity degree is the shortest number of proper exposing reductions needed to reach the feasible system's minimal face; zero is relative strict feasibility in the original cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and the nonempty feasible system \(S=K\cap L\) has minimal face \(F_{\min}\).
Each reduction step replaces the current face by its intersection with an exposing hyperplane valid for \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The singularity degree \(d(S,K)\) is the minimum number of proper facial-reduction steps needed to reach \(F_{\min}\). The regime \(d=0\) is strict feasibility relative to \(K\), \(d=1\) is one-step exposure of the minimal face, and \(d\geq 2\) requires a sequential exposing chain.

notation.meaning: Minimal face containing the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Chain Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial bounds on proper facial-reduction steps; \(\ell(K)\) counts faces, including endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell(K)\) be the largest number of faces in any strictly descending chain beginning at \(K\). Because every facial-reduction step produces a strict face inclusion, \[d(S,K)\leq \ell(K)-1.\] Since every proper inclusion in a chain from \(K\) to \(F_{\min}\) decreases dimension by at least one, one also has \[d(S,K)\leq \dim K-\dim F_{\min}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial-reduction complexity is bounded both by the longest strict face chain of the cone and by the dimension drop from the original cone to the minimal face.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and facial-reduction chains use only strict face inclusions.
\(S\) is a nonempty conic feasible set with minimal face \(F_{\min}\), singularity degree \(d(S,K)\), and finite maximum face-chain length \(\ell(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The singularity degree satisfies \[d(S,K)\leq \ell(K)-1\] and \[d(S,K)\leq \dim K-\dim F_{\min}.\]

notation.meaning: Maximum number of faces in a strictly descending face chain beginning at the cone.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the minimal face \(F_{\min}\) is nonexposed in \(K\), no single first-stage certificate \(z\in K^*\) can satisfy \(F_{\min}=K\cap z^{\perp}\). Consequently one-step facial reduction cannot recover \(F_{\min}\); a chain through intermediate faces, or a richer lifting, is necessary.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A face \(F\unlhd K\) is exposed if there is \(z\in K^*\) such that \(F=K\cap z^{\perp}\). If \(F_{\min}\) is not exposed in \(K\), then no single certificate from \(K^*\) identifies it directly. Thus every facial-reduction construction reaching \(F_{\min}\) must either use multiple reductions in successively smaller faces or replace the original representation by a lifting in which the relevant face becomes exposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexposed minimal face cannot be identified by one dual hyperplane. Recovering it requires sequential reductions or a richer lifted representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete finite-dimensional obstruction to identifying every cone face by one ambient dual hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2\le 1\}\), \(C=\operatorname{conv}(D\cup\{(2,0)\})\), and \[K=\operatorname{cone}\{(x,y,1):(x,y)\in C\}\subseteq\mathbb R^3.\] For \(p=(1/2,\sqrt3/2)\), the ray \[R=\operatorname{cone}\{(p,1)\}\] is an extreme ray of the closed cone \(K\), but it is nonexposed: \[\nexists z\in K^*\quad R=K\cap z^\perp.\]

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\unlhd K\quad\text{and}\quad\nexists z\in K^*:\ R=K\cap z^\perp.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(F_0:=K\). At iteration \(i\), if \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}(F_i)\neq\varnothing\), stop and output \(F_i\). The branch \(\tau=0\) represents homogeneous directions and may encode infeasibility or unboundedness certificates when the construction's certificate scalar is strictly positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outcome interface for homogeneous self-dual embeddings; the skew-adjoint operator and sign convention may vary by construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:E\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(K\subseteq E\), \(x,s\in E\), and \(y,r\in\mathbb{R}^m\). A homogeneous self-dual embedding uses \(u=(x,y,\tau)\) and \(v=(s,r,\kappa)\) satisfying \[v=Qu,\qquad u\in K\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}_+,\qquad v\in K^*\times\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}_+,\] where \(Q^*=-Q\) encodes \((A,b,c)\). The branch \(\tau>0\) permits normalization to the original primal-dual pair. The branch \(\kappa>0\) represents homogeneous alternative directions and yields standard infeasibility certificates when the corresponding strict sign condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous self-dual embedding places normalized solutions and homogeneous alternative directions in one skew-adjoint conic feasibility system and distinguishes their outcomes using two nonnegative scalar coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, and \(A:E\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in E\) are the primal-dual data.
\(Q:E\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}\to E\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}\) is a skew-adjoint linear operator encoding \((A,b,c)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every exact embedded solution belongs to one conic feasibility system. If \(\tau>0\), normalization recovers a primal-dual feasible pair and the embedding complementarity yields optimality. If \(\kappa>0\), the homogeneous identities yield a primal- or dual-infeasibility certificate when the required strict separation sign holds.

notation.meaning: Primal variable and dual slack in the Euclidean space.
Dual multiplier and embedding residual in \(\mathbb{R}^m\), with \(r=0\) at feasibility.
Primal cone and its dual cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Solution Embedding Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-normalization outcome of a homogeneous self-dual embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an embedded solution has \(\tau>0\), \(\kappa=0\), \(Ax=b\tau\), and \(A^*y+s=c\tau\), with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle\). Define \[(\bar x,\bar y,\bar s):=(x,y,s)/\tau.\] Then \(A\bar x=b\), \(A^*\bar y+\bar s=c\), \(\bar x\in K\), \(\bar s\in K^*\), and \(\langle c,\bar x\rangle=\langle b,\bar y\rangle\). Thus \(\bar x\) and \((\bar y,\bar s)\) are primal and dual optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive embedding normalization scales the embedded variables into primal and dual feasible points; equality of their objective values certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:E\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in E\).
The primal problem is \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), and the dual problem is \(\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\).
An exact homogeneous self-dual embedding solution satisfies \(\tau>0\), \(\kappa=0\), and the displayed scaled feasibility and zero-gap identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized variables \(\bar x=x/\tau\), \(\bar y=y/\tau\), and \(\bar s=s/\tau\) are primal and dual feasible and have equal objective values; consequently they are optimal.

notation.meaning: Normalized primal variable, dual multiplier, and dual slack.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Certificate Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard strong-primal-infeasibility outcome recovered from an exact embedding solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal conic system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying \[A^*y\in K^*,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle<0.\] Its existence certifies that the primal system is infeasible. Because the inequality is strict, the certificate can be normalized so that \(\langle b,y\rangle=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An embedding certifies primal infeasibility by producing a dual-cone separator whose pairing with the right-hand side is strictly negative; the separator can be normalized to have pairing minus one.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:E\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The primal conic feasibility system is \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\).
An embedding outcome supplies \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(y\) is a directly verifiable certificate of primal infeasibility and can be rescaled to satisfy \(\langle b,y\rangle=-1\).

notation.meaning: Closed primal cone and dual cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and let \(A:X\to Y\), \(b\in Y\), and \(c\in X\). Consider the primal problem \[\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in X,\ Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\] and its dual \[\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:(y,s)\in Y\times K^*,\ A^*y+s=c\}.\] A vector \(d\in X\) is a dual-infeasibility certificate if \(d\in K\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\). An embedding outcome producing a positive multiple of such a vector certifies that the dual feasible set is empty. If the primal is feasible at \(x_0\), then \(x_0+td\) is primal feasible for every \(t\geq0\), and \(\langle c,x_0+td\rangle\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-cone direction annihilated by the constraints and having negative objective pairing certifies dual infeasibility; if the primal is feasible, the same direction proves primal unboundedness.

children.title: Outcome Normalization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scaling regimes governing extraction of solutions or certificates from embeddings.

knowledge_statements.title: Outcome Normalization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale normalization for nonzero outcomes of a positively homogeneous certificate-producing embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\neq0\) solve a positively homogeneous embedding, so every \(\alpha z\) with \(\alpha>0\) represents the same outcome ray. If a nonnegative scalar functional \(h(z)\) satisfies \(h(z)>0\), the ray has the unique normalized representative
\[\widehat z=\frac{z}{h(z)},\qquad h(\widehat z)=1.\]
For an embedding with nonnegative status coordinates \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\), the common choice \(h(z)=\tau+\kappa\) separates normalized solution outcomes with \(\widehat\tau>0\) from normalized certificate outcomes with \(\widehat\kappa>0\). If \(\tau+\kappa=0\), this normalization is undefined and no normalized status may be assigned by this rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous outcome ray may be scaled uniquely when its normalization functional is positive; zero normalization mass marks a degenerate outcome outside this regime.
assumptions_latex: The embedding equations and cone constraints are positively homogeneous in \(z\).
\(h\) is positive on the outcome ray being normalized.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative solution and certificate status coordinates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the leaf, but uniqueness of z/h(z) requires explicit positive degree-one homogeneity of h, not merely positivity on the ray. The claimed separation by tau and kappa also needs embedding-specific assumptions, such as mutually exclusive exact status regimes. No source is supplied for those conventions.

children.title: Degenerate Embedding Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Embedding solutions whose scaling or facial position obstructs direct recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Embedding Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy boundary for homogeneous embeddings using solution and certificate status coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\neq0\) satisfy a homogeneous embedding with nonnegative status coordinates \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\). The outcome is degenerate when
\[\tau=0,\qquad \kappa=0.\]
Then neither division by \(\tau\) can recover a primal-dual solution nor division by \(\kappa\) can recover a normalized infeasibility certificate. Consequently, feasibility of the embedding alone does not justify an optimal, primal-infeasible, or dual-infeasible status. Any status requires additional analysis of the remaining coordinates, the minimal faces they occupy, or a separately verified certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both embedding status coordinates vanish, neither a solution nor an infeasibility certificate can be normalized, so no standard terminal status follows.
assumptions_latex: The embedding interprets \(\tau>0\) as a solution regime and \(\kappa>0\) as a certificate regime.
The returned embedding vector \(z\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau=\kappa=0\Longrightarrow\) the standard solution and certificate recovery maps are both undefined.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits. The recovery-map conclusion is plausible for a homogeneous embedding with the stated tau and kappa convention, but that convention and the asserted need for facial or auxiliary analysis are embedding-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Indeterminate Embedding Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Embedding outcomes that do not support a unique mathematical status.

knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate Embedding Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical outcome boundary when an embedding iterate supports no validated terminal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an embedding output \(z\) and declared tolerances, call the outcome indeterminate if it satisfies none of the validated predicates for approximate optimality, primal infeasibility, or dual infeasibility. Equivalently, either its embedding residual exceeds the acceptance tolerance, its normalization denominator is too small, or every recovered candidate violates at least one required feasibility, gap, sign, or cone-membership test. An indeterminate outcome asserts only that the current computation produced no accepted certificate; it does not imply that the original primal or dual problem is feasible, infeasible, bounded, or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no solution or infeasibility predicate passes its numerical checks, the result is indeterminate and makes no mathematical claim about the original problem.
assumptions_latex: All terminal predicates and numerical tolerances are fixed before classifying \(z\).
Cone-membership and residual tests are evaluated in a declared scaling.

notation.meaning: Validated optimality and infeasibility acceptance predicates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the claimed equivalence between failure of all terminal predicates and the listed residual, denominator, and candidate-test failures is valid only after those predicates are defined exhaustively. The solver-specific tolerances, scaling, and status semantics require an inspectable interface or solver-standard source.

children.title: Facial-Analysis Requirements
children.top_down_role: Outcome classes requiring additional facial classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Analysis Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition triggering minimal-face analysis when strict conic feasibility fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic feasible set \(S=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\), facial analysis is required when \(S\neq\varnothing\) but \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\). Let \(F_{\min}\) be the intersection of all faces of \(K\) containing \(S\). Then \(F_{\min}\) is the unique minimal face containing every feasible point, and the appropriate reduced representation replaces \(x\in K\) by \(x\in F_{\min}\). Status conclusions that rely on strict feasibility or interior normalization must remain qualified until this face is identified or an independent exact certificate is verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible system with no point in the relative interior of its cone requires analysis on the unique minimal face containing its feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\Longrightarrow F_{\min}\subsetneq K\) and the facially reduced constraint is \(x\in F_{\min}\).

notation.meaning: Minimal face of K containing the feasible set.

children.title: Qualified Status Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on reliable status interpretation for degenerate embeddings.

knowledge_statements.title: Qualified Status Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between mathematically certified statuses and tolerance-qualified solver reports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A terminal conic status is unqualified only when an exact primal-dual solution or an exact infeasibility certificate satisfies its defining equalities, cone memberships, and strict sign condition. If these relations hold only within positive tolerances, or depend on an unverified normalization, scaling, or facial reduction, the status must be explicitly qualified as approximate. If no declared tolerance makes all required predicates hold simultaneously, the outcome is indeterminate rather than optimal or infeasible. Thus a small embedding residual alone is insufficient to cross the boundary into an unqualified mathematical status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact verified predicates support unqualified statuses; tolerance-based predicates support only approximate statuses, and failed predicates require an indeterminate report.
assumptions_latex: Exact and approximate acceptance predicates are declared separately.
All residuals use fixed norms and data scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{exact}}\Rightarrow S_{\mathrm{exact}}\), while \(P_{\varepsilon}\land\neg P_{\mathrm{exact}}\Rightarrow S_{\mathrm{approx}}\); failure of both predicates forbids either status.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the distinction between unqualified, approximate, and indeterminate statuses is an interface contract rather than a universal conic theorem. The predicates and the claim that failure forces an indeterminate status require an authoritative solver-status source.

For the primal-dual pair \[\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in X,\ Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad \sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:(y,s)\in Y\times K^*,\ A^*y+s=c\},\] an exact optimal status is certified by \((x,y,s)\in X\times Y\times X\) satisfying \[Ax=b,\quad x\in K,\quad A^*y+s=c,\quad s\in K^*,\quad \langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle=0.\] These relations certify that \(x\) is primal optimal and \((y,s)\) is dual optimal with common finite objective value \(\langle c,x\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle\).

children.title: Approximate-Optimal Status

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-qualified solver status under a fully declared primal-dual accuracy predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared finite-dimensional conic primal-dual formulation and a declared accuracy predicate \(Q\) containing primal-equation, primal-cone, dual-equation, dual-cone, and objective-gap tests, a returned tuple \((x,y,s)\) has approximate-optimal status when \(Q(x,y,s)\) holds. This status certifies satisfaction of those declared numerical tests only. Unless the corresponding residuals and cone violations vanish and the gap is exactly zero, it does not by itself assert exact feasibility or exact mathematical optimality.

children.title: Accuracy-Qualification Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Tolerance regimes separating exact-status reporting from qualified reporting.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface-independent structure of an accuracy policy without imposing a particular solver's normalization formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An accuracy-qualification policy for a returned primal-dual tuple \(z\) consists of declared nonnegative measures \(\rho_p(z),\rho_d(z),\rho_K(z),\rho_{K^*}(z),\rho_g(z)\), declared tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_K,\tau_{K^*},\tau_g\), and the norms, data scaling, and normalization rules used to compute them. The tuple passes exactly when every declared inequality \[\rho_p\le\tau_p,\quad\rho_d\le\tau_d,\quad\rho_K\le\tau_K,\quad\rho_{K^*}\le\tau_{K^*},\quad\rho_g\le\tau_g\] holds. Different norms, scalings, normalizations, or tolerances define different qualification predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accuracy qualification is a declared conjunction of primal, dual, cone, and gap tests; changing their normalization or tolerances changes the predicate.
assumptions_latex: All measures, norms, scaling rules, and tolerances are declared before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(z)=\bigwedge_{j\in\{p,d,K,K^*,g\}}[\rho_j(z)\le\tau_j],\qquad Q\text{ depends on the declared normalization and scaling}.

notation.meaning: Declared error or violation measure for component j
Declared acceptance tolerance for component j

knowledge_statements.title: Declared Accuracy-Qualification Predicate
Accuracy-Qualification Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware threshold predicate controlling qualification of an optimality report.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_p=Ax-b\), \(r_d=A^*y+s-c\), and \(g=\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle\). Given absolute and relative tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\), define
\[T(q)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,q\}.\]
An accuracy-qualified report requires
\[\|r_p\|\leq T(\max\{\|Ax\|,\|b\|\}),\quad \|r_d\|\leq T(\max\{\|A^*y+s\|,\|c\|\}),\]
\[|g|\leq T(\max\{|\langle c,x\rangle|,|\langle b,y\rangle|\}),\]
together with separately declared cone-membership thresholds. Changing norms, scaling, or thresholds changes the qualification predicate and must therefore be reported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality accuracy is qualified by absolute-plus-relative bounds for primal residual, dual residual, objective gap, and separately specified cone violations.
assumptions_latex: All norms and data scalings are fixed.
Absolute and relative tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A report is accuracy-qualified only if every declared scaled residual, gap, and cone-membership inequality is satisfied.

children.title: Optimal-Status Downgrade Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Residual or consistency issues that prevent an unqualified optimal status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary excluding exact or approximate optimal labels, without prescribing interface-specific replacement labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_{\mathrm{exact}}\) be the conjunction of exact primal feasibility, primal cone membership, dual feasibility, dual cone membership, and zero objective gap. Let \(P_{\mathrm{approx}}\) be the declared tolerance-qualified conjunction for the same formulation. If \(P_{\mathrm{exact}}\) fails, an exact optimal label is not certified. If \(P_{\mathrm{approx}}\) also fails, an approximate-optimal label is not certified. In particular, passing an objective-gap test alone cannot preserve either label when a required feasibility or cone-membership test fails. Any replacement status is determined by the originating interface and by whatever other certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure of any exact test excludes exact optimal status; failure of any required approximate test also excludes approximate-optimal status, and a small gap alone cannot override infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Both predicates refer to the same declared primal-dual formulation.
Every component required by each predicate is fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Status Downgrade Boundaries

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.

The primal constraint orientation is \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(b\in Y\). For the primal system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), a vector \(y\in Y\) certifies primal infeasibility when \[A^*y\in K^*,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle<0.\] These relations certify that \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\). An unqualified primal-infeasible status requires exact verification under this orientation; a tolerance-based version is only an approximate or qualified status and does not by itself establish exact emptiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the declared equality-form conic system, a dual-space vector whose adjoint image lies in the dual cone and whose pairing with the right-hand side is negative certifies primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Status

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(c\in X\). For the dual system \(A^*y+s=c\), \((y,s)\in Y\times K^*\), a vector \(d\in X\) certifies dual infeasibility when \[d\in K,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad \langle c,d\rangle<0.\] These relations certify that the dual feasible set is empty. This status alone does not assert primal feasibility; if some \(x_0\in K\) satisfies \(Ax_0=b\), then \(x_0+td\) is primal feasible for every \(t\geq0\) and its objective tends to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the declared equality-form dual system, a primal-cone direction annihilated by the constraints and having negative cost certifies dual infeasibility, but it does not establish primal feasibility by itself.

children.title: Certificate Orientation Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between certificate orientation and reported infeasibility status.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Orientation Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orientation for a minimization-form primal conic program and its maximization-form dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(D=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is \(u\) satisfying \(A^*u\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,u\rangle<0\). It corresponds to the dual improving recession direction \(d=-u\), since \(-A^*d\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,d\rangle>0\). A dual-infeasibility certificate is \(r\in K\) satisfying \(Ar=0\) and \(\langle c,r\rangle<0\); it is a primal improving recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate for one problem's infeasibility is oriented as an improving recession direction for the paired problem.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(A\) is linear and \(K^*=\{s:\langle s,x\rangle\ge 0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\mapsto -u\) maps primal-infeasibility certificates to dual improving directions, while \(r\) is simultaneously a dual-infeasibility certificate and primal improving direction.

children.title: Infeasibility-Status Qualification
children.top_down_role: Accuracy qualifiers attached to otherwise definitive infeasibility classifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent qualification of certificate evidence without prescribing solver-specific tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact certified-infeasible status is justified when the relevant cone membership, homogeneous linear equation, and strict sign inequality are verified exactly, or when rigorous error enclosures imply those exact predicates. Acceptance based only on positive residual tolerances or an uncertified floating-point sign test supports at most an approximate infeasibility indication. Failure to validate a submitted certificate proves neither feasibility nor weak infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tolerance-only evidence is approximate; exact predicates or rigorous bounds implying them are required for a certified infeasibility status, and certificate failure is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual certificate orientations are those of the sibling exact-status leaves.
Any claimed rigorous error bounds account for all cone, linear-equation, and strict-sign errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{exact predicates or rigorous implication}\Rightarrow\text{certified strong infeasibility},\qquad\text{tolerance-only acceptance}\not\Rightarrow\text{exact infeasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-versus-Approximate Infeasibility Status

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure-based qualification of primal and dual infeasibility according to whether an ordinary strict conic certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_P=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\) and \(F_D=\{(y,s):A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\). A certificate \(A^*u\in K^*\), \(\langle b,u\rangle<0\) exists if and only if \(b\notin\operatorname{cl}A(K)\). Thus \(b\in\operatorname{cl}A(K)\setminus A(K)\) is weak primal infeasibility and admits no certificate of that strict form. Similarly, a certificate \(d\in K\), \(Ad=0\), \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\) exists if and only if \(c\notin\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{range}A^*+K^*)\); membership in \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{range}A^*+K^*)\setminus(\operatorname{range}A^*+K^*)\) is weak dual infeasibility and admits no such strict certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong infeasibility is separated from the feasible image by a strict finite certificate; weak infeasibility lies in the image's closure and has no ordinary strict certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\notin\operatorname{cl}A(K)\iff\exists u\,[A^*u\in K^*,\ \langle b,u\rangle<0],\quad c\notin\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{range}A^*+K^*)\iff\exists d\,[d\in K,\ Ad=0,\ \langle c,d\rangle<0].
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-versus-Weak Infeasibility Qualification
Infeasibility-Status Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes exact certified infeasibility from approximate or unresolved solver indications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal program \(Ax=b,\ x\in K\), the status “primal infeasible” is exactly certified when a reported \(u\) satisfies \(A^*u\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,u\rangle<0\). For its dual, “dual infeasible” is exactly certified when a reported \(r\) satisfies \(r\in K\), \(Ar=0\), and \(\langle c,r\rangle<0\). A vector satisfying only numerical residual tolerances qualifies the status as approximate unless validated error bounds imply an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unqualified infeasibility status requires an exact separating certificate; residual-only evidence must be labeled approximate unless rigorous error bounds validate it.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The primal-dual orientation is the minimization convention specified locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact certificate predicates justify infeasibility; tolerance tests alone justify only a qualified numerical status.

children.title: Primal Unboundedness Status
children.top_down_role: Status conventions for primal recessionary behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Unboundedness Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for objective unboundedness of the minimization-form primal program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). A certified “primal unbounded” status consists of a feasible point \(x_0\in K\) with \(Ax_0=b\) and a recession vector \(r\in K\) with \(Ar=0\) and \(\langle c,r\rangle<0\). Then \(x(t)=x_0+tr\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\), while \(\langle c,x(t)\rangle=\langle c,x_0\rangle+t\langle c,r\rangle\to-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal unboundedness is certified by a feasible point and a cone-feasible nullspace direction that strictly decreases the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.

children.title: Dual Unboundedness Status
children.top_down_role: Status conventions for dual recessionary behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Unboundedness Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for objective unboundedness of the maximization-form dual program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\). A certified “dual unbounded” status consists of a feasible pair \((y_0,s_0)\) and a direction \(d\) satisfying \(-A^*d\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,d\rangle>0\). For every \(t\ge0\), \(y(t)=y_0+td\) and \(s(t)=s_0-tA^*d\) remain dual feasible, and \(\langle b,y(t)\rangle\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual unboundedness is certified by a feasible dual point and a direction preserving dual-cone feasibility while strictly increasing the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(K^*\) is the dual cone of a convex cone \(K\).

children.title: Recession-Certificate Orientation
children.top_down_role: Orientation conventions for certificates supporting unboundedness claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Certificate Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign conventions linking improving recession directions to infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the primal-dual pair \(P=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(D=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), a primal recession certificate has orientation \(r\in K\), \(Ar=0\), and \(\langle c,r\rangle<0\). A dual recession certificate has orientation \(-A^*d\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,d\rangle>0\). Thus \(r\) is also a dual-infeasibility certificate, whereas \(-d\) is a primal-infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal improving ray directly certifies dual infeasibility; the negative of a dual improving ray certifies primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone and \(K^*\) is its dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\mapsto r\) and \(d\mapsto-d\) give the stated recession-to-infeasibility orientation.

children.title: Paired-Problem Status Mapping
children.top_down_role: Connection between unboundedness of one problem and infeasibility evidence for its pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Paired-Problem Status Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way implications between unboundedness and infeasibility in a conic primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the weakly dual conic pair \(P=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(D=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), primal unboundedness implies dual infeasibility, and dual unboundedness implies primal infeasibility. The converses do not follow from weak duality alone: infeasibility of one member need not supply feasibility plus an improving recession direction for the other, particularly in non-strictly-feasible or weakly infeasible conic systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unboundedness of either member forces infeasibility of its paired problem, but paired infeasibility alone does not generally prove unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: Weak duality holds for the displayed primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ unbounded}\Rightarrow D\text{ infeasible}\) and \(D\text{ unbounded}\Rightarrow P\text{ infeasible}\), without general converse implications.

notation.meaning: Primal minimization and dual maximization problems.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mutual Infeasibility Refutes Both Converse Implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional conic pair showing that infeasibility of either member need not make its paired problem unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=Y=\mathbb R\), \(K=\mathbb R_+\), \(A=0\), \(b=1\), and \(c=-1\). Then \(P=\inf\{-x:0x=1,\ x\ge0\}\) is infeasible. Its paired dual \(D=\sup\{y:0y+s=-1,\ s\ge0\}\) is also infeasible because its equality requires \(s=-1\). Thus primal infeasibility does not imply dual unboundedness, and dual infeasibility does not imply primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both members of a standard conic primal-dual pair can be infeasible, refuting both infeasibility-to-unboundedness converses.
assumptions_latex: The pair uses \(P=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(D=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ infeasible}\centernot\Rightarrow D\text{ unbounded},\qquad D\text{ infeasible}\centernot\Rightarrow P\text{ unbounded}.

notation.meaning: The displayed primal and dual conic programs.

children.title: Infeasible-or-Unbounded Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Presolve or embedding outcomes that do not distinguish terminal mathematical regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical meaning and certificate boundary when an interface uses the status for an unresolved infeasibility-or-unboundedness disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a solver interface defines an “infeasible or unbounded” result to mean only \[P\text{ is infeasible}\ \lor\ P\text{ is unbounded}.\] The result does not determine either disjunct. Exact infeasibility requires an independently validated alternative-system certificate; unboundedness requires the interface-appropriate feasible point and improving recession direction. Without such additional evidence, neither terminal mathematical status follows from the disjunctive report.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When defined as an unresolved disjunction, an infeasible-or-unbounded status certifies neither branch separately; a branch-specific certificate is required.
assumptions_latex: The originating interface explicitly assigns the displayed disjunctive meaning to its status.
\(P\) is the problem after any transformations whose status the interface reports.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P\text{ infeasible}\lor P\text{ unbounded})\not\Rightarrow P\text{ infeasible},\qquad (P\text{ infeasible}\lor P\text{ unbounded})\not\Rightarrow P\text{ unbounded}.

notation.meaning: Conic problem to which the reported status applies

children.title: Unreliable Termination Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Termination outcomes without a fully reliable mathematical classification.

children.title: Unknown Status
children.top_down_role: Termination outcomes lacking a supported mathematical classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status used when available output supports no recognized mathematical termination claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver status is “unknown” when the returned data do not validate any declared terminal predicate—optimality, primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, primal unboundedness, or dual unboundedness—under the solver interface's prescribed residual and certificate tests. Formally, if \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\) are those validated predicates for returned data \(z\), then “unknown” means \(\neg T_1(z)\land\cdots\land\neg T_m(z)\), without asserting that the underlying problem lacks a definite mathematical status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown means the returned evidence validates no recognized terminal predicate, not that the mathematical problem itself has no definite status.
assumptions_latex: The solver interface specifies terminal predicates \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Unknown-status semantics are interface-specific and need not equal the negation of exactly the listed terminal predicates. The proposed biconditional requires an authoritative solver-interface source.

children.title: Inaccurate Status
children.top_down_role: Qualified outcomes whose residual evidence does not meet nominal accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Inaccurate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified status for evidence meeting relaxed but not standard numerical acceptance criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(z)\) be the nonnegative vector of normalized residuals and certificate violations computed from returned data \(z\). Given componentwise standard tolerances \(\tau\) and relaxed tolerances \(\widehat\tau\) with \(0\le\tau<\widehat\tau\), a terminal classification is “inaccurate” when its qualitative sign and cone conditions hold, \(R(z)\le\widehat\tau\), and \(R(z)\nleq\tau\). This label reports weakened numerical evidence and does not convert an approximate certificate into an exact mathematical certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inaccurate means a candidate terminal status passes relaxed validation thresholds but fails at least one standard threshold.
assumptions_latex: The interface declares standard tolerances \(\tau\) and relaxed tolerances \(\widehat\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(z)\le\widehat\tau\land R(z)\nleq\tau\) qualifies the associated terminal status as inaccurate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxed-versus-standard threshold model is plausible but solver-specific; some interfaces use different residuals, scaling, or status rules. An authoritative interface source is required.

children.title: Numerical-Failure Status
children.top_down_role: Termination outcomes attributed to numerical breakdown.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Failure Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination caused by breakdown of numerical computation rather than a validated problem classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A “numerical failure” status applies when the computation terminates because a required numerical operation is invalid or unreliable—for example, nonfinite iterates, failed factorization, or irrecoverable loss of residual evaluation—and no returned data \(z\) validate a terminal mathematical predicate \(T_i(z)\). The status characterizes the algorithmic run, not the feasibility, infeasibility, boundedness, or optimal value of the underlying exact conic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical failure describes an unusable computational run and makes no mathematical claim about the exact problem unless a separate certificate validates one.
assumptions_latex: The solver detects a declared numerical-breakdown event.
No terminal predicate \(T_i(z)\) is independently validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{numerical\ failure}\not\Rightarrow T_i(z)\) for any mathematical terminal status \(T_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between numerical breakdown and a mathematical problem classification is sound, but the triggering events and status meaning are solver-interface definitions requiring an authoritative source.

children.title: Status-Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Evidence limits separating qualified classifications from unresolved outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Status-Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating exact certification, tolerance-qualified classification, and unsupported solver output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For returned data \(z\), let \(E(z)\) denote satisfaction of an exact certificate predicate, \(S_\tau(z)\) satisfaction of the standard numerical test, and \(S_{\widehat\tau}(z)\) satisfaction of a declared relaxed test. Reliability classes are separated by \(E(z)\), \(S_\tau(z)\), and \(S_{\widehat\tau}(z)\): exact certification requires \(E(z)\); standard numerical status requires \(S_\tau(z)\); an inaccurate qualification may use \(S_{\widehat\tau}(z)\land\neg S_\tau(z)\); and failure of \(S_{\widehat\tau}(z)\) supports no such terminal classification. Finite-precision tests alone do not imply \(E(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact, standard, inaccurate, and unsupported statuses are separated by exact predicates and declared standard or relaxed validation thresholds.
assumptions_latex: The interface publishes the tests represented by \(S_\tau\) and \(S_{\widehat\tau}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(z)\), \(S_\tau(z)\), \(S_{\widehat\tau}(z)\land\neg S_\tau(z)\), and \(\neg S_{\widehat\tau}(z)\) define distinct reliability regimes.

notation.meaning: Numerical validation predicate at tolerance tau.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed four-regime boundary assumes particular nested validation tests and treats them as exhaustive. Those assumptions are interface-specific and require an authoritative source defining the tests and threshold ordering.

children.title: Linear Objective Data
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing storage of linear objective coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Objective Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-schema representation of an affine scalar objective through its linear coefficient vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a decision variable \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), linear objective data are a vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) defining the linear functional \(x\mapsto\langle c,x\rangle=c^\mathsf{T}x\). In a minimization interface the variable-dependent objective is \(c^\mathsf{T}x\); in a maximization interface it is the same functional with the declared opposite optimization sense. Any additive constant is objective metadata separate from \(c\), and no quadratic term is encoded by linear objective data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear objective data are the coefficient vector whose inner product with the decision vector gives the variable-dependent objective value.

children.title: Quadratic Objective Data
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing storage of quadratic objective terms.

assumptions_latex: The solver uses the convention \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective \(x\mapsto\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) is convex if and only if \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex quadratic-objective field and its scaling convention.

source_refs.locator: 2 Mixed Semidefinite-Quadratic-Linear Programs p. 41

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\geq0\), a decision vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), linear data \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and constant data \(d\in\mathbb{R}\), quadratic objective data consist of a symmetric matrix \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\). Under the half-quadratic convention, the complete objective is \[f(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d.\] This objective is convex precisely when \(Q\succeq0\). If only one triangular part is stored, it determines \(Q\) by symmetry and does not alter the factor \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix supplies the quadratic coefficient under the one-half scaling convention; the resulting quadratic objective is convex exactly when that matrix is positive semidefinite, and triangular storage does not change the scaling.

children.title: Objective Constant Metadata
children.top_down_role: Representation and recovery treatment for objective offsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Constant Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic role of the scalar constant in objective data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be an objective on a nonempty feasible set \(X\), and let \(d\in\mathbb{R}\). The metadata field \(d\) represents the constant shift in \(f(x)=g(x)+d\). Then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}g(x),\qquad \inf_{x\in X}f(x)=d+\inf_{x\in X}g(x),\] with the equality interpreted in the extended-real sense. Thus omitting \(d\) preserves optimizers but changes every reported objective value by \(-d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective constant shifts the optimal value but leaves the feasible set and all minimizers unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding \(d\) preserves the minimizer set and shifts the infimum by \(d\).

children.title: Quadratic-Support Boundaries

assumptions_latex: The target interface accepts convex cone programs.
The stated rotated-second-order-cone encoding uses the convention \(2uv\geq\lVert w\rVert_2^2\) with \(u,v\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint Matrix as a Solver-Schema Linear Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical semantics of the matrix field after fixing the enclosing canonical-form convention; serialization syntax is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the enclosing convention \(Ax+s=b\), with \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(s\in K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\). The constraint-matrix field represents the linear map \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), hence \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(A_{ij}\) is the coefficient of \(x_j\) in affine row \(i\). Dense and sparse encodings are semantically equivalent exactly when decoding them produces the same matrix \(A\). An encoding whose indices, values, or duplicate-entry rule do not determine a unique \(A\) is not valid matrix data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint-matrix field is the linear operator from solver columns to affine rows; storage formats are equivalent when they decode to the same matrix.
assumptions_latex: The enclosing schema declares the convention \(Ax+s=b\).

notation.meaning: constraint linear map and its matrix representation
coefficient of decision coordinate j in affine row i

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Matrix as a Solver-Schema Linear Map
Constraint Matrix Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix field in the canonical slack-form conic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the canonical constraint convention \[Ax+s=b,\qquad s\in K.\] For \(n\) scalar decision coordinates and a cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), constraint matrix data are a linear map represented by \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Entry \(A_{ij}\) is the coefficient of decision coordinate \(x_j\) in affine row \(i\). Sparse or dense storage is semantically equivalent provided absent sparse entries denote zero and the stored row and column indices use the declared index bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint matrix maps the solver's decision vector into the affine rows paired with the cone-valued slack.

children.title: Affine Offset Data
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing representation of canonical affine offsets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact update of affine offset data when decision coordinates are translated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the slack convention \(Ax+s=b\) with \(s\in K\). Under the change of variables \(x=x_0+u\), the same constraint becomes \[Au+s=b-Ax_0.\] Thus the constraint matrix and cone are unchanged while the offset in \(u\)-coordinates is \(b':=b-Ax_0\). Failing to update \(b\) changes the represented feasible set unless \(Ax_0=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translating the decision variable changes the affine offset from b to b minus A times the translation.
assumptions_latex: The declared convention is \(Ax+s=b\) with \(s\in K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Offset Transformation Under Variable Translation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogeneous-Coordinate Encoding of Affine Offset Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the offset as the constant column of an augmented affine operator under the declared slack convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the convention \(Ax+s=b\), define \(\widehat x=(x,1)\) and \(\widehat A=\begin{bmatrix}A&-b\end{bmatrix}\). Then \[Ax+s=b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widehat A\widehat x+s=0.\] Thus the final column of \(\widehat A\) is \(-b\). With a homogenizing coordinate \(\tau\), the homogeneous equation is \(Ax-b\tau+s=0\), recovering the original affine system at \(\tau=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the slack convention, the affine offset is the negative constant column of the augmented constraint operator.

notation.meaning: constraint operator augmented by its constant column
decision vector augmented by a homogenizing coordinate equal to one

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous-Coordinate Encoding of Affine Offset Data

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the offset field under slack form and its conversion to an affine-inclusion convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the declared convention \(Ax+s=b\) with \(s\in K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), the affine offset is the row-aligned vector \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and feasibility is \(b-Ax\in K\). If another interface instead writes \(Ax+c\in K\) using the same operator \(A\), equivalence requires \(c=-b\) and replacement of \(A\) by \(-A\), because \(b-Ax=(-A)x+b\). Equivalently, retaining \(A\) gives \(Ax-b\in -K\). Thus numeric offsets cannot be transferred without converting the complete sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In slack form b is the row-aligned right-hand side; changing to an affine-inclusion convention requires coordinated signs for the operator, offset, and possibly the cone.

notation.meaning: row-aligned affine offset in slack form

knowledge_statements.title: Offset Semantics and Sign-Convention Conversion
Affine Offset Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-hand-side field in the canonical slack-form constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the convention \(Ax+s=b\) with \(s\in K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), affine offset data are a vector \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Equivalently, feasibility requires \(b-Ax\in K\). Coordinate \(b_i\) is paired with row \(i\) of \(A\) and coordinate \(i\) of the cone representation. Changing to an interface convention such as \(Ax+b\in K\) requires an explicit sign conversion; the same numeric vector cannot be transferred between these conventions without reinterpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The offset vector supplies the right-hand side of every affine row and must follow the solver's declared sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and feasibility is equivalent to \(b-Ax\in K\).

children.title: Cone-Block Row Assembly

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Row Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered assembly of affine rows for a product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_r\), where \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\), and set \(m=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\). For block data \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\), row assembly is \[A=\begin{bmatrix}A_1\\ \vdots\\ A_r\end{bmatrix},\qquad b=\begin{bmatrix}b_1\\ \vdots\\ b_r\end{bmatrix}.\] With \(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)\), the constraint \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), is equivalent to \(A_i x+s_i=b_i\), \(s_i\in K_i\), for every \(i\). The metadata order must equal the stacking order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rows and offsets are stacked in exactly the same order as their product-cone blocks, yielding equivalent blockwise constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\) is equivalent to \(A_i x+s_i=b_i,\ s_i\in K_i\) for all \(i\).

notation.meaning: vector dimension of the ith cone block
affine data assigned to block i

children.title: Affine-Dimension Consistency
