knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Dimension Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete dimensional predicate for assembled affine cone data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For data \((A,b,K)\) and decision dimension \(n\), affine-dimension consistency holds exactly when there exists \(m\geq0\) such that \[A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n},\qquad b\in\mathbb{R}^m,\qquad K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m.\] If \(K=\prod_{i=1}^r K_i\) with \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\), one additionally requires \(m=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\), and the row intervals assigned to the blocks must be disjoint, ordered, and cover \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). These conditions make \(b-Ax\in K\) well typed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix rows, offset length, total cone dimension, and all ordered block dimensions must agree exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine constraint is well typed if and only if all displayed dimensions and the block-row partition agree.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Type Descriptors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type tags identifying the factors of an ordered product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordered product cone \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_r\), a cone type descriptor is an ordered tuple \((\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_r)\) whose entry \(\tau_i\) selects a declared cone family \(\mathcal{K}_{\tau_i}\). Together with valid dimension and parameter metadata, it determines \(K_i=\mathcal{K}_{\tau_i}(m_i,\theta_i)\). Equality of numeric dimensions alone does not permit exchanging type tags: for example, a nonnegative-orthant block and a second-order-cone block of the same dimension define different feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each ordered type tag selects the cone family for one block; dimensions alone do not determine cone semantics.
assumptions_latex: The interface declares a finite set of supported cone-family tags.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Dimension Descriptors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector-space dimensions attached to ordered cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given cone type tags \((\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_r)\), cone dimension descriptors are integers \((m_1,
\ldots,m_r)\) with \(m_i\geq0\), subject to the admissibility rules of each family \(\mathcal{K}_{\tau_i}\). They assert that \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\) and that the assembled product cone satisfies \[K=\prod_{i=1}^rK_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m},\qquad m=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i.\] Consequently, the total descriptor dimension must equal the number of affine constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block dimensions specify each cone's vector-space size, and their sum must equal the affine row count.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is the number of cone blocks.
Each \(m_i\) satisfies its cone family's admissibility rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(K\text{'s ambient space})=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\), which must equal the affine row count.

children.title: Cone Parameter Descriptors
children.top_down_role: Metadata for exponent weights and other cone-specific parameters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic ordered metadata for cone families whose identity depends on values beyond type and dimension; the supported family catalog is supplied by the enclosing interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ordered cone blocks \((\tau_i,m_i)_{i=1}^r\), let \(P_i=\Theta_{\tau_i}(m_i)\) be the parameter domain declared by the enclosing cone interface. A cone parameter descriptor assigns \(\theta_i\in P_i\) to each parameterized block and thereby selects \(K_i=\mathcal K_{\tau_i}(m_i,\theta_i)\). Parameter-free families have no parameter record, equivalently a singleton empty parameter value. Descriptor association is blockwise and order preserving. Metadata are valid exactly when every required descriptor is present once, no descriptor is attached to a parameter-free block, and \(\theta_i\in P_i\) for every parameterized block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each parameterized cone block receives exactly one ordered parameter value from the domain declared jointly by its type and dimension.
assumptions_latex: The enclosing interface declares its supported cone types and each domain \(\Theta_\tau(m)\).
Cone blocks have a fixed order and declared dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_i=\mathcal K_{\tau_i}(m_i,\theta_i)\text{ is unambiguously selected for every parameterized block }i.

notation.meaning: interface-declared admissible parameter domain for type tau and dimension m
cone selected by type, dimension, and parameter

knowledge_statements.title: Schema-Relative Cone Parameter Descriptors
Cone Parameter Descriptors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity predicate for family-specific cone parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each cone block with type \(\tau_i\) and dimension \(m_i\), let \(\Theta_{\tau_i}(m_i)\) be the declared admissible parameter set. A parameter descriptor \(\theta_i\) is valid exactly when \(\theta_i\in\Theta_{\tau_i}(m_i)\), in which case the block is \(K_i=\mathcal{K}_{\tau_i}(m_i,\theta_i)\). Parameter-free families use the unique empty tuple. Parameters are interpreted blockwise and in order; a parameter belonging to one block cannot be consumed by another. For example, a three-dimensional power cone requires an exponent \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block's parameter tuple must belong to the admissible set determined jointly by its cone type and dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metadata are valid if and only if \(\theta_i\in\Theta_{\tau_i}(m_i)\) for every block \(i\).

notation.meaning: admissible parameter set for type tau and dimension m

children.title: Matrix-Side Dimension Descriptors

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Side Dimension Descriptors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion between matrix order and vectorized semidefinite-block dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real symmetric positive-semidefinite block of matrix order \(p\geq1\), the matrix-side descriptor is \(p\), while its vectorized cone dimension is \[m=\dim\mathbb{S}^p=\frac{p(p+1)}{2}.\] Under a fixed bijective symmetric-vectorization map \(\operatorname{svec}:\mathbb{S}^p\to\mathbb{R}^m\), the cone block is \(\operatorname{svec}(\mathbb{S}_+^p)\). Hence a semidefinite block's affine-row allocation must have length \(p(p+1)/2\), and the declared triangular ordering and off-diagonal scaling must match the solver convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real symmetric matrix block of order p occupies p(p+1)/2 cone-vector rows under the declared symmetric vectorization.
assumptions_latex: The block contains real symmetric matrices.
A fixed bijective symmetric-vectorization convention is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix order \(p\) induces the vector dimension \(m=p(p+1)/2\).

notation.meaning: cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consistency test between a positive real symmetric matrix order and its vectorized cone dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,p\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\). A declared vector dimension \(m\) is compatible with a full real symmetric matrix block of order \(p\) exactly when \(m=p(p+1)/2\). Equivalently, \(8m+1\) is the odd perfect square \((2p+1)^2\), in which case \(p=(\sqrt{8m+1}-1)/2\) is unique. A nontriangular positive integer \(m\) cannot be the dimension of \(\mathbb S^p\) under a bijective symmetric vectorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive vector dimension represents a full real symmetric matrix block exactly when it is triangular, and then the matrix order is unique.
assumptions_latex: The block represents all of \(\mathbb S^p\) through a bijective symmetric vectorization.

children.title: Variable Index Maps
children.top_down_role: Mappings between source variables and canonical solver columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping from represented source-variable scalar components to their canonical solver columns; auxiliary and eliminated entities are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_R\) be the finite set of scalar components of source variables represented directly as solver coordinates, and let \(J_R\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the solver columns assigned to them. A variable index map is a bijection \(\pi:V_R\to J_R\). For an assignment \(z:V_R\to\mathbb R\), packing and inverse lookup satisfy \(x_{\pi(v)}=z(v)\) and \(z(v)=x_{\pi(v)}\). Every objective and constraint reference to a represented component must use the same \(\pi\). Solver columns for auxiliary entities lie outside \(J_R\); eliminated or affinely transformed source quantities require a separate recovery map rather than an entry in \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The map bijectively packs directly represented source-variable components into their designated solver columns and supports exact inverse lookup on that subset.
assumptions_latex: \(V_R\) is the finite set of directly represented source scalar components.
\(J_R\) is the declared subset of solver columns assigned to those components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi:V_R\leftrightarrow J_R\text{ gives lossless packing and inverse lookup on the represented subset}.

notation.meaning: solver columns owned by represented source variables

knowledge_statements.title: Represented Source-Variable Index Map
Variable Index Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between canonical scalar variables and solver-vector coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}\) be the ordered set of canonical scalar decision entities. A variable index map is a bijection \(\pi:V\to\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The solver vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) represents an assignment \(z:V\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(x_{\pi(v)}=z(v)\) for every \(v\in V\). Its inverse reconstructs \(z(v)=x_{
\pi(v)}\). Validity requires every canonical variable to occur exactly once, every solver coordinate to be used exactly once, and all objective and constraint references to use the same \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable index map bijectively assigns each canonical scalar variable to one solver-vector coordinate and is shared by all data fields.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) contains exactly \(n\) distinct scalar variable entities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\) provides lossless forward packing and inverse reconstruction of every variable assignment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bijection is mathematically coherent, but no source establishes that the target canonical mapping system requires a bijection over exactly the retained scalar variables or excludes transformed, auxiliary, duplicated, or eliminated coordinates. children.title: Constraint Index Maps
children.top_down_role: Mappings between source constraints and canonical solver rows.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward and inverse correspondence between source constraints and the solver rows attributed to them; generated rows are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the finite source-constraint set and let \(R_C\subseteq R\) be the solver rows declared to be owned by source constraints. A constraint index map assigns each \(c\in\mathcal C\) an ordered tuple \(I_C(c)\) of distinct elements of \(R_C\). The tuple images are pairwise disjoint and their union is \(R_C\). Hence the inverse owner map \(O_C:R_C\to\mathcal C\) is uniquely defined by \(O_C(r)=c\) when \(r\in\operatorname{set}(I_C(c))\). Rows generated independently by canonicalization belong to \(R\setminus R_C\) and are not required to be covered by \(I_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each source constraint owns an ordered, disjoint tuple of source-attributed solver rows, with exhaustive coverage only of that row subset and unique reverse ownership.
assumptions_latex: \(R_C\subseteq R\) is the declared source-constraint-owned row set.

notation.meaning: solver rows owned by source constraints
ordered solver-row tuple assigned to source constraint c

children.title: Auxiliary-Entity Index Maps
children.top_down_role: Mappings for variables or rows introduced during canonicalization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locations and provenance of entities generated during canonicalization, relative to the entity types declared by the enclosing schema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the finite set of auxiliary-entity types declared by a canonicalization schema, let \(\mathcal A=\bigsqcup_{t\in T}\mathcal A_t\), and let \(U=\bigsqcup_{t\in T}U_t\) be the corresponding disjoint union of target-location sets. An auxiliary-entity index map is a type-preserving injection \(I_A:\mathcal A\to U\) satisfying \(I_A(\mathcal A_t)\subseteq U_t\). It has an inverse owner map on its image. Each auxiliary entity also records its generating source entity or transformation, its local ordinal, and any declared shape needed to interpret its target location. Types not declared by the schema are outside the map's domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generated canonical entities receive unique typed target locations and retain enough provenance for reverse ownership lookup.
assumptions_latex: The enclosing schema declares the supported entity types and their target-location sets.

children.title: Index-Map Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Integrity checks supporting reliable source-to-solver translation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic validation procedure for the structural predicates declared by the schema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Validate an index-map family by traversing each forward entry, checking its type, range, tuple shape, and local distinctness; record each index's declared owner; reject forbidden ownership collisions; compare the recorded owners with every inverse lookup and stored offset or slice; and finally verify the required coverage multiplicity of every mandatory target index. children.title: Cone-Row Ordering
children.top_down_role: Global row-order conventions for canonical cone constraints.

assumptions_latex: The product cone is represented by ordered blocks \(K_1,\ldots,K_B\) with dimensions \(d_1,\ldots,d_B\).
Each block has a fixed internal coordinate order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines global row positions after block order and internal coordinate conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(o_1=0\) and \(o_b=\sum_{a=1}^{b-1}d_a\) for \(2\le b\le B\). The cone-row ordering map is \(\rho(b,j)=o_b+j\) for \(1\le b\le B\) and \(0\le j<d_b\). Thus a block vector \(s=(s^{(1)},\ldots,s^{(B)})\in K_1\times\cdots\times K_B\) is stored as the length-\(m\) vector satisfying \(s_{\rho(b,j)}=s^{(b)}_j\), where \(m=\sum_{b=1}^{B}d_b\). The map \(\rho\) is a bijection onto \(\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone rows are ordered by concatenating each block's fixed internal coordinates at prefix-sum offsets, producing a bijection to all global rows.

children.title: Cone-Block Ordering
children.top_down_role: Global ordering conventions for heterogeneous cone factors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States how changing the outer block order acts on a product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_B\), where \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\), and let \(\sigma\) be a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,B\}\). Define
\[
P_\sigma(x_1,\ldots,x_B)=(x_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,x_{\sigma(B)}).
\]
Then \(P_\sigma\) is a linear bijection and
\[
x\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P_\sigma x\in K_{\sigma(1)}\times\cdots\times K_{\sigma(B)}.
\]
Thus block order changes serialization but not blockwise cone membership when every block-aligned coordinate object is permuted consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permuting whole cone blocks gives a linearly isomorphic product cone, provided all block-aligned coordinates are permuted identically.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma\) is a permutation of the block indices.

notation.meaning: linear permutation of whole cone blocks

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Equivalence of Cone-Block Orders

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal ambiguity caused by an ordering-key collision between labeled blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B=\{a,b\}\), where \(a\ne b\) are labeled cone-block instances and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa(b)\). Sorting solely by \(\kappa\) admits both sequences \((a,b)\) and \((b,a)\). Without a declared deterministic tie-breaker, the serialization is not unique, even if \(K_a=K_b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct blocks with the same effective key admit two serializations, so that key does not define a unique block order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa\) does not induce a unique serialization of \(\mathcal B\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equal-Key Serialization Ambiguity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prefix-Offset Representation of an Ordered Cone Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contiguous coordinate intervals induced by an already fixed cone-block sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\), \(i=1,\ldots,B\), be an ordered block sequence with \(d_i>0\). Define \(s_1=0\) and \(s_{i+1}=s_i+d_i\). Then block \(i\) occupies \(I_i=[s_i,s_{i+1})\), and \[\bigsqcup_{i=1}^B I_i=[0,D),\qquad D=\sum_{i=1}^B d_i.\] Thus every product vector has a unique block decomposition once the sequence and dimensions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefix sums of ordered block dimensions assign unique consecutive coordinate intervals to cone blocks.

notation.meaning: Starting coordinate offset of block i
Coordinate interval assigned to block i

knowledge_statements.title: Prefix-Offset Representation of an Ordered Cone Product

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction and validation of an outer block sequence from complete effective keys.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\) labeled cone blocks with positive dimensions and comparable effective keys, reject any invalid dimension or duplicate effective key. Sort the blocks by increasing key, assign positions \(1,\ldots,B\), and compute prefix offsets from the ordered dimensions. Comparison sorting takes \(O(B\log B)\) comparisons and validation plus offset construction takes \(O(B)\) time and \(O(B)\) output storage. If the input is already certified as key-sorted, validation and offset construction take \(O(B)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate unique complete keys, sort the blocks, assign positions, and compute offsets; comparison-based construction is logarithmic-linear, or linear for certified sorted input.
assumptions_latex: There are \(B\) labeled blocks with positive integer dimensions.
Effective keys lie in a totally ordered set and are comparable.
The complete key includes every required deterministic tie component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unique effective keys yield one deterministic sequence and prefix-offset table in }O(B\log B)\text{ comparisons}.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Cone-Block Ordering Construction

assumptions_latex: A finite family of cone blocks \(\mathcal B\) is declared.
Each block has a stable ordering key and a positive dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sorting by the declared key produces a unique block sequence and therefore a unique product-cone representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone-block ordering is induced by an injective key \(\kappa:\mathcal B\to L\) into a totally ordered set \(L\). Writing \(b_1,\ldots,b_B\) for the unique enumeration satisfying \(\kappa(b_1)<\cdots<\kappa(b_B)\), the serialized cone is \(K=K_{b_1}\times\cdots\times K_{b_B}\). The block-position map \(\pi_B:\mathcal B\to\{1,\ldots,B\}\) is defined by \(\pi_B(b_i)=i\). Cone type alone need not determine the order; every tie-relevant component must be included in \(\kappa\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every repeated-block family \(f\), assign a bijection \(q_f:\mathcal B_f\to\{0,\ldots,|\mathcal B_f|-1\}\). If \(b\in\mathcal B_f\), its global ordering key must contain \((f,q_f(b))\) after all higher-priority components. Consequently, for distinct \(b,b'\in\mathcal B_f\), \(q_f(b)<q_f(b')\) implies \(\kappa(b)<\kappa(b')\). The ordinal must be derived from stable source identity or an explicitly persisted order, rather than allocation order or hash-table traversal.

children.title: Ordering-Stability Requirements
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements shared by solver input and result recovery.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reproducibility by comparing explicitly declared layout data under a source-identity correspondence, avoiding undefined literal equality between models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a canonicalized model \(M\), let \(L(M)\) contain the ordered source identifiers, block indices, row intervals, and block-local coordinate maps. Let \(\phi:E(M)\to E(M')\) be a bijection preserving every source identifier and ordering-relevant persisted datum. The ordering is stable when \(L(M')=\phi_*L(M)\), where \(\phi_*\) relabels only the source entities and leaves all numerical positions unchanged. A sufficient implementation condition is sorting by a persisted strict-total-order key preserved by \(\phi\). Allocation addresses, randomized iteration order, and nondeterministic completion order cannot be unrecorded key components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layout stability means identity-equivalent models have the same declared indices, row intervals, and local coordinate maps after source entities are relabeled; sorting by preserved deterministic keys is sufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:E(M)\to E(M')\) preserves source identifiers and all persisted ordering metadata.
\(L(M)\) records the layout fields being compared.

children.title: Semidefinite Vectorization Conventions
children.top_down_role: Packed-triangle ordering and off-diagonal scaling variants.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates packed-triangle traversal and nonzero coordinate-scaling conventions without prescribing a solver-specific order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,v_2:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^{n(n+1)/2}\) pack the same independent matrix entries, possibly in different orders and with different nonzero coordinate scalings. Then \(v_2(X)=DPv_1(X)\) for a permutation matrix \(P\) and nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\). If \(a_1^\top v_1(X)\) represents a linear functional, its coordinates in the second convention are \(a_2=D^{-\top}Pa_1\), giving \(a_2^\top v_2(X)=a_1^\top v_1(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Packed symmetric conventions differ by permutation and diagonal scaling; paired coefficient coordinates transform by the inverse transpose.
assumptions_latex: Both maps pack exactly one copy of every independent entry of a real symmetric matrix.
Every coordinate scaling factor is nonzero.
review_flags: Exact traversal and scaling conventions remain interface-specific.
knowledge_statements.title: Change of Packed Symmetric Coordinates

assumptions_latex: Matrices lie in the real symmetric space \(\mathbb S^n\).
Packed entries use one fixed triangular traversal order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled convention is an isometry for the trace inner product, whereas the unscaled convention requires explicit off-diagonal weights.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Packed symmetric vectorization has standard unscaled and square-root-of-two-scaled variants.
Exact supporting discussion of solver vectorization conventions remains to be sourced.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes packed-triangle ordering from off-diagonal scaling for real symmetric matrices.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Semidefinite programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), \(\operatorname{vech}(X)\in\mathbb R^{n(n+1)/2}\) lists exactly one triangular copy of each entry in the declared traversal order. The scaled map uses the same order and satisfies \((\operatorname{svec}(X))_{ii}=X_{ii}\) and \((\operatorname{svec}(X))_{ij}=\sqrt{2}X_{ij}\) for packed positions with \(i<j\). Hence \(\langle X,Y\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{svec}(X)^\top\operatorname{svec}(Y)\). For unscaled packing, \(\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\sum_iX_{ii}Y_{ii}+2\sum_{i<j}X_{ij}Y_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Packed symmetric matrices require a declared triangle order; scaling off-diagonal entries by square root of two preserves the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Vectorization Conventions

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Semidefinite programming p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and formulas are standard and mathematically consistent for a fixed packed-triangle order. The cited introductory semidefinite-programming locator does not demonstrably support the exact vech/svec convention, square-root-of-two scaling, or packed-position indexing. A specific definition, section, or page discussing symmetric vectorization is required.

children.title: Nonsymmetric-Cone Coordinate Ordering
children.top_down_role: Coordinate and sign layouts for exponential and power cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Coordinates under a Stored-to-Mathematical Transform
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determines the dual block layout induced by an invertible coordinate transform used for a nonsymmetric primal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^3\) be a closed convex cone, let \(T\) be invertible, and let the stored primal cone be \(C=T^{-1}K=\{u:Tu\in K\}\). Under the Euclidean pairing, \(C^*=T^{\mathsf T}K^*\). Equivalently, a mathematical dual coordinate \(y\in K^*\) corresponds to the stored coordinate \(v=T^{\mathsf T}y\), since \(v^{\mathsf T}u=y^{\mathsf T}Tu\). For a signed permutation, \(T^{-1}=T^{\mathsf T}\), but the declared directions of the primal membership and dual coordinate maps must still be respected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If T maps stored primal coordinates into the mathematical cone, the paired stored dual coordinates use the transpose map; a nonsymmetric primal layout cannot simply be reused as its dual layout.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^3\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Coordinates under a Stored-to-Mathematical Transform

assumptions_latex: Each nonsymmetric cone block declares its cone type, parameters, coordinate permutation, and sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership is interpreted only after applying the declared coordinate and sign transformation to the stored triple.

notation.meaning: Closed exponential cone in mathematical coordinate order.
Signed permutation from stored to mathematical coordinates.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Exponential and power cone interfaces conventionally require explicit coordinate, parameter, primal-dual, and sign metadata.
Exact solver-interface conventions vary and require a dedicated source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixes mathematical coordinate order while allowing explicitly declared solver-side permutations and sign transforms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use mathematical order \((x,y,z)\) with \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,y,z):y>0,\ y\exp(x/y)\le z\}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha=\{(x,y,z):x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ |z|\le x^\alpha y^{1-\alpha}\}\). If a solver stores \(u\in\mathbb R^3\), its block metadata must specify a signed permutation \(T\) and interpret membership as \(Tu\in K_{\exp}\) or \(Tu\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\). The metadata must also distinguish primal from dual cone coordinates; neither permutation nor sign change is inferred from cone type alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential and power blocks use declared mathematical triples; any solver permutation, sign change, parameter, or primal-dual choice must be explicit.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric-Cone Coordinate Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed primal exponential and power cone definitions are standard and the representation kind fits the leaf. The record also makes interface claims about signed permutations and primal-versus-dual metadata without defining the dual-coordinate transformation or citing a solver specification. Exact conventions vary materially across solvers, so source uncertainty affects the intended statement.

children.title: Block Offset Accounting
children.top_down_role: Bookkeeping for starting positions of serialized cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Block Lookup from Prefix Offsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers a serialized coordinate's unique nonempty block and local coordinate, including layouts containing zero-dimensional blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0=o_1\le o_2\le\cdots\le o_{B+1}=m\) with \(o_{b+1}-o_b=d_b\ge0\). For \(r\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\), set \(b=\max\{i\in\{1,\ldots,B\}:o_i\le r\}\) and \(j=r-o_b\). Then \(o_b\le r<o_{b+1}\), \(0\le j<d_b\), and \((b,j)\) is the unique block-local pair satisfying \(r=o_b+j\). An upper-bound binary search computes it in \(O(\log B)\) comparisons; a monotone scan assigns all rows in \(O(B+m)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper-bound lookup in nondecreasing prefix offsets recovers the unique nonempty block and local coordinate; binary search handles individual rows and a monotone scan handles the full layout.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Block Lookup from Prefix Offsets

assumptions_latex: Cone blocks are ordered and have nonnegative serialized dimensions \(d_1,\ldots,d_B\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines zero-based half-open slices for consecutive cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(o_1=0\) and \(o_b=\sum_{a=1}^{b-1}d_a\) for \(2\le b\le B+1\), where \(d_{B+1}\) is not used. Block \(b\) occupies the half-open slice \(S_b=[o_b,o_{b+1})\cap\mathbb Z\), whose cardinality is \(|S_b|=d_b\). These slices satisfy \(S_b\cap S_c=\varnothing\) for \(b\ne c\) and \(\bigcup_{b=1}^{B}S_b=\{0,\ldots,o_{B+1}-1\}\), with \(o_{B+1}=\sum_{b=1}^{B}d_b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exclusive prefix sums give each ordered cone block a contiguous half-open slice; the slices are disjoint and exactly cover the cone vector.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Triangular-Dimension Test for Packed Symmetric Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when a stored coordinate dimension can represent one packed real symmetric matrix block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonnegative integer \(d\) is the packed coordinate dimension of a real symmetric matrix of order \(p\) if and only if \(8d+1\) is an odd perfect square. The order is then uniquely \(p=(\sqrt{8d+1}-1)/2\), and \(d=p(p+1)/2\). Thus declarations of both \(d\) and \(p\) are consistent exactly when this triangular-number identity holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A packed symmetric-block dimension is valid exactly when it is triangular, and the corresponding matrix order is unique.
assumptions_latex: The block stores the independent entries of a real symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists p\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:d=\frac{p(p+1)}2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 8d+1\text{ is an odd perfect square}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates decision-space columns and serialized cone-space rows in the affine solver data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic equation \(Ax+s=b\) with \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(s\in K\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_K}\), dimension consistency requires \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_K\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_K}\). An objective vector must satisfy \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and any cone dual vector must lie in \(\mathbb R^{m_K}\). If a block operator \(A_b\) corresponds to a cone slice of dimension \(d_b\), then \(A_b\in\mathbb R^{d_b\times n}\), and stacking the \(A_b\) in block order recovers \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine matrix has one column per solver variable and one row per serialized cone coordinate; all associated vectors and block operators must match.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Side Dimension Accounting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the dimension-accounting leaf, and all variables, matrix shapes, and block dimensions are explicit and internally consistent for the convention Ax+s=b. No inspectable source establishes that solver-form convention or the associated block-stacking schema, so the interface claim remains needs-source candidate knowledge.

children.title: Accounting Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Mismatch conditions involving dimensions, offsets, or matrix orders.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that a correct terminal offset does not validate intermediate block boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_1=d_2=2\), \(m=4\), and \((o_1,o_2,o_3)=(0,3,4)\). Although \(o_3=m=d_1+d_2\), the induced half-open slices have cardinalities \(3\) and \(1\), not \(2\) and \(2\). Thus terminal-count equality alone does not imply accounting consistency; each increment must satisfy \(o_{b+1}-o_b=d_b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correct total offset can conceal incorrect internal block boundaries; every offset increment must match its block dimension.

notation.meaning: Declared serialized dimension of block b.

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal-Count Equality Is Insufficient
Accounting Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions for vectorized products of scalar, vector, and symmetric-matrix cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the cone layout be \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_b\), with storage dimension \(d_i\) for block \(K_i\). Define offsets by \(o_1=0\) and \(o_{i+1}=o_i+d_i\). The layout is accounting-consistent precisely when \(o_{b+1}=m\), the intervals \([o_i,o_{i+1})\) are pairwise disjoint and cover \([0,m)\), and every matrix-valued block uses one declared vectorization convention whose stored dimension equals its convention-specific value. Consequently, an affine map represented by \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has exactly one row for every stored cone coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block offsets must partition all cone coordinates exactly, matrix blocks must obey their declared vectorization, and the affine map must have one row per stored coordinate.

notation.meaning: stored scalar dimension of cone block i
starting offset of cone block i

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports solver-layout accounting conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the accounting-consistency leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no citation is supplied for the solver-layout, matrix-vectorization, or row-accounting interface semantics. An inspectable implementation specification or modeling-system reference is required.

children.title: Solver Representation Selection Interface
children.top_down_role: Selection between direct cone support, exact bridges, and unsupported model paths.

children.title: Direct Cone-Support Detection
children.top_down_role: Capability queries for cone types, dimensions, and constrained-variable forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Cone-Support Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capability predicate for submitting a constrained-variable form without reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a solver \(S\), cone family \(K(\theta)\), dimension \(d\), and constrained-variable form \(F\), define \(\operatorname{Direct}(S,K(\theta),d,F)\) to hold exactly when the solver capability declaration accepts the tuple \((K,\theta,d,F)\) and the solver can receive that representation without introducing auxiliary variables or replacing the cone constraint by another constraint family. A model constraint \(g(x)\in K(\theta)\) is directly supported only if this predicate holds and the stored dimension of \(g(x)\) equals \(d\). Family support alone does not imply support for every parameter, dimension, or form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone constraint is directly supported only when the solver accepts its family, parameters, dimension, and variable form without a reformulation or auxiliary variables.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\) is represented in form \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\in K(\theta)\) is submitted unchanged if and only if \(\operatorname{Direct}(S,K(\theta),d,F)\) holds.
review_flags: No supplied locator documents a solver capability-query contract.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capability condition matches the direct-support detection leaf, but its exact tuple-based support contract and unchanged-submission semantics are interface-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Natural versus Extended Formulation Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection between direct natural cones and exact standard-cone lifts.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural versus Extended Formulation Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact selection rule between a natural cone and a lifted standard-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(g(x)\in K\) and an exact lift \(g(x)\in K\iff\exists z\; H(x,z)\in L\). Select the natural formulation when \(K\) is directly supported and its declared implementation cost is preferred. Otherwise select the extended formulation only when \(L\) is supported, the projection of its feasible set onto \(x\) equals the original feasible set, and objective values are unchanged. If neither representation is supported, or if the proposed lift supplies only an inner or outer approximation, exact automatic selection fails. Among exact supported choices, a declared deterministic cost order may select the representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a directly supported natural cone when preferred; otherwise use a supported exact lift whose projection and objective agree with the original model.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) are closed convex cones.
The lift preserves the original objective, which is independent of \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:g(x)\in K\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,z):H(x,z)\in L\}\) for every selectable exact lift.

notation.meaning: auxiliary variables of the extended formulation
product cone used by the lift

review_flags: Supplied sources discuss conic models but not this representation-selection policy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits selection between natural and exact extended formulations, and it distinguishes exact lifts from approximations. The selection policy, implementation-cost preference, and support semantics nevertheless require a specific modeling-system or solver-interface source.

children.title: Automatic Constraint Bridges
children.top_down_role: Modeling-system transformations selected from solver capabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Constraint Bridges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capability-driven application of exact constraint transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a constraint type \(T_0\), solver-supported set \(\mathcal S\), and a registry of exact bridges \(B:T\to(T_1,\ldots,T_k)\) carrying recovery maps. Initialize a worklist with the original constraint. Repeatedly remove a constraint of type \(T\); submit it if \(T\in\mathcal S\), otherwise choose an admissible bridge by the declared precedence rule, introduce its auxiliary variables and target constraints, record its recovery map, and append unsupported targets to the worklist. Reject a bridge that revisits an active type or lacks exact forward and recovery semantics. Stop successfully when every generated constraint is supported; compose recorded recovery maps in reverse order after solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly replace unsupported constraints with exact registered transformations until all targets are supported, while recording metadata needed to recover the original solution.
assumptions_latex: Every selected bridge preserves feasibility under projection.
The bridge registry and precedence rule are finite and deterministic.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies automatic bridge execution and recovery semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is appropriate for the automatic-bridge leaf, but the worklist procedure, precedence behavior, cycle rejection, and recovery-map contract are implementation semantics for which no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Bridge Composition Calculus
children.top_down_role: Ordering and composition of multiple exact representation bridges.

children.title: Sequential Bridge Composition
children.top_down_role: Representation paths formed from multiple compatible exact bridges.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Associativity of Finite Exact Bridge Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parenthesization invariance of compatible exact bridge chains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,B_2,B_3\) be composable exact bridges with recovery maps \(R_1,R_2,R_3\), applied in that order. After identifying lifted formulations differing only by auxiliary-variable order or renaming, the two parenthesizations impose the same existential constraints and both recover through \(R_1\circ R_2\circ R_3\). Thus finite exact bridge composition is associative up to auxiliary-coordinate isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible exact bridge chains are independent of parenthesization apart from harmless auxiliary-coordinate changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Associativity of Finite Exact Bridge Composition

assumptions_latex: Each bridge equivalence holds for every input in its declared domain.
The codomain representation of \(B_1\) lies in the domain of \(B_2\).

notation.meaning: recovery map associated with the i-th bridge

review_flags: Corrected the missing membership command in the first bridge target.
No supplied locator directly supports bridge-composition semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of exact bridges and their recovery maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1\) represent \(u\in C\) exactly as \(\exists y\;F(u,y)\in D\), and let \(B_2\) represent \(F(u,y)\in D\) exactly as \(\exists z\;G(u,y,z)\in E\). Their sequential composition is the representation \[u\in C\iff\exists(y,z)\;G(u,y,z)\in E.\] If \(R_2\) recovers a \(D\)-level solution from the \(E\)-level solution and \(R_1\) recovers the original solution from the \(D\)-level solution, then the composed recovery map is \(R_1\circ R_2\). Thus exactness and recoverability are preserved by finite sequential composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two exact bridges compose by existentially retaining both auxiliary blocks; solution recovery applies the second bridge's map before the first bridge's map.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Bridge Composition

children.title: Bridge Selection Precedence
children.top_down_role: Priority conventions among competing supported bridge paths.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unique bridge selection when exact admissible alternatives have no declared ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1\ne B_2\) be admissible exact bridges from the same unsupported state \(T\), with no declared preference or tie-breaker. A procedure selecting the first registered bridge returns \(B_1\) for registry order \((B_1,B_2)\) and \(B_2\) for \((B_2,B_1)\). Thus exactness and admissibility alone do not determine a selected bridge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two admissible exact bridges are selected inconsistently when registry order is the only implicit tie-breaker.
assumptions_latex: B_1\text{ and }B_2\text{ are admissible exact bridges from }T
review_flags: Establishes the need for declared precedence but does not prescribe an interface-specific policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Does Not Determine Precedence
Bridge Selection Precedence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic ordering of multiple admissible bridge paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unsupported type \(T\), let \(\mathcal B(T)\) be its admissible bridges. Assign each \(B\in\mathcal B(T)\) a lexicographic key \(\kappa(B)=(f(B),c(B),p(B),i(B))\), where \(f\) indicates known conversion failure, \(c\) is estimated total bridge cost, \(p\) is declared priority, and \(i\) is a unique stable identifier. Discard bridges with \(f(B)=1\) or an active-cycle target, then select the bridge with minimal key. If no bridge remains, report unsupported conversion. The unique identifier makes selection deterministic when all substantive criteria tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter failed or cyclic bridges, then choose the admissible bridge with the smallest deterministic lexicographic cost-and-priority key.
assumptions_latex: Every bridge has a unique stable identifier \(i(B)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{admissible}}(T)}\kappa(B)\) is unique when the admissible set is nonempty.

notation.meaning: registered bridges applicable to type T

review_flags: Precedence criteria are interface-policy dependent and lack a supplied source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits bridge-selection precedence and is internally deterministic, but the particular failure, cost, priority, and identifier ordering is a specific invented policy rather than a source-supported general rule. A modeling-system specification with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Equivalent Bridge Paths
children.top_down_role: Alternative exact bridge compositions reaching a common supported form.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant lifted equations show that equal primal projections do not identify dual recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar \(x\), let path \(P\) impose \(x=0\), and path \(Q\) impose \(x=0\) and \(2x=0\). Both project to \(\{0\}\). For objective \(cx\), stationarity in \(P\) requires \(c+\lambda=0\), whereas stationarity in \(Q\) requires \(c+\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0\). The first multiplier is unique, while the second pair is generally nonunique; primal equivalence therefore supplies no canonical equality of recovered multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundant equality preserves primal feasibility but changes and can make nonunique the multiplier representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\mathcal F_P=\operatorname{proj}_x\mathcal F_Q=\{0\}\quad\text{but their multiplier representations are not canonically identical}

notation.meaning: multiplier for the equation in path P
multipliers for the redundant equations in path Q

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Equivalence Without Multiplier Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of projected-feasible-set equality for objectives depending only on original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{proj}_X\mathcal F_P=\operatorname{proj}_X\mathcal F_Q=F\). For every \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), the lifted problems \(\inf\{f(x):(x,y)\in\mathcal F_P\}\) and \(\inf\{f(x):(x,z)\in\mathcal F_Q\}\) have the same value. Whenever minimizers exist, their minimizing original variables both equal \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-equivalent paths preserve the value and original-variable minimizers of every objective independent of auxiliary variables.

notation.meaning: lifted feasible sets of the paths

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Invariance Under Primal-Equivalent Paths

assumptions_latex: Both paths originate from the same constraint over space \(X\).
Both lifted formulations are well-defined on their declared domains.
review_flags: Corrected the malformed projection command in the conclusion.
No supplied locator addresses equivalence of modeling-system bridge paths.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic equivalence criterion for alternative exact bridge compositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let bridge paths \(P\) and \(Q\) transform the same original constraint into lifted feasible sets \(\mathcal F_P\subseteq X\times Y_P\) and \(\mathcal F_Q\subseteq X\times Y_Q\). They are primal-equivalent when \[\operatorname{proj}_X\mathcal F_P=\operatorname{proj}_X\mathcal F_Q.\] They are recovery-equivalent when, additionally, their recovery maps return identical values for every original-model primal and dual quantity declared recoverable, after accounting for any documented coordinate isomorphism. Equal projected feasible sets alone does not establish equivalence of dual recovery, statuses, numerical conditioning, or certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative bridge paths are primal-equivalent when their lifted feasible sets have the same projection; recovery equivalence additionally requires agreement of all declared recovered quantities.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Bridge Paths

children.title: Bridge-Cycle Prevention
children.top_down_role: Structural safeguards against cyclic or nonterminating bridge selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp path-length consequence of active-state nonrepetition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the normalized bridge graph has \(n<\infty\) states and an expansion path rejects every edge whose target is already active, then no accepted path repeats a state. Consequently every accepted bridge path contains at most \(n\) states and at most \(n-1\) bridge edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With n normalized states and active-state rejection, an accepted bridge path has at most n minus one edges.
assumptions_latex: \text{No accepted path repeats a normalized state}
review_flags: Bounds individual path depth, not total work when bridges branch into multiple target constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-State Bridge-Path Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal nonterminating bridge registry excluded by active-path cycle detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider distinct unsupported normalized states \(T,U\) with the only bridge edges \(T\to U\) and \(U\to T\). Expansion without active-path rejection produces \(T,U,T,U,\ldots\). If \(T\) remains active while \(U\) is expanded, rejecting \(U\to T\) terminates that branch with conversion failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two bridges generating each other's unsupported state recurse forever unless the returning edge is rejected.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ and }U\text{ have no supported terminal expansion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\to U\to T\to\cdots\text{ is nonterminating without cycle rejection}
knowledge_statements.title: Two-State Bridge Cycle
Bridge-Cycle Prevention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclicity condition ensuring bridge search cannot revisit an active representation state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form a directed graph whose vertices are normalized constraint-representation states and whose edge \(T\to U\) records that a bridge from \(T\) generates a constraint of state \(U\). During expansion, maintain the active recursion set \(A\). A candidate bridge from \(T\) is admissible only if none of its generated states belongs to \(A\); equivalently, a globally certified registry may require the reachable bridge graph to be acyclic. With finitely many states, active-set rejection prevents recursive bridge cycles, and a globally acyclic registry makes every bridge path finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject any bridge that generates a representation already active in the current expansion; a finite acyclic bridge graph guarantees finite paths.
assumptions_latex: The normalized representation-state set is finite.
Bridge targets are normalized before cycle testing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\notin A\) for every accepted edge \(T\to U\); global acyclicity implies termination of every bridge path.

notation.meaning: states active on the current bridge path

review_flags: No supplied locator specifies bridge-graph cycle prevention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The acyclicity condition matches the bridge-cycle prevention leaf and distinguishes path-local active-set rejection from global acyclicity. No cited source supports the normalization, graph, or termination contract used by the interface.

children.title: Conversion Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where no exact supported bridge exists or representation metadata would be lost.

children.title: Unsupported Cone Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cone families lacking native support or an available exact bridge.

assumptions_latex: Only registered exact bridges are eligible.
The target solver capability set \(\mathcal S\) is fixed for the query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\notin\mathcal S\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_G(K)\cap\mathcal T_{\mathcal S}=\varnothing\) imply exact conversion failure.

notation.meaning: terminal bridge states whose generated constraint types are all solver-supported

review_flags: Corrected the malformed empty-set command and defined the terminal-state set.
No supplied source documents this solver-interface failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when neither direct support nor an exact supported bridge path exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cone constraint \(g(x)\in K\), let \(\mathcal S\) be the solver-supported representation types, let \(G\) be the directed graph of admissible exact bridges, and let \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal S}\) be the set of terminal bridge states whose generated constraint types all belong to \(\mathcal S\). Exact conversion is unavailable precisely when the natural representation of \(K\) is not in \(\mathcal S\) and no finite path in \(G\) reaches \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal S}\). In that case an interface must report unsupported conversion unless the user explicitly authorizes an approximation or supplies an additional bridge; silently replacing \(K\) by a different cone is not exact conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conversion fails when the cone is not directly supported and no finite exact bridge path reaches only solver-supported constraint types.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Cone Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed graph-search procedure over registered exact bridges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite directed graph \(G=(V,E)\) of registered exact bridges, graph search from the natural representation \(v_0\) reaches a solver-supported terminal representation if and only if such a registered path exists. Adjacency-list search takes \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time and \(O(|V|)\) auxiliary storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph search detects whether a registered exact bridge path reaches a solver-supported representation.
assumptions_latex: E\text{ contains every bridge eligible for the query}
review_flags: Graph traversal and its complexity implement bridge discovery; this failure leaf owns the negative reachability condition, not the search algorithm.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Bridge Reachability Test

intermediate_metadata.reason: The immutable seed exhausts the generic unsupported-cone boundary relative to fixed solver capabilities and an exhaustive eligible bridge registry. The proposed graph-search implementation is deferred to the bridge-method scopes. Lossy conversion, parameter-preservation failure, and recovery-metadata loss are excluded siblings.

children.title: Lossy Conversion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conversions that discard semantics, precision, or recoverability metadata.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Optimum Does Not Certify Exact Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between objective agreement and feasible-set preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=[0,1]\), \(\widetilde F=\{0\}\), and minimize \(f(x)=x\). Then \(\widetilde F\subsetneq F\), yet both problems have value zero and unique minimizer zero. Agreement for one objective therefore does not certify equality of feasible sets or exact bridging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict inner approximation can preserve one optimum and optimizer, so objective agreement does not prove exactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Equal Optimum Does Not Certify Exact Conversion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Bounds from Inner and Outer Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value implications of lossy feasible-set inclusion for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common minimization objective \(f\), write \(v(S)=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\). If \(\widetilde F\subseteq F\), then \(v(F)\le v(\widetilde F)\). If \(F\subseteq\widetilde F\), then \(v(\widetilde F)\le v(F)\). The inequalities hold in the extended reals, but inclusion alone supplies no finite approximation-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner conversions give upper bounds and outer conversions give lower bounds for minimization, but inclusion alone gives no error estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde F\subseteq F\Rightarrow v(F)\le v(\widetilde F),\qquad F\subseteq\widetilde F\Rightarrow v(\widetilde F)\le v(F)

notation.meaning: infimum of the common objective over S

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Bounds from Inner and Outer Conversions

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(\widetilde F\) are subsets of the same original-variable space.
Projection eliminates only introduced auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\neq\widetilde F\) implies the conversion is not an exact bridge.
review_flags: Corrected malformed projection and tilde commands in the statement.
The mathematical distinction is standard, but no supplied locator supports bridge approximation semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact cone reformulation and inner or outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original feasible set be \(F=\{x:g(x)\in K\}\) and let a conversion produce \(\widetilde F=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,z):H(x,z)\in L\}\). The conversion is exact only when \(F=\widetilde F\). It is lossy when strict inclusion holds in either direction: \(\widetilde F\subsetneq F\) is an inner approximation and \(F\subsetneq\widetilde F\) is an outer approximation. If neither set contains the other, the conversion is an inconsistent approximation. A lossy conversion must not be selected as an exact bridge and requires an explicit approximation policy and error semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conversion is lossy whenever its projected feasible set differs from the original, whether by inner, outer, or non-nested approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Lossy Conversion Boundaries

children.title: Parameter-Preservation Failures
children.top_down_role: Bridge paths unable to preserve cone-specific parameter data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete semantic loss when distinct power-cone parameters are mapped to one target parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\alpha<1\), define \(K_\alpha=\{(x,y,z):x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ x^\alpha y^{1-\alpha}\ge |z|\}\). The point \((4,1,2)\) belongs to \(K_{1/2}\), since \(4^{1/2}=2\), but not to \(K_{1/4}\), since \(4^{1/4}=\sqrt2<2\). A bridge mapping both parameters to the same representation of \(K_{1/2}\) is therefore not parameter-preserving.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Erasing a power-cone exponent changes membership: an explicit point belongs at one-half but not one-quarter.

notation.meaning: three-dimensional power cone with exponent alpha

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Cone Parameter Erasure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stagewise Parameter Preservation in Bridge Chains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition criterion for retaining parameter semantics through multiple bridges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider parameter maps \(\theta_i=\phi_i(\theta_{i-1})\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The bridge chain is parameter-preserving on \(\Theta_0\) when every \(\phi_i\) is defined and admissible on all parameter values reachable from \(\Theta_0\), and every stagewise membership equivalence holds uniformly there. If any stage is undefined, inadmissible, or nonexact at a reachable parameter, the chain is not parameter-preserving for the corresponding source parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bridge chain preserves parameters exactly when every reachable stage has a total admissible parameter map and uniform exact membership equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{stagewise preservation on every reachable parameter}\Rightarrow\text{preservation by the composed chain}
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Parameter Preservation in Bridge Chains

assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is the declared admissible domain of \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the displayed equivalence for any \(\theta\in\Theta\) precludes a parameter-preserving exact bridge on \(\Theta\).

notation.meaning: map from source to target parameters

review_flags: Corrected malformed membership, equivalence, existential-quantifier, parameter, and target-membership notation.
No supplied locator covers parameter preservation by automatic bridges.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a bridge to preserve parameterized cone membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parameterized cone family \(\{K(\theta)\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\), an exact parameter-preserving bridge with parameter map \(\phi\) must satisfy \[g(x)\in K(\theta)\iff\exists z\;H(x,z;\phi(\theta))\in L\] for every admissible \(\theta\in\Theta\), with \(\phi\) defined on the entire declared parameter domain \(\Theta\). Parameter preservation fails if \(\phi(\theta)\) is undefined or inadmissible, if the equivalence holds only for a strict subset of parameter values, or if distinct parameter values requiring different feasible sets are mapped to an indistinguishable target representation. Such a bridge must be rejected for the affected parameter value even when the unparameterized cone family is supported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bridge fails parameter preservation when its parameter map is invalid, only partially defined, or changes the feasible set for some admissible parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Preservation Failures

children.title: Recovery-Metadata Loss
children.top_down_role: Conversion paths that obstruct faithful solution or certificate back-mapping.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Metadata Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to reconstruct original-model results after an otherwise valid reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an exact bridge map original constraints and variables to a lifted model, and let \(q\) denote every original-model result promised by the interface, such as primal values, dual multipliers, or constraint certificates. Recovery is well-defined only if stored metadata \(M\) determines a map \(R_M\) from every relevant lifted solution \(s\) to the promised result \(q=R_M(s)\). Recovery-metadata loss occurs when \(M\) omits a required index map, scaling, sign convention, elimination map, or bridge-composition record, so that two compatible recovery interpretations yield different \(q\). Feasibility equivalence alone does not repair this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery fails when missing indices, scalings, conventions, or composition records make an original primal, dual, or certificate value non-unique from the lifted solution.
assumptions_latex: The interface declares a set of original-model quantities recoverable.
The lifted solver result \(s\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If no unique declared map \(R_M(s)\) exists, the corresponding original-model quantity is not recoverable.
review_flags: No supplied locator documents recovery metadata for bridge implementations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the recovery-metadata loss leaf, and the statement clearly separates feasibility equivalence from recoverability. The promised-result contract and required recovery metadata are modeling-interface semantics with no cited implementation or scholarly source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed law for composing recovery maps across exact bridges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two exact bridges have solution maps \(B_1:X\to Y\) and \(B_2:Y\to Z\), with recovery maps \(R_1:Y\to X\) and \(R_2:Z\to Y\). If \(R_1B_1=\operatorname{id}_X\) and \(R_2B_2=\operatorname{id}_Y\), then \((R_1\circ R_2)(B_2\circ B_1)=\operatorname{id}_X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery maps compose in reverse bridge order.
review_flags: The general composition law is primarily owned by Bridge Composition Calculus; this leaf needs only the failure caused by absent or ambiguous composition metadata.
knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Recovery-Metadata Law

children.title: Cone Membership Tests
children.top_down_role: Cone-local services for classifying points relative to closed cone domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership characterization for a closed convex cone through its dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex cone and \(K^*:=\{y:\langle y,z\rangle\geq0\ \forall z\in K\}\). Then \[x\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle y,x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K^*.\] Equivalently, \(K=K^{**}\). If \(x\notin K\), there exists \(y\in K^*\) with \(\langle y,x\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in a closed convex cone is equivalent to satisfying every dual-cone halfspace inequality; a violated inequality certifies nonmembership.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Halfspace Cone Membership Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of distance-zero membership for a nonclosed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2:v>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\). Then \(K\) is a convex cone but is not closed. For \(x=(1,0)\), \[d_K(x)=0\qquad\text{while}\qquad x\notin K.\] Thus \(d_K(x)=0\) characterizes membership only when the set is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonclosed cone, a point outside the cone can have zero distance to it, so closedness is essential to the distance-zero membership test.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to K

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Zero Failure Without Closedness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership predicate expressed by distance to the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(d_K(x):=\inf_{z\in K}\|x-z\|_2\). Then \[x\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_K(x)=0.\] Convexity is not needed for this equivalence, although it is required for the dual-halfspace characterization used for closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point belongs to a nonempty closed cone exactly when its distance to the cone is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed cone.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to K

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Cone Distance Membership Criterion
Cone Membership Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership in a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and define \(d_K(x):=\inf_{z\in K}\|x-z\|_2\). An exact cone-membership test is a predicate \(M_K:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying
\[
M_K(x)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_K(x)=0.
\]
Thus a negative result requires \(d_K(x)>0\); equality to zero is sufficient because \(K\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point belongs to a closed cone exactly when its Euclidean distance from that cone is zero.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to K

review_flags: Exact closed-set distance characterization is standard, but no supplied locator directly supports the generic cone-membership interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed-set distance characterization and content kind are correct, but the record supplies no inspectable source.

children.title: Cone Interior Tests
children.top_down_role: Cone-local services for classifying strict interior membership.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Interior Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interior membership for a full-dimensional cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a full-dimensional closed convex cone. An exact interior predicate \(I_K:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{0,1\}\) satisfies
\[
I_K(x)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{int}K
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists r>0\; B_2(x,r)\subseteq K.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) precisely when its distance to the complement is positive: \(d_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K}(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is interior to a full-dimensional cone exactly when some positive-radius Euclidean ball around it lies in the cone, equivalently when its distance to the complement is positive.

notation.meaning: open Euclidean ball of radius r about x
Euclidean distance from x to a set S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual characterization of ambient interior membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex cone with nonempty interior. Then \[x\in\operatorname{int}K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle y,x\rangle>0\quad\text{for every }y\in K^*\setminus\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is strictly inside a full-dimensional closed convex cone exactly when it pairs positively with every nonzero dual-cone vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Dual-Pairing Interior Test

children.title: Boundary Classification
children.top_down_role: Service outcomes distinguishing interior, boundary, and exterior points.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological boundary classification for a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex cone. A point \(x\) is classified as a boundary point exactly when
\[
x\in\partial K
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in K\ \text{ and }\ \forall r>0,\ B_2(x,r)\cap(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K)\ne\varnothing.
\]
If \(K\) is full-dimensional, this is equivalent to \(x\in K\) and \(d_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K}(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone point is on the boundary exactly when every neighborhood also contains a point outside the cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\partial K\iff x\in K\) and every neighborhood of \(x\) meets \(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual characterization of boundary points of a full-dimensional closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex cone with nonempty interior, and let \(K^*:=\{y:\langle y,z\rangle\geq0\ \forall z\in K\}\). For \(x\in K\), \[x\in\partial K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\in K^*\setminus\{0\}\text{ such that }\langle y,x\rangle=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is on the cone boundary exactly when a nonzero dual-cone vector supports the cone orthogonally at that point.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Supporting-Witness Boundary Test

children.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Test Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical qualification of membership classifications near cone boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound cone-position decisions when a computed point has a certified normwise error radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(\widehat x\) be computed, and suppose the unknown exact point \(x\) satisfies \(\|x-\widehat x\|_2\leq\delta\). Set \(U:=\overline B_2(\widehat x,\delta)\). Then \(U\subseteq K\) certifies \(x\in K\), and \(U\cap K=\varnothing\) certifies \(x\notin K\). If \(U\) meets both \(K\) and \(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K\), membership is unresolved. A tolerance declaration without a valid error guarantee is only a numerical convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error ball wholly inside or outside the cone gives a sound classification; if it meets both sides, exact membership is ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\subseteq K\Rightarrow x\in K\), and \(U\cap K=\varnothing\Rightarrow x\notin K\); a ball meeting both sides is inconclusive.

notation.meaning: certified uncertainty ball around the computed point

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Ball Position Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of treating a distance tolerance as exact cone membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb{R}_+\), choose \(\varepsilon>0\), and set \(x=-\varepsilon/2\). Then \[d_K(x)=\varepsilon/2\leq\varepsilon\qquad\text{although}\qquad x\notin K.\] Hence \(d_K(x)\leq\varepsilon\) cannot certify exact membership for any positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every positive distance tolerance can accept an exterior point, even for the nonnegative ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Tolerance False Feasibility
Tolerance-Sensitive Test Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware approximate position tests for closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate membership, robust interiority, and near-boundary status are determined by distances compared with a scale-adjusted tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_K(x)\) and \(d_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K}(x)\) determine the stated tolerance-sensitive classifications relative to \(\tau(x)\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to a set S
